## REVIEW R27 — the heaviest review of the sprint by finding count: **6 MAJOR + 10 MINOR across three lenses, every one demonstrated by running the code.** 🔴 **Two of them had already written FALSE METADATA into the PUBLISHED PR-CSI-015 report**, and a third would have silently flipped its headline from 3-of-27 to 2-of-27. **The numbers survive untouched.** All fixed, with six tests that FAIL on the pre-fix code

### 0. Scope, and why the count is so high

Window: **S-297…S-305**, i.e. since R26. Three lenses in parallel — the census reader, the gates/freeze/argv path, and one lens tasked only with **the class rather than the instance**, which is the thing S-305 named and did not finish.

⚠ **The reason R27 out-found R25 and R26 is that S-305 told it where to look.** S-305 wrote: *"The pattern is fixing the instance in front of me instead of grepping for the class."* R27 was pointed at exactly that, and **the fourth and fifth instances were both waiting.**

### 1. 🔴 MAJOR — the FOURTH instance of the S-305 class, and the first to reach a PUBLISHED artefact

S-301 replaced the hardcoded dose status **at the print banner** and left the identical hardcode **160 lines below**, where it is written into the JSON for every cell arm:

```
scripts/dcs_csi_head_census.py:358
  g0[arm]["dose_expectation_status"] = "PREDICTED (DOSE_UNIT/band_width, untested uniformity
                                        assumption -- S-292)"
```

```
the PUBLISHED report:  27 x "PREDICTED ... untested uniformity assumption"
its own prereg:        DOSE_EXPECTATION.STATUS = "MEASURED (PR-CSI-014 observed exactly 224.0 ...)"
its own stdout:        "PER-CELL DOSE VALIDATION: predicted 224, observed [224.0] -> CONFIRMED"
```

**The artefact contradicted its own preregistration, its own banner and its own verdict, in the
safe-sounding direction.** Fixed: the status is read from the prereg, whatever the prereg says.

### 2. 🔴 MAJOR — S-301's lesson applied at ONE consumer of four, and the published report went out with its criterion NULL

`_bar_for()` learned `DETECTABILITY_PREREGISTERED_PER_HEAD`. The **three other readers of the same
block did not**, so on PR-CSI-015 they all resolved to `None`:

```
CELL_FAMILY.DETECTABILITY_PREREGISTERED                            = null
CELL_FAMILY.NOTHING_CLEARED_THE_BAR_IS_A_PREREGISTERED_COHERENT_OUTCOME = null
CELL_FAMILY.WEAKER_CRITERION_NOTE: "The prereg froze |E| > preregistered_bar"
                                                     ^^^^ which is ALSO null on a multi-head family
```

**The report told a reader the criterion lived in a field the report had left empty.** The headline
was computed correctly against the per-head bars sitting right there — but the published artefact
could not be audited against its own criterion, which is the whole point of publishing it.

Fixed by **one resolver** (`_detect()`) that every consumer goes through — because "fixed at the site
in front of me" is the defect. It accepts both spellings (`..._CLEARS_IT` from PR-014,
`..._CLEARS` from PR-015), and its absence default now **warns** instead of asserting that the prereg
records something (R20-6).

### 3. 🔴 MAJOR — the fail-open that would have flipped the headline

`_bar_for` refused when **both** bar sources were absent. It fell through silently when a prereg
carried a `PER_HEAD` block **but omitted one head** and also carried a legacy global bar.

R27 demonstrated it **on the real 29 arms**:

```
delete per_head["23"], leave head 2's frozen global 0.019181
  -> banner prints "head 23  |E| > 0.019181" as if preregistered
  -> CL_H23_L07 (E = -0.018514) flips CLEARS -> below the bar
  -> headline 3 of 27 -> 2 of 27
  -> head 23 flips from preregistered outcome A to outcome C, THE DISTRIBUTED-PROFILE NULL
  -> exit 0, no warning
```

**S-301 closed total absence and left partial absence wide open — one branch away from the refusal it
had just written.** Fixed: a per-head declaration must be **total**, or the read refuses.

### 4. 🔴 MAJOR — the FIFTH instance: S-305's own fix fails open on the negation of its own keyword

```
_dose_confirmed = ("MEASURED" in s.upper() and "PREDICTED" not in s.upper())
```

`"NOT MEASURED"` contains `"MEASURED"`. R27 ran the real sweep against the real 29 arms with
`STATUS` set to `NOT MEASURED`, `NOT YET MEASURED` and `UNMEASURED` — **all three printed the identity
branch**, announcing an explicitly-unmeasured dose as an identity *"so a deviation is a CODE defect"*.

⚠ **S-305's comment above that line asserts the opposite of what the line does**: *"everything else,
absence included, is UNVERIFIED (R20-6: absence is not a pass)."* Fixed: the status must **begin with**
the word and every negative form is refused explicitly.

### 5. 🔴 MAJOR — a guard swallowed by its own exception handler, on an arm that cleared the bar

The sweep caught `SystemExit` **and** bare `Exception` from `strict_run_dir` and printed
`-- not landed --`, incrementing **neither** `landed` nor `fails`. So every refusal reason collapsed
into "hasn't started yet":

```
corrupt CL_H19_L14's DONE.json ledger (231 vs a 230-line results.jsonl)
  -> "CL_H19_L14   -- not landed --"
  -> "GATE 0: every landed arm passes (28 of 29)",  exit 0
```

**CL_H19_L14 is one of the three cells that cleared the bar.** A second complete run dir from the void
job 918967 did the same — exactly the S-103/S-104 relaunch shape the frozen read warns about.

Fixed: an arm with **no** directory is *not landed*; an arm whose directories **exist and were
refused** is a **FAILURE**, named with its reason. Verified on three cases:

```
real arms, right job    -> "every landed arm passes (29 of 29)"                         exit 0
real arms, wrong job    -> "29 FAILURE(S) ... 29 had directories that were REFUSED"      exit 1
prefix matching nothing -> "NOTHING TO CHECK -- 0 of 29 declared arms resolved"          exit 3
```

### 6. The MINORs worth naming

* `min_abs_E_for_ci95_to_exclude_0` **is falsified by this family's own data by ~7×.** It is 1.96·SE
  of the **nine-cell head** arm, whose per-domain spread is far larger than a single cell's. **7 of the
  24 non-clearing cells have a ci95 excluding 0**, the smallest at **14%** of the bar. So *"24 of 27
  below the bar"* must **never** be read as *"24 cells show no effect"* — it means *not detectable at
  the preregistered resolution*. The `WEAKER_CRITERION_NOTE` now says this in the artefact itself.
* `head_2_cross_check` in the freeze script is **tautological** — `recomputed` and `frozen_in_pr014`
  are both `round(HEAD_2_FROZEN_BAR, 6)`, the same module constant, so they **cannot** differ, while the
  note claims a reproduction the published numbers do not witness. R26 §1's shape in a new artefact.
  The genuine comparison exists at line 258 and is never published. **Recorded, not fixed** — the
  prereg is frozen and committed, and R26's chain-of-custody rule forbids editing it after the fact.
* `screen = {"19": "L14", "17": "L14", "23": "L7"}` is a **bare literal** in the freeze script and the
  script never opens the screen artefact it cites. Two reviewers independently re-derived it from the
  288-cell grid and **it is correct** — but it is the prediction side of the whole headline, unpinned.
  Together with S-307 §5 (the screen is gitignored, zero git history) this is the sprint's weakest
  provenance link, and it is now named twice.
* The argv generator's `EXPECT_N` is a **constant standing where the prereg is the source**, and its
  `codeword` default `"basket"` is never checked against the prereg — so S-251's defect (basket rows
  under button tags, `--check` passing) is **still reachable**. Demonstrated: removing `codeword` from
  PR-013's button prereg and running `--check` exits 0 announcing *"CODEWORD CHECK PASSED: 'basket'"*.
  ⚠ **This one is load-bearing for the next family, which is on BUTTON.** Fixed before PR-CSI-016.
* VOID condition 6 (*"`score_behavior.py` edited while these arms are in flight"*) **has no enforcing
  check anywhere**, and PR-015 exhibited its precondition: the 29 arms recorded **four distinct git
  HEADs**, with `CL_BASE` — the subtrahend of all 27 contrasts — at `fbf1fbf5` and every cell arm
  later. **VOID 6 is clear on the facts** (`git diff fbf1fbf5 64a2dad3 -- src/ scripts/score_behavior.py`
  is **empty**; the in-flight commits touched only `external_md`, the sweep and a test), but it was
  clear by luck rather than by a check.

### 7. ✅ What R27 VERIFIED CORRECT, which is also a finding

```
the 3-of-27 headline, re-derived from raw results.jsonl by 3 independent implementations   max |dE| 4.7e-09
all four bars re-derived from D34's RAW rows: 0.009082 / 0.010223 / 0.006615 / 0.019181    all 6 digits
  (and the ALTERNATIVE reading of "per-domain SD" gives 0.0598/0.0601/0.0654 and does NOT
   reproduce -- so the prereg's phrase unambiguously means the PAIRED DELTA, and that is what ran)
every arm: slurm_job_id 922176, node n-301 (single node -> VOID 1 cannot fire), attn eager (VOID 2),
  CL_BASE carries no --intervene (VOID 4), dose 224.0 x27 / 2016.0 / 0, decode edits 0, violations {}
both rank readers refuse PR-CSI-015 by name (S-302's claim, verified by running them)
```

📌 **And the verdict is robust to the bars entirely.** The three clearing cells sit at 2.58×, 4.30×
and 2.80× their bars; the largest **non**-clearing cell is 0.44× of its own. **Every bar could be
rescaled by any factor in [0.44×, 2.58×] — or the three heads' bars permuted among themselves — and
the clearing set would be byte-identical.** That matters because S-307 §6 correctly flagged the bars
as validation-derived and not held out: **they are not load-bearing.**

### 8. The published report is REGENERATED, and here is exactly what moved

R26 refused to rewrite D34 and the chain of custody was why. **This case is different and the
difference is checkable**: the arms are on disk, the read is frozen and unchanged (md5 `4841486c`),
and the reader is deterministic. So the frozen read was **re-executed** with the fixed reader:

```
md5 BEFORE  800f343da9ba7707178c05db49a1a46c
md5 AFTER   293f9ce70518de09ca8ea8684277748f

fields compared   575
fields CHANGED     51
  of which NUMERIC  0     <- every E, every ci95, the clearing set, n_domains, the anchors: IDENTICAL
```

All 51 are `null -> value` (the detectability block, its per-head entries, the coherent-outcome text,
the method string) or the false dose status `-> ` the prereg's own. **No number moved, and the before
md5 is recorded here so the regeneration is auditable rather than silent.**

⚠ Independent corroboration that the reader is deterministic: an R27 reviewer re-ran the frozen read
**without** `--require-slurm-job` and got `800f343d` — byte-identical to the original. *That is also a
MINOR finding in its own right: the report records neither the run dirs it read nor the job filter, so
nothing in the JSON distinguishes a job-bound read from an unbound one.*

### 9. Verification

```
6 new tests, each written against the PROPERTY and not the wording
  -> ALL SIX FAIL on the pre-fix code (checked by reverting both scripts to HEAD and re-running)
  -> all pass on the fixed code.   35 tests in test_csi_cell_identity.py, 46 with test_knockout_cells
```

⚠ **And R27 broke a test in this very file** — `test_a_real_gate0_failure_and_zero_landed_have_
DIFFERENT_exit_codes` did `src.index("landed arm(s) FAILED")`, a **literal**, and it failed the moment
the summary line was reworded although the property it protects was untouched. **That is exactly the
anti-pattern S-305 named**, sitting in the file where the lesson should have landed first. Rewritten to
assert the property: the zero-landed path and the failure path must exit with **different non-zero**
codes, found by structure rather than by wording.

### 10. Verdict of R27

**No BLOCKER. The science is untouched — three independent re-derivations put the headline at 4.7e-09.
The artefact was not.** Two defects had already published false metadata, one was a single branch away
from flipping a preregistered outcome, and two of the six MAJORs are the *fourth and fifth* instances
of a class **named in the immediately preceding entry**. Naming a class is not fixing it; the grep has
to be part of the fix, and now there are tests that fail without it.

## S-309 — 🔴 **AMENDMENT to S-294's blocked-axis inventory: `button validation` is NOT blocked. It was blocked for HEAD 2, and only for head 2 — PR-CSI-013's own RANDOM control draws already measured 20 other heads there, and head 19 sits at |E|/bar = 5.69.** ⚠ And a **POST-HOC** recomputation that reframes S-290: with head 19 as candidate, PR-CSI-013 would have ranked **1 of 21, p = 0.047619 — the attainable floor exactly**

### 1. Why this entry exists before any new arm is designed

S-294 measured that **every** candidate held-out axis for a cell-level confirmatory test was blocked,
each for a different reason, and §6 concluded that design steps 4 and 5 were **UNREACHABLE**. That
finding has governed every design decision since, including PR-014's and PR-015's demotion to
descriptive censuses. **It is the single most consequential constraint in the sprint**, so before
spending 2 GPU-hours it was re-tested against what is actually on disk today.

**Four of its five rows stand. One does not.**

### 2. 🔴 The row that falls: `button validation`

S-294 wrote: *"button validation — **HEAD 2 IS NULL THERE** — D35: E = −0.003522, ci95 crosses 0,
rank 6 of 21."* Every word is true **of head 2**. PR-CSI-013 also ran **20 further single-head arms on
button validation** as its control family (job 919531, one allocation, one architecture), and nobody
had read them as measurements in their own right. Re-derived from
`reports/DCS_CSI_PR013_BUTTON_HEAD_validation.json`, with `bar = 1.96·SD/√23` back-derived from each
arm's own published ci95 (the S-294/PR-015 method):

```
head  arm           E           ci95                      excl0    bar        |E|/bar
  19  BT_CTRL_01  -0.035568  [-0.042265, -0.029752]  YES    0.006256    5.69   <- LIVE, and large
  11  BT_CTRL_05  -0.016310  [-0.022155, -0.011091]  YES    0.005532    2.95
  20  BT_CTRL_19  -0.007248  [-0.009822, -0.004850]  YES    0.002486    2.92
   6  BT_CTRL_06  -0.005090  [-0.007158, -0.003070]  YES    0.002044    2.49
  29  BT_CTRL_11  +0.009291  [+0.005855, +0.013067]  YES    0.003606    2.58
  24  BT_CTRL_00  -0.002854  [-0.004430, -0.001387]  YES    0.001521    1.88
   2  BT_SINGLE   -0.003522  [-0.015452, +0.006019]  no     0.010736    0.33   <- the blocked one
```

⚠ **Head 2 is not merely small on button — it is the NOISIEST arm in the family.** Its SD is
0.0263 against head 19's 0.0153 and head 24's 0.0037. S-294 derived its pessimism from head 2's
`SD/|E| = 0.92`; head 19 on button is `SD/|E| = 0.43`. **The axis was judged by its worst member.**

**Head 19 agrees across codewords to 88.7 %** (button −0.035568 vs basket −0.040109). And it entered
PR-013 **by a random draw, not a selection**: the frozen `control_draw_rule` is *"single seed counter
from 20261101, +1 per attempt, accept iff the head is not already drawn"*, and head 19 came in at seed
**20261102** — the second draw. **Its button liveness is as clean an observation as this sprint owns.**

**S-294 §5's table is AMENDED, not withdrawn.** The correct row reads:

> `button validation` — **blocked for head 2**; **LIVE for heads 19, 11, 20, 6, 29, 24, 16, 10**,
> whose effects were measured there by PR-CSI-013's own random control draws.

### 3. The other four rows stand, and today's result does NOT fix them

```
basket validation   still NOT held out -- it is where the head set was selected            UNCHANGED
basket train        still CONTAMINATED on the head coordinate (HD_TOPK was a TRAIN pick)   UNCHANGED
the 3 TEST domains  still need n > 3.8 at the most optimistic SD/|E| ever observed         UNCHANGED, UNTOUCHED

```

⚠ **PR-015 does not repair `basket train`.** Its head set `{17,19,23}` comes from D34, a *validation*
census — S-307 §6 states this precisely and nothing today changes it.

📌 One refinement worth recording: *"a third codeword"* is **unbuilt, not unbuildable**. The bank
metadata records `torch = None, cuda_available = None, hostname = c-003` — **the banks are built on
CPU** — and PR-CSI-008 already screened 40 candidates to 25 survivors. Separately,
`ts116m_{button,basket}_{gun,knife}` banks **already exist on disk**; those are a *concept* axis, which
rule §3.4 blocks until installability is measured, and that measurement costs **2 clean arms (~334 s)**.

### 4. ⚠ POST-HOC, AND IT MUST CARRY THAT LABEL EVERY TIME IT IS WRITTEN

The basket TRAIN screen's `ranking_most_negative_first` opens `[19, 17, 23, 6, 13, 2, …]`. **PR-CSI-013
nominated head 2 — the screen's SIXTH** — because its rule (frozen S-248) took the strongest head from
the *validation census*. Recomputing PR-013's own rank statistic with head 19 as the candidate and the
remaining 20 arms as controls, on arms that already exist:

```
E(head 19) = -0.03556758
controls strictly better: 0     ties: 0
rank = 1 of 21     p = 0.047619  =  the attainable floor 1/21, exactly
```

⛔ **THIS IS NOT A REPLICATION AND MUST NEVER BE QUOTED AS ONE.** Three reasons, all disqualifying on
their own:

1. **The control pool was drawn for h\* = 2.** Had the frozen rule nominated head 19, it would have
   drawn 20 controls from the 31 heads other than 19 — a **different pool**, with head 2 eligible.
   This recomputation reuses a pool built for a different candidate.
2. **It is read after the fact**, on numbers already published. Selection re-enters the moment a
   candidate is chosen knowing its value.
3. **It lands exactly on the floor.** `p = 1/21` is what rank 1 always gives here; it is the *best
   attainable* number, not evidence of a large effect.

**What it does license, and this is worth a great deal:** it reframes S-290's
`DOES NOT REPLICATE AT RANK 1` verdict. **What failed on button was the NOMINATION RULE, not
necessarily the phenomenon.** The TRAIN surrogate this sprint has been treating as the junior
instrument picked the head that is large and clean on button; the intervention-based validation census
picked the one that is null and noisiest there. That belongs beside D35 whatever gets launched next —
and it is a second, independent line of evidence for the same thing PR-015 found: **the screen is a
better selector than its standing in this sprint implies.**

⚠ **And it is a warning about my own result.** If the screen is the better nominator at HEAD level
too, then AM-32's *"the screen ranked head 2 only 6th"* was evidence against the **census**, not
against the **screen** — and I have been reading it the other way round all sprint.

### 5. What is chosen, and what is declined

**PR-CSI-016 — the cell census on `button` validation, heads 17/19/23.** Because:

* it is the first design in this sprint that is **held out on TWO coordinates** — the layer prediction
  is basket TRAIN (67 domains), the read is button VALIDATION (23 domains). PR-015 held out one.
* **it can carry a p.** The per-head argmax has an exact floor of 1/9 under *"no depth structure
  transfers"*; across K heads the all-match floor is `9^-K`: **K=3 gives 1.37e-03, and 2-of-3 gives
  3.43e-02** — both clear α = 0.05. PR-014 and PR-015 had to be rewritten as descriptive precisely
  because no such floor existed (S-294 §6). **This is a real test with a preregistrable PASS and FAIL.**
* it is a direct **Gate B** test (does it transfer?) at cell granularity — the only gate today's result
  can attack.
* the 23 domains are **identical** to basket's (S-256), so it controls the **codeword**, not the
  domain sample. The prereg must say so.

⚠ **Its real risk, priced rather than hidden.** Heads 17 and 23 have **never had a button arm**. If a
head's whole-head button arm comes in at `|E|/bar < 1.5` its argmax is noise and it must be **dropped
with its power stated**, not counted as a miss — which could collapse the test to K=1 (floor 0.111, no
certification). Head 19 is guaranteed in at 5.69. **The fallback value is a powered head-level
cross-codeword replication of D34 for three heads plus a full button depth map**, which is worth the
allocation on its own.

**DECLINED — S-306 §8's fresh-head family on basket validation.** S-306 counted 15 fresh live heads
from D34's ci95 alone. An argmax test needs **two** things per head: a detectable head effect **and a
sharp screen prediction**. Joining D34 to the screen:

```
fresh head   |E|/bar   screen argmax margin over runner-up
     6        2.58            5.96      usable
     4        1.96            4.42      usable
    21        2.12            2.17      usable
    11        1.98            1.51      flat screen
    13        1.90            1.08      screen is flat -- no prediction exists
     3        1.41            3.80      underpowered
```

**About 3 of the 15 clear both filters.** That is K = 3 — the *same* floor as PR-CSI-016 — for 29 arms,
while being held out on **one** coordinate instead of two and repeating exactly the head-selection flaw
S-307 §6 flagged. **PR-CSI-016 dominates it.** S-306 §8's "15 fresh heads" is therefore **corrected to
~3 usable**, and the sketch is withdrawn in favour of the button family.

📌 Also recorded as **closed**, so nobody re-derives it: nominating the heads from the TRAIN screen too
(`S[h]` top-K = 19, 17, 23, 6, 13, 2, 24, 28) would make head *and* layer TRAIN-derived — the cleanest
design in principle. Of the fresh ones only head 6 has both a live basket effect and a sharp peak
(13 has margin 1.08, 24 has |E|/bar 1.30, 28 is null). **K = 1, floor 0.111. NOT RUNNABLE.**

### 6. Gates A–E, honestly

```
Gate A  NOT TOUCHED. PR-015 is a knockout localisation; Gate A needs candidate-specific RESCUE, and
        Phase 1 closed NEGATIVE there (rank 4 of 11 on both splits, S-054/S-058).
Gate B  NOT TOUCHED by today's result -- PR-015 is basket-only. PR-CSI-016 attacks it directly.
Gate C  DIRECTLY TOUCHED, and this is PR-015's gate: the strongest Gate C evidence the sprint owns.

Gate D  NOT TOUCHED, and priced as CANNOT ANSWER BEFORE RUNNING: the four peak cells together are

Gate E  NOT TOUCHED and correctly so -- it is gated on A-D.
```

### 7. 📌 The next design after PR-CSI-016, recorded now so it is not lost

**Does the winning cell actually read the DEMONSTRATIONS?** PR-015 localised the *destination*
— which (layer, head) at the query-codeword row. **Nothing has localised the SOURCE.** The whole chain
is named *"demonstration → query retrieval"*, and `grep -c nondemo` over this 26,000-line log returns

## S-310 — 🔴 **R27 filed the denominator collision as "not exploitable today". Designing PR-CSI-016 made it exploitable ONE ENTRY LATER** — the census reader refuses a prereg carrying both `head_sets` and `cell_sets`, so PR-016's whole-head arms *must* be 9-cell lists, and a 9-cell band arm is indistinguishable from `CL_KO` on **both** the identity field and the dose. Fixed, with a test that fails without it

### 1. How the design walked into it

PR-CSI-016 needs, in one allocation: `BT_BASE`, `BT_KO`, three **whole-head** arms (to supply each
head's bar and to deliver the head-level cross-codeword replication of D34 that has never been run),
and 27 cell arms. The obvious encoding is `head_sets` for the three and `cell_sets` for the 27.

```
scripts/dcs_csi_head_census.py:188
  if _cs and pr.get("head_sets"):
      sys.exit("REFUSING: prereg %r carries BOTH head_sets and cell_sets. An arm family is one or
                the other ...")
```

**That refusal is correct and stays.** So a whole-head arm in a cell family must be written as its nine
cells — `HD_17 = [[6,17],[7,17],…,[14,17]]`. Which is where R27's finding detonates:

```
CL_KO      knockout_heads = ""  -> recorded_heads() maps "" to "ALL"     dose 2016
HD_17      knockout_heads = ""  -> recorded_heads() maps "" to "ALL"     dose 9 x 224 = 2016
```

**Identical on the identity field. Identical on the dose.** The old check was
`ok_id = (recorded_heads(d) == "ALL")` — the entire discriminator. R27 demonstrated it on a 3-arm
scratch family and filed it as *"not exploitable — no current family contains a full-band 9-cell
arm."* **The next family does.**

### 2. The fix, and the one field that still separates them

A genuine all-32 arm carries **no cell list at all**; `recorded_cells` returns the sentinel
`NOT_A_CELL_ARM` for an empty field (deliberately *not* `"ALL"` — S-291's asymmetry). So:

```
ok_id = (recorded_heads(d) == "ALL") and (recorded_cells(d) == "NOT_A_CELL_ARM")
```

applied at **both** sites — the reader and the sweep — in the same edit, because applying it at one
is the class this sprint keeps re-learning. **Absence of the `knockout_cells` field is NOT a pass**
(R20-6): a config that never recorded it cannot rule out a 9-cell arm, and now says so.

### 3. Verification

```
the REAL family, both tools:   CL_KO ... "ALL 32, no cell list"   PASS    29 of 29   exit 0
the numbers after the patch:   max |dE| vs the committed report = 0.000e+00
```

Two tests, on a scratch `SCORE_DIR` of **symlinks to the 29 real arm dirs** with only `CL_KO`'s
`config.json` replaced — so every byte of the run except the one field under test is genuine:

```
knockout_cells = "6:17,7:17,...,14:17"  -> the sweep must REFUSE
knockout_cells = ""  (the real value)   -> the sweep must PASS      <- the companion, because a
                                                                      guard that refuses everything
                                                                      is not a guard
```

⚠ **Both were run against the PRE-FIX code.** The refusal test **FAILS** there — the sweep printed
`GATE 0: every landed arm passes (29 of 29)` and exited 0 **with a one-head-wide arm standing in for
the all-32 denominator** — and the companion passes in both. The test is not vacuous.
`tests/test_csi_cell_identity.py`: **37 passing.**

### 4. 📌 What this says about R27's triage, and it is not a criticism of R27

R27 graded this MAJOR-but-inert on the true observation that no existing family could trigger it.
**The half-life of "not currently reachable" was one entry.** The rule worth keeping: *a collision
that is inert only because no artefact has the shape yet is a dated liability, and the date is
whenever the next design needs that shape.* It cost nothing to fix here and would have cost a
32-arm allocation — ~1.8 GPU-hours — to discover from a silently-wrong denominator.

### 5. Status

```
PR-CSI-016   NOT yet frozen, NOT launched. Blocker 1 of 2 cleared.
             Remaining: the per-head bar must be freezable as a RULE computed from this family's own
             HD_<hh> arm, because heads 17 and 23 have NO prior button arm and therefore no bar can
             be frozen as a NUMBER. The reader currently REFUSES a prereg whose per_head block lacks
             a numeric bar -- which is S-308's own fix, working exactly as intended, and now in the
             way. It must learn a rule WITHOUT reopening the fail-open it just closed.
queue        EMPTY. Idle GPU is the binding cost and is being paid while this is built correctly.
```

## S-311/S-312 — **PR-CSI-016 IS BUILT AND FROZEN, and REVIEW R28 STOPPED IT REACHING A GPU TWICE.** 🔴 **Two BLOCKERS made the frozen read NON-EXECUTABLE END TO END — and one of them survived NINE GREEN TESTS OF MY OWN because my test helper fabricated a report shape the producer never emits.** Plus a sprint-wide correction: **`test_domains = 3` is FALSE; the manifest says 23**

### 1. What was built (S-311), and the one thing that made it possible

S-309 chose PR-CSI-016: the per-cell census of heads 17, 19, 23 on **button** validation. 32 arms.
Held out on **two** coordinates — the layer prediction is basket TRAIN (67 domains), the read is
button VALIDATION (23) — and the **first CSI cell family that can carry a p**.

The blocker was structural: **heads 17 and 23 have never had a button arm**, so no bar for them can
exist as a number before the run — while S-308 had just made a missing numeric bar a **REFUSAL**.

**S-311's answer is to freeze the DERIVATION rather than the number.** The prereg names, per head, the
full-band arm its bar is computed from; only the arithmetic waits for data. The reader refuses a
source arm that is missing, not in the family, did not land, or **narrower than the whole head** —
that last one because a bar computed from a single cell is computed from the quantity it judges.

⚠ **And the rule is only trustworthy because it agrees with a number where both exist.** D34's
`SINGLE_17` *is* head 17's full band, so the read-time rule must reproduce the `0.009082` PR-CSI-015
froze. It does, to every printed digit, and that is asserted as a test rather than claimed.

The whole-head arms have to be written as **nine-cell lists** (the reader refuses a prereg carrying
both `head_sets` and `cell_sets`), which is exactly the collision S-310 closed one entry earlier.

### 2. 🔴 R28 BLOCKER 1 — STEP 1 of the frozen read refused before loading a single arm

```
$ python scripts/dcs_csi_head_census.py --prereg configs/dcs_csi_pr016_cell_census_button.json ...
REFUSING: prereg 'PR-CSI-016' does not declare NO_RANK_TEST -- it is a RANK-TEST preregistration
         (candidate + control family + floor) and this is the CENSUS reader. (S-247)
```

The prereg was missing **five** fields the reader validates as preconditions: `NO_RANK_TEST`,
`CENSUS_DELIVERABLE`, `SELECTION_RE_ENTERS_WHEN`, `DOSE_IDENTITY_IS_BLIND_HERE`, and
`WHAT_THIS_CANNOT_ANSWER`. **And the refusal was actively misleading** — it told the operator this was
a rank prereg and pointed at the wrong tool.

⚠ **The bitter part is that this is S-296's check, whose own comment says it exists so that "a missing
field costs milliseconds and not a GPU allocation."** It worked perfectly. **Nobody had pointed it at
the frozen prereg.** Root cause, named by the reviewer: the S-311 tests exercise the new bar-rule path
by *mutating PR-CSI-015's* prereg, which carries all five — **so the real PR-016 prereg was never once
handed to the reader it was written for.**

### 3. 🔴 R28 BLOCKER 2 — the preregistered PRIMARY could never read a real census. **And it was mine.**

```
scripts/dcs_csi_pr016_argmax_test.py:47   g0.get("all_pass", g0.get("pass", False))
scripts/dcs_csi_head_census.py:638        writes {"per_arm": ..., "identity": ...}
```

`all_pass` **has never been written by anything.** Not in PR-012's, PR-014's or PR-015's committed
reports; `grep -rn all_pass scripts/` finds it only in my own reader. So the primary refused **every
possible healthy census report** — and would have done so **after 32 arms and ~1.9 GPU-hours**.

⛔ **All nine of its tests passed**, because `tests/test_csi_pr016_argmax.py`'s helper hand-wrote
`{"all_pass": True}`. **A test that invents its input validates the test, not the code.** That is
R27's class exactly, committed by me one entry after I wrote R27 up.

Both are now fixed, and the fix made the check **stronger than it was pretending to be**: it reads
the per-arm record, so a report with a failing arm and a cheerful summary flag is refused too —
demonstrated by R28 (`per_arm['BC_H17_L06']['pass'] = False` with `all_pass = True` used to publish
`VERDICT PASS`). The test helper now emits the **real** shape, and a new test pins that shape against
the published PR-015 report so the two cannot drift apart again.

### 4. ⚠ R28 MAJOR — the SPANNING RULE does not close the hole it was built for

The spanning rule blocks `M=2`. **It leaves `M=3` wide open.** If the button intervention carries the
top-of-band bias the design itself hypothesises, heads 17 and 19 are pinned to L14 **for free** and the
only informative event is head 23 landing on L7 — probability **1/9 = 0.1111**, which cannot clear
α at all. R28 **built that world and ran the real reader on it**:

```
K = 3 admitted, M = 3 matches, p = 0.001372 ... spanning rule SATISFIED ... VERDICT: PASS
```

**The binomial p understates the type-I error of the scientific claim by ~81×.**

Two **robustness co-primaries** are now frozen, before any number exists:

```
p_conditional   Binom(K_unique, 1/9) over ADMITTED heads whose predicted layer is NOT shared.
                With 17 and 19 both on L14, K_unique = 1 and the floor is 0.1111.
p_permutation   the exact permutation p over assignments of the prediction MULTISET to the admitted
                heads -- it asks whether the screen put the ODD prediction on the RIGHT head, which a
                shared band bias CANNOT fake. With {L14, L14, L7} its floor is 1/3.
```

⛔ **They deliberately do NOT gate the PASS/FAIL**, because requiring them would make this family
unable to pass for a **structural** reason (`K_unique = 1`) rather than an empirical one. **They bound
the wording**: the headline must be stated with the **weakest of the three, each named**, and quoting
the binomial p alone is **forbidden** whenever two admitted heads share a predicted layer. S-307
established that as the honest use of a robustness number; the difference is that these are frozen
*before* the run rather than computed after it.

### 5. 🔴 A SPRINT-WIDE CORRECTION: `test_domains = 3` IS FALSE. The manifest says **23**.

R28 flagged it; I verified it from the manifest and both banks rather than taking it:

```
data/boombness_prompts/dcs_ts116_domain_split.json
  n_train 70   n_validation 23   n_test 23        manifest_sha16 be7d2c772d814ef3
bank basket  rows by split: {train 13440, validation 4416, test 4416}   distinct TEST domains: 23
bank button  rows by split: {train 13440, validation 4416, test 4416}   distinct TEST domains: 23
```

**PART I §3.2 said 23 TEST all along.** PR-CSI-014's and PR-CSI-015's preregs both record
`test_domains: 3`, and **S-294's axis inventory rests on it** — *"the 3 TEST domains — UNDERPOWERED —
need n > 3.8 at best"* — which is one of the five rows that made a confirmatory cell test
**UNREACHABLE** and demoted PR-014 and PR-015 to descriptive censuses.

⚠ **The real blocker is different and far more tractable: TEST is not UNDERPOWERED, it is UNBUILT.**

```
runargs/dcs_cont/exclude_basket_bomb_sow_{train,validation}.txt   exist
runargs/dcs_cont/exclude_button_bomb_sow_{train,validation}.txt   exist
runargs/dcs_cont/exclude_*_bomb_sow_test.txt                      DOES NOT EXIST
```

TEST has never been run because **nobody built its exclusion list**, not because it is too small.

⛔ **NOTHING is done with this now, and PR-CSI-016 does not touch TEST.** §3.2 says TEST is read
**once**, only under a preregistration that freezes everything. This entry records the measurement and
the corrected count; **the axis inventory is re-derived, and the decision taken, in a later entry with
its own design.** Writing `test_domains: 23` into PR-016's prereg is the only change made here.

### 6. The rest of R28, and what it verified correct

```
MAJOR  the exclusion was keyed on the STRING bar_source_arm, not on ARM GRANULARITY -- so a head
       whose bar is a NUMBER leaked its 9-cell arm into the depth map, the clearing counts and the
       per-CELL dose check, printing "REFUTED -- the uniformity assumption is WRONG" on a healthy run
MAJOR  a head carrying BOTH a number and a source arm SILENTLY DELETED the named arm, with none of
       the rule's guards ever running on it (demonstrated: an arm carrying head 23's own headline
       cell vanished, "2 of 26 cells CLEAR", exit 0)
MAJOR  `z` was neither required nor bounded: a rule without z used 1.96 and then RECORDED "z": 1.96
       as though the prereg had frozen it; z = 0.0 gave a bar of 0 and "11 of 27 cells CLEAR"
MAJOR  ⚠ S-310 OVER-REACHED AND BROKE A PUBLISHED FAMILY -- requiring the all-32 arm to record an
       empty knockout_cells made D34 (PR-CSI-012) UNREADABLE, because its HD_KO predates the flag
MINOR  `layers` read late; MUST_NOT_BE_SAID chosen by a binary PASS test, so a spanning CANNOT ANSWER
       published "the screen is useless" while holding p = 0.034; a dropped head whose argmax DID
       match was published as MATCHES_SCREEN=false; ties published a quotable M/p; no split check;
       the 1/9 null was a hardcoded literal; the admission boundary failed at exactly 1.5 in IEEE
```

All fixed. `z` is now validated **once where the rule is read** rather than inside a per-head branch —
a parameter checked inside a branch is only checked for the heads that reach it.

✅ **VERIFIED CORRECT by R28, independently:** the statistic (all nine p-table entries recomputed with
exact `Fraction`s); the null is 1/9 and one-sided in the right direction; **the argmax cannot leak the
whole-head arm**; admission touches only the whole-head arm; a dropped head is never a miss and p uses
the post-drop K; every verdict branch is reachable and its text true of the state that produced it;
the screen literal re-derives from the artefact; the launcher path is clean on all 32 argv lines with
no arm whose NAME disagrees with its FLAGS; the tag namespace composes as PR-015's did; no `csi9_*`
directory exists to resume into; and the S-311 bar arithmetic is the **paired delta**, not the raw
per-domain means — the reading that would have been 6× wrong and silently passed every gate.

Both blockers existed because **nobody had run the two readers in sequence on a report of the shape

```
                              values, because these ARE D34's arms), 3 of 27 clear, dose CONFIRMED
```

Arm order puts the 27 single cells first and the three `HD_` whole-head arms last, so **ADMISSION —
the gate that decides whether the primary is readable at all — is known only when the family is
nearly complete.** Expected cost ≈ 32 × 167 s ≈ 1.5 h of arms plus one model load.

📌 One thing IS already known, and it was known before the submit: **the frozen read executes end to

## S-315 — ⚠ **MY OWN R27/S-308 FIX MISFIRED THE FIRST TIME IT MET A LIVE FAMILY: it reported an IN-FLIGHT arm as a GATE 0 FAILURE and exited 1.** The frozen reads say GATE 0 may be swept at any time, so under S-308 every mid-family sweep was a false alarm. Fixed by a filesystem fact rather than a text parse, with both halves pinned

### 1. How it surfaced, which is the good part

PR-CSI-016 is running. The frozen read permits an incremental GATE 0 sweep at any time — it is
endpoint-blind and exits 3 rather than 0 when nothing has landed — so I ran one at 5 of 32 arms:

```
BC_BASE     230      0.0      0   0  0  not intervened        PASS
BC_KO       230   2016.0   2016   0  0  ALL 32, no cell list  PASS
BC_H17_L06  230    224.0    224   0  0  matches prereg        PASS
BC_H17_L07  230    224.0    224   0  0  matches prereg        PASS
BC_H17_L08  230    224.0    224   0  0  matches prereg        PASS
BC_H17_L09  ⚠ GATE 0 FAIL -- 1 run dir(s) EXIST but were REFUSED: 0 complete run dirs (need exactly 1)

GATE 0: 1 FAILURE(S) over 6 arm(s) ...    EXIT=1
```

**`BC_H17_L09` was being written at that instant.** Nothing is wrong with it.

### 2. The defect, stated exactly

R27 found the sweep swallowing every `strict_run_dir` refusal into `-- not landed --`, counting toward
neither `landed` nor `fails` — so a corrupted ledger on `CL_H19_L14`, *one of the three cells that
cleared PR-015's bar*, printed *"every landed arm passes (28 of 29)"* and exited 0. S-308's fix was:

> *"An arm that HAS directories and was refused is a FAILURE; only an arm with NO directory at all is
> 'not landed'."*

**That is right for a ledger mismatch, a bad `DONE.status`, or two complete dirs. It is wrong for an
arm that has not finished writing**, which also has a directory and is also refused — because its
`DONE.json` does not exist yet. S-308 conflated *in flight* with *broken*.

⚠ **And the consequence is worse than the defect it replaced.** A sweep that reports a spurious FAIL on
every incremental run is a sweep whose **real** failures get waved through as "oh, that's just the
running arm." S-308 made the guard louder and therefore easier to ignore.

### 3. The fix, and why it is a filesystem fact rather than a parse

The discriminator could have been read out of `strict_run_dir`'s refusal text — *"0 complete run dirs"*
versus a ledger message. **That would have been a substring test on prose, which is the exact class
S-305 and R28 have now caught twice** (`"MEASURED" in s` matching `"NOT MEASURED"`). So instead:

```
_done = [x for x in _cands if os.path.exists(os.path.join(x, "DONE.json"))]
if not _done:   -> IN FLIGHT: neither passed nor failed, no exit code change
else:           -> GATE 0 FAIL, exactly as S-308 requires
```

An arm none of whose candidate directories carries a `DONE.json` has not finished writing. That is a
fact about the disk, not about the wording of an error.

📌 **A DIED arm is indistinguishable from an in-flight one at this instant, and is reported the same
way — INCOMPLETE, neither passed nor failed.** Only the final sweep, once the job is gone, can tell
them apart, and the arm-count guard is what catches a family that never completed. Recorded so the
`IN FLIGHT` label is not later mistaken for a liveness claim.

And a partial sweep now says so in its own banner, because the failure mode of a mid-family sweep is
being mistaken for the family's verdict:

```
GATE 0: every landed arm passes (5 of 32). ... No endpoint field was read.
  .. 1 arm(s) IN FLIGHT (run dir present, no DONE.json). THIS SWEEP IS PARTIAL and is NOT the
     family's GATE 0 verdict.
```

### 4. Verification — BOTH halves, because fixing one by breaking the other is the failure mode

Two tests on a scratch `SCORE_DIR` of symlinks to PR-015's 29 real arm dirs, one dir materialised:

```
DONE.json REMOVED from CL_H23_L14        -> must be IN FLIGHT, rc 0, "THIS SWEEP IS PARTIAL",
                                            "every landed arm passes (28 of 29)"
DONE.json ledger CORRUPTED on CL_H19_L14 -> must be GATE 0 FAIL, rc != 0, NOT excused as in flight
```

⚠ **My first attempt at the vacuity check was invalid and I nearly recorded it as a pass.** I hand-cut
the new branch out of the file, which left a `NameError`, so both tests failed — *for a crash, not for
the behaviour*. **A test that fails because the code does not import proves nothing.** Redone properly
by reverting the file to its committed S-308 state with `git stash`:

```
against committed S-308:  IN-FLIGHT test  FAILS -- "IN FLIGHT" absent; the arm was refused and
                                                  counted as a failure        <- the right reason
                          S-308 test      PASSES                              <- already correct there
against S-315:            both PASS
```

**That is the pattern a fix should show: the new property fails without it, and the old property holds
either way.** 65 tests pass across `test_csi_cell_identity.py` and `test_csi_pr016_argmax.py`.

### 5. 📌 A smaller one, recorded because it cost me a wrong belief for several minutes

My own progress grep was `^\[w3\] [0-9]+/32`. The runner right-aligns the counter — `[w3]  5/32` —
so the pattern matched **nothing** and I read "0 arms landed" at 36 minutes into a healthy job and
began looking for a stall that did not exist. **A scratch grep is not a tool and is not committed, but
a monitoring pattern that silently matches nothing reports "no progress" and "no failures" in exactly
the same voice.** The corrected pattern is `^\[w3\] +[0-9]+/32`.

### 6. State

```
PR-CSI-016  job 923233 RUNNING on n-301. GATE 0 clean on every landed arm; the sweep is PARTIAL.
            arm times ~155 s (button), BC_BASE 1428.4 s incl. the 1265.8 s load, BC_KO 208.1 s.
NO endpoint has been read. The frozen read (90ee8a12) is untouched and its PRIMARY is open.
```

## S-316 — ⚠ **S-309 §7's design premise is WITHDRAWN before it cost anything: `nondemo_matched_d*` is COUNT-matched, not MASS-matched, and this repository already refuted a count-matched control — twice — in a module whose artifact field is literally named `ctrl_mass_band_REFERENCE_ONLY`.** The source-localisation question is **BLOCKED PENDING A MEASUREMENT**, not runnable

### 1. What I was about to design, and why it looked right

S-309 §7 recorded the next family after PR-CSI-016 as the one *"most able to KILL a claim"*: the whole
chain is named **demonstration → query retrieval**, PR-014/015 localised only the **destination**
(which cell), and nothing has ever tested that the damage is specific to **demonstration** keys rather
than to blocking a dose-matched set of arbitrary earlier keys at the same cell.

`grep -c nondemo` over this 27k-line log returns **4**, all of them S-309 proposing this. The controls
exist in code: `KNOCKOUT_ARMS = ("demo_all", "nondemo_random", "allpast") + NONDEMO_DRAW_ARMS`, with
`nondemo_matched_d{1,2,3}` as three seeded strict draws. It looked like 14 arms and no new code.

### 2. 🔴 THE FINDING — it is count-matched, and the repo says that is not a control

`nondemo_control_draw`'s own docstring, verbatim:

> *"ONE seeded draw of non-demo key positions, **count-matched** to the demo block on THIS row."*

and its `match_ratio` is `n_drawn / n_demo_keys` — a **count** ratio. "Strict" guarantees only that it
never under-matches the **count**; it refuses the row instead.

**This repository already tried a count-matched control, refuted it, and renamed the artifact field to
warn against it.** `src/boombness/retrieval_strength.py:9-25`, verbatim:

> *"The 8-row smoke (job 777298) refuted it immediately: `demo_mass 0.0374` vs `ctrl_mass 0.2489`,
> with demo > ctrl in **0 of 4** measurable rows … a count-matched draw matches SIZE but not POSITION,
> and attention is dominated by the **BOS sink** and by **recency**: a random non-demo draw collects
> sink mass, while the demonstration block sits in the middle distance.
> **The control was measuring position, not retrieval.**"*

```
the field is named               ctrl_mass_band_REFERENCE_ONLY
on the full Llama artifact       the count-matched draw carries ~5.7x the demo block's L6-14 mass,
                                 demo > ctrl in 0 of 12 rows            (C-CONT-019, predecessor log)
```

⚠ **The control is the LARGER intervention, not the smaller one.** C-CONT-019's own conclusion: *"My
'dose-matched control' is plausibly the larger intervention. The frozen expected sign could have been
produced — or reversed — by the control rather than by the pathway."*

### 3. And the repo's resolution history says the answer was never a source draw at all

```
original     nondemo_random          matched on COUNT      -> ~5.7x the attention mass   REFUTED (C-CONT-019)
correction 1 position-matched        matched on POSITION   -> edited 33% more cells      REFUTED (C-CONT-024)
correction 2 the LAYER-BAND control  same rows, keys, count AND position; differs only in
                                     the band's FUNCTION (L6-14 vs the near-inert L20-31)  ACCEPTED
```

`retrieval_strength.py` states the reasoning: *"Positional priors are shared by both bands and largely
cancel."* **The predecessor solved this problem and the solution was a BAND control, not a non-demo
source draw.** A band control answers *"is it THIS band?"* — it does **not** answer *"is it the
DEMONSTRATIONS?"*, which is why S-309 §7's question is still genuinely open. But the instrument
S-309 §7 proposed to answer it with is the one already refuted.

### 4. ⚠ THE NUANCE THAT STOPS THIS BEING A FLAT KILL, and I nearly wrote the flat version

C-CONT-019 names **two** mechanisms: the **BOS sink** and **recency**. Today's pool excludes both:

```
pool = [i for i in range(1, max(0, n - 1)) if i not in demo_keys and i not in protected]
        ^ index 0 (BOS) excluded          ^ `protected` = query_span_positions = the request and
                                            everything after it, i.e. RECENCY
```

and the code comment records why: *"without that exclusion this control deletes the question"* —
review finding **M1**, applied to `nondemo_random` and `nondemo_matched_d*` alike. **Both arms share
this pool today.**

⛔ **So I cannot say the refutation transfers, and I cannot say it does not.** The 8-row smoke that
produced `ctrl_mass 0.2489` was *"Draft 1"*; **what its pool contained at that time is not established
by anything I have read**, and the M1 protection may postdate it. The honest statement is:

> **The attention mass of the CURRENT protected draw has never been measured.** The two mechanisms
> that refuted the original draw are both excluded from today's pool, and whether that is enough is an
> open, measurable question — not an assumption to build a 14-arm family on.

### 5. What that makes the status, and what it would take to unblock

**S-309 §7 is DOWNGRADED from "the next family" to BLOCKED PENDING A MEASUREMENT.** The measurement is
the cheap part of the experiment and it must come first:

```
needed   the attention mass, per row, of (a) the demo block and (b) a nondemo_matched_d* draw,
         in band 6-14, on the basket validation population
blocker  score_behavior.py records NO attention-mass field -- grep for attn_mass/attention_mass/
         mass_removed/masked_mass/prob_mass over src/ returns NOTHING. `n_prefill_edits` is a COUNT
         of edits, which is exactly the quantity that already matched while the mass did not.
blocker  retrieval_strength.py computes mass but exposes only `main()` -- it is a script, not a
         reusable function, so it cannot be called on an arbitrary key set without work.
```

⚠ **And if the measurement comes back showing the protected draw still carries more mass, the family
must NOT be run as a source test.** S-050 recorded what happens when a result turns out to be **dose
rather than direction**: a random rank-5 subspace beat the installation subspace, and the analyser
printed "PRIMARY PASSES" over it. A control that removes more attention than the arm it controls for
is that failure waiting to happen, one axis over.

📌 One asymmetry worth freezing now, because it survives the confound in one direction only:

```
nondemo ~ 0 while demo is large   -> CONFOUNDED. Could be source-specificity, could be mass.
nondemo ~ demo despite LESS mass  -> CLEAN REFUTATION of source-specificity.
```

**The design can kill the demonstration→query claim cleanly and cannot confirm it cleanly.** That is a
usable property for a falsification-oriented family, but it has to be preregistered as such rather
than discovered in the read.

### 6. What was measured this tick, and what was NOT established

```
MEASURED   PR-CSI-016 GATE 0, incrementally, at 17 of 32 landed arms: every landed arm PASSES.
           BC_BASE 0 edits / BC_KO 2016 / every cell arm 224.0, decode edits 0, violations {}.
           The sweep correctly labelled the in-flight arm and printed "THIS SWEEP IS PARTIAL"
           (the S-315 fix, working on the family that exposed the defect).
MEASURED   button arm time ~155-156 s, against basket's 167.2 s (S-306). BC_BASE 1428.4 s including
           the 1265.8 s load; BC_KO 208.1 s.
NOT ESTABLISHED  anything about PR-CSI-016's endpoint. No E, no argmax, no admission. The frozen
           read (90ee8a12) is untouched and its PRIMARY is open on every branch.
NOT ESTABLISHED  whether nondemo_matched_d* is mass-matched. §4. This is the whole point of the entry.
NOT ESTABLISHED  that a band control answers the source question. It does not; it answers a
           different one, and S-309 §7's question remains open with no admissible instrument yet.
```

📌 **Recorded about method, not results:** S-309 §7 was written from a design memo that quoted
`score_behavior.py:1487ff` accurately — *"it inherits the band check, the scope, the head subset, the
liveness gate and the pre-flight unchanged"* — and I took that to mean the family was free. **The
comment is true and was written before `--knockout-cells` existed**, and it says nothing about whether
the control is a valid control. *A quote that is accurate about mechanism can still be silent about
validity*, and the check that mattered was four directories away in a module nobody had cited this
sprint.

# S-317 — 🔴 **PR-CSI-016 IS READ. VERDICT: CANNOT ANSWER — the SPANNING RULE FIRED ON REAL DATA.** The binomial says p = 0.012346 and **it is not quotable**, because head 23 — the one admitted-eligible head whose screen prediction was *not* L14 — is **null on button** and was dropped, leaving **K_unique = 0**. ⚠ **Without R28 this entry would have read "p = 0.012, the screen transfers across codewords," and that would have been wrong**

## 0. Preconditions, then the frozen read in its own order

```
32/32 arms landed, job 923233, n-301, rc=0 on every arm, MODEL LOADS 1
frozen read  runargs/dcs_csi_pr016_read.txt   md5 90ee8a12   UNCHANGED since the commit that preceded the submit
prereg       configs/dcs_csi_pr016_cell_census_button.json   md5 183d72a7
```

## 1. STEP 0 — GATE 0, endpoint-blind, **32 of 32 PASS**

```
BC_BASE  230   0.0 edits   not intervened        PASS
BC_KO    230   2016.0      ALL 32, no cell list  PASS   <- the S-310 discriminator, on the family that needed it
27 cells 230   224.0 each  matches prereg        PASS
HD_17/19/23  2016.0 each   matches prereg        PASS   <- 9 x 224, exactly as predicted
```

## 2. STEP 1 — the depth map, and the S-311 bar RULE doing its job

The bars did not exist before this family ran. They were computed at read time from each head's own
whole-head arm, by a rule frozen before launch:

```
head 17  bar 0.007424      head 19  bar 0.006525      head 23  bar 0.004873
```

📌 **The one bar that was predictable was predicted, and the prediction holds.** PR-CSI-013's
`BT_CTRL_01` implied head 19's button bar at **0.006256**; the rule computed **0.006525** — a **4.3 %**
disagreement against a preregistered *"more than 25 % is a finding"* threshold. **The S-311 rule and
the PR-013-derived number agree.**

```
head 17 : 1 of 9 clear -> L14   E = -0.024047  ci95 [-0.032878, -0.017851]
head 19 : 1 of 9 clear -> L14   E = -0.039228  ci95 [-0.045230, -0.033703]
head 23 : 0 of 9 clear
2 of 27 cells clear.  (13 of 27 have a ci95 excluding 0 -- the WEAKER fact, not the criterion.)
```

## 3. STEP 2 — the preregistered PRIMARY, and why it CANNOT ANSWER

```
ADMISSION (from the whole-head arm ALONE, ratio >= 1.5):
  head 17  HD_17  E=-0.028734  ci95 [-0.036964,-0.022843]  |E|/bar=3.87  ADMITTED
  head 19  HD_19  E=-0.035568  ci95 [-0.042524,-0.029630]  |E|/bar=5.45  ADMITTED
  head 23  HD_23  E=-0.003038  ci95 [-0.007974,+0.001620]  |E|/bar=0.62  DROPPED (not a miss)

ARGMAX vs the frozen basket-TRAIN screen prediction:
  head 17  argmax L14   screen said L14  -> MATCH
  head 19  argmax L14   screen said L14  -> MATCH

K = 2 admitted, M = 2 matches, p = 0.012346  (Binom(K, 1/9), one-sided)
conditional  K_unique=0  M_unique=0  p = 1.000000
permutation  over 1 assignment of the prediction multiset  p = 1.000000
matching layers ['L14'] -> SPANNING RULE VIOLATED

VERDICT: CANNOT ANSWER -- all 2 matching heads share band layer L14, so a shared depth bias and a
correct screen are INDISTINGUISHABLE here. p = 0.012346 is NOT quotable as a pass.
```

⚠⚠ **THIS IS THE OUTCOME R28 FORCED INTO THE DESIGN HOURS BEFORE LAUNCH, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT
HAPPENED.** R28 built a synthetic world in which a shared top-of-band bias pins heads 17 and 19 to L14
and showed the reader printing `p = 0.001372 ... VERDICT: PASS` over it. **The real data landed in
almost exactly that world.** Without the spanning rule and the two robustness co-primaries — added on
2026-09-23 between the freeze and the submit — this entry would now be claiming the screen transfers
across codewords at p = 0.012.

**The mechanism of the failure is structural, and the prereg priced it:** the design's power to separate
"the screen is right" from "the band edge is where knockouts bite" rested entirely on head 23, the only
admitted-eligible head whose prediction was **not** L14. **Head 23 has no button effect at all.**

## 4. ✅ WHAT DID REPLICATE — the head-level cross-codeword test, which had never been run

This is PR-CSI-016's preregistered fallback value, and it delivered:

```
head   basket (D34)   button (PR-016)   button/basket   button ci95 excludes 0
 17     -0.029218       -0.028734           98.3%             YES
 19     -0.040109       -0.035568           88.7%             YES
 23     -0.016503       -0.003038           18.4%             NO (crosses 0)
```

**Two of D34's three heads carry essentially the same load on a different codeword. Head 23 does not
transfer at all.** That is a genuine Gate-B result at HEAD level, on 23 held-out-by-codeword domains,
and it is the first cross-codeword head measurement for heads 17 and 23 in the sprint.

📌 **And a provenance check that could not have been arranged:** `HD_19` here and PR-CSI-013's
`BT_CTRL_01` are the same head, the same codeword, the same split — run in **different jobs, different
families, different tag namespaces, four days apart**.

```
PR-016 HD_19      = -0.03556758   (job 923233)
PR-013 BT_CTRL_01 = -0.03556758   (job 919531)
difference        = +0.00e+00      BIT-IDENTICAL
```

Greedy decoding requires this, so it is bookkeeping rather than discovery — but it is the check that
would have caught a population, bank, exclusion-list or model-revision drift between two families
built five entries apart, and it passes exactly.

## 5. ⚠ The uncomfortable structural fact, stated because it bounds everything above

On **button**, of the four heads with a basket screen prediction:

```
head 19  predicted L14  -> LIVE on button   (|E|/bar 5.45)
head 17  predicted L14  -> LIVE on button   (|E|/bar 3.87)
head 23  predicted L7   -> NULL on button   (|E|/bar 0.62, ci95 crosses 0)
head  2  predicted L10  -> NULL on button   (D35: E = -0.003522, ci95 crosses 0)
```

**Both heads whose predicted layer is NOT L14 are null on button, and both heads whose predicted layer
IS L14 are live.** With n = 4 that is not a finding — but it is the exact configuration that makes this
design unable to answer its question, and it will make **any** future button family unable to answer
it too, by the same argument. ⛔ **A second attempt at this test on button is not merely underpowered;
it is structurally blocked until a live button head with a non-L14 prediction exists.**

## 6. What may and may not be said

The report carries the CANNOT-ANSWER list, which is neither the IF_POSITIVE nor the IF_NULL set:

> *"CANNOT ANSWER is NOT a null and NOT a positive. Neither list applies, because no verdict was
> reached."*

**PERMITTED** — *"On button validation, the two heads of D34's three that retain an effect (17 and 19,
at 98.3 % and 88.7 % of their basket values) both concentrate that effect in a single cell at L14, the
layer the basket TRAIN screen named. Head 23 does not transfer to button at all. The agreement cannot
be separated from a shared top-of-band bias by this design, because the only head whose prediction
would have distinguished them is the one with no button effect."*

**FORBIDDEN, and the first is the sentence I would most like to write:**

* *"p = 0.012346"* / *"the screen's cell prediction transfers across codewords."* **The primary is
  CANNOT ANSWER.** Quoting the binomial alone is forbidden by the prereg whenever two admitted heads
  share a predicted layer, and here `K_unique = 0`.
* *"head 23's mechanism is refuted."* It is **null on button**; a null on a codeword where the head has
  no effect is **CANNOT ANSWER at the head level**, exactly as rule §3.3 says of a floor-limited endpoint.
* *"the basket result is weakened."* S-306/S-307 stand on their own data. **This is a statement about
  TRANSFER**, and the transfer question is unresolved, not negative.
* anything about the other 29 heads, about DOMAIN generality, or about TEST (S-314: spent and
  selection-contaminated).

```
             head-level cross-codeword replication, 2 of 3 heads, plus a full button depth map.
queue        EMPTY.
NOT ESTABLISHED  whether the screen's cell prediction transfers across codewords. The design that
             was built to answer it cannot, and §5 says no button family can until a live button
```

```
all 31 non-base effects reproduced          max |diff| = 4.9851e-09   (8-decimal rounding)

13 of 27 have a ci95 excluding 0            CONFIRMED
ADMISSION: 17 ADMITTED 3.8705 | 19 ADMITTED 5.4506 | 23 DROPPED 0.6235 (ci95 crosses 0)  CONFIRMED
K=2, M=2, p = 0.012345679012                CONFIRMED
K_unique = 0, p_conditional = 1.0, p_permutation = 1.0 over 1 assignment  CONFIRMED
matching layers {L14} -> SPANNING RULE VIOLATED -> CANNOT ANSWER          CONFIRMED
head 23 argmax = L11 (-0.00294503), the screen's L7 second (-0.00278640)  CONFIRMED
```

Provenance re-checked from each run's own files: 230 rows on all 32 arms, `slurm_job_id` 923233 and
node **n-301 on all 32**, eager attention on all 32 (VOID 2 clear), uniform 3090s (VOID 1 clear),
`BC_BASE` carrying no intervention flag (VOID 4 clear), and **the 23 domains' intersection with the 23

### 2. ✅ THE BAR TRAP, MEASURED ON THIS FAMILY — and it is worse here than where it was named

I re-derived the bars myself before reading any verifier, and both readings were computed:

```
head   PAIRED-delta SD, ddof=1 -> bar      RAW per-domain means -> bar      factor
 17    0.007423719  == published            0.069069810                      9.30x
 19    0.006525442  == published            0.070561930                     10.81x
 23    0.004872546  == published            0.072675430                     14.92x
                     (ddof=0 on the paired deltas gives 0.007260/0.006382/0.004765 -- also wrong,
                      so the ddof is pinned too)
```

⚠ **Under the wrong reading NOT ONE CELL would clear ANY bar** — the largest |E| in the family is
0.039228 against a smallest wrong-bar of 0.069070. **The family would have read "0 of 27 clear": a
complete, clean-looking false null.** S-307/S-308 recorded this trap at ~6×; on button it is **9–15×**,
because the raw per-domain `y_install` spread is large relative to the knockout deltas. The producer
used the frozen S-311 rule correctly.

### 3. ⚠ CORRECTION (a) — S-317 §2's "4.3 % agreement" compares TWO DIFFERENT ESTIMATORS

S-317 §2 wrote: *"PR-CSI-013's `BT_CTRL_01` implied head 19's button bar at 0.006256; the rule computed
0.006525 — a 4.3 % disagreement against a preregistered 'more than 25 % is a finding' threshold. The
S-311 rule and the PR-013-derived number agree."*

**That is not what was compared.** My own freeze script computes the "prediction" as

```
sd  = (hi - lo) / 2.0 / 1.96 * sqrt(23)        # dcs_csi_pr016_freeze.py
bar = 1.96 * sd / sqrt(23)
```

and the `1.96` and `sqrt(23)` **cancel algebraically**. Verified numerically:

```
freeze script's predicted_bar = 0.00625619
(hi - lo) / 2                 = 0.00625619     identical to 1e-15
```

**The "prediction" is exactly half of PR-013's BOOTSTRAP ci95 width.** The round trip through `sd` is
vacuous decoration. So 0.006256 was never an S-311-rule quantity, and 4.3 % is **not** a
reproducibility measurement — it is the ordinary gap between a percentile-bootstrap half-width and a
normal-approximation SD estimate on the same 23 numbers.

⛔ **And the true cross-job number is better than the one I reported.** PR-013's `BT_CTRL_01` and
PR-016's `HD_19` are bit-identical (§4), so the S-311 rule applied to either gives **the same
0.006525 — a 0.0 % disagreement.** I reported a 4.3 % agreement between the wrong pair of things when
an exact agreement between the right pair was available.

📌 The prereg's *"more than 25 % is a finding"* clause therefore **never had the meaning I gave it**.
It compares a bootstrap half-width to a normal-approximation bar; those can differ by more than 25 %
on a skewed bootstrap **with nothing wrong at all**. The clause is retained as recorded — it is frozen

### 2. ⚠ THE DESIGN FAULT THE MEMO MISSED — head 19 is not an admissible candidate

The design memo proposed head 19 among the candidates and noted it as *"(already mapped)"* without
drawing the consequence. **PR-CSI-016 has ALREADY measured head 19's nine button cells and found its
argmax at L14, matching the screen.** Including it in PR-CSI-018's `M` would be **counting a known
success as if it were a fresh draw** — selection on data already read, and the cleanest possible way to
manufacture a p.

⛔ **Head 19 is EXCLUDED.** So are heads 17 and 23, for the same reason: PR-CSI-016 mapped all three.
**PR-CSI-018's candidates must be drawn only from heads never cell-mapped on button.** The six that
qualify are **11, 20, 29, 6, 24, 27** — all fresh, none touched by PR-016.

### 3. The permutation floor, which is what the head set actually buys

The permutation null asks whether the screen put its predictions on the **right heads**, so its floor
is `1 / (distinct assignments of the prediction multiset)` — repeated layers shrink the space:

```
candidate set                              distinct assignments   floor
6 fresh heads (11,20,29,6,24,27)                   180           0.00556   <- recommended
  multiset {L8, L11, L6, L11, L10, L10}
4 fresh, one per distinct layer                     24           0.04167   thin: M=3 and M=4 both give 1/24
5 fresh (the four distinct + 16 at L14)            120           0.00833
6 fresh + 16                                      1260           0.00079
```

**All six fresh heads is the right set**: it uses every admissible head, has the strongest floor of the
fresh-only options at **0.00556**, and — unlike the 4-head variant — leaves room for a miss. At 4
heads a single miss is fatal, because with four distinct layers *exactly three* fixed points is
combinatorially impossible, so `M=3` and `M=4` both evaluate to `1/24` and the design has no
graceful degradation at all.

⚠ **Head 16 is a judgement call I am NOT making unilaterally in a design note.** Adding it takes the
floor to 0.00079, but it predicts **L14** — the layer the whole spanning-rule apparatus exists to guard
against — and PR-016's experience is that an L14 prediction can match for reasons unrelated to the
screen. It is recorded as an option and will be decided **in the freeze script, with the reason
written down**, not here.

## S-321 — **PR-CSI-018 IS FROZEN: 62 arms, six FRESH button heads, none predicting L14, permutation floor 0.00556.** The design PR-CSI-016 could not be. ⚠ **And freezing it forced the judgement S-320 deferred, plus an anti-gaming clause I wrote only because I caught myself about to shop a threshold**

S-320 recorded the order as **R29 → freeze → launch**. **I have done freeze → R29 instead**, because
R28's two BLOCKERs were both *inside* the frozen artefacts — a prereg missing the census reader's
precondition fields, and a primary reader gating on a key its producer never writes. **A review that
runs before the artefacts exist cannot find that class.** R29 now has the whole family to review, which
is strictly more than it would have had. Nothing reaches a GPU before it runs.

### 2. What is frozen

**Every candidate's prediction is re-derived from the 288-cell screen by the freeze script, and a
drift to L14 on any head is a REFUSAL.** The nomination uses the TRAIN screen (layer) and PR-013's
button magnitude (eligibility) — **never any button CELL data**.

### 3. The three p-values, and why the permutation one is the point

```
binomial     P(Binom(K, 1/9) >= M)                                    floor at K=6  1.88e-06
conditional  over admitted heads with a UNIQUE predicted layer         K_unique = 2 at K=6
permutation  over distinct assignments of {L6, L8, L10, L10, L11, L11}  180 -> floor 0.00556
```

**PR-CSI-016 died with `K_unique = 0` and a permutation space of size 1.** Here the multiset has four
distinct layers and 180 assignments, so **a shared band-edge bias cannot fake the answer** — a bias
says nothing about *which head gets which layer*. That, and only that, is what the extra 30 arms buy.

### 4. The judgement S-320 deferred, now made: **head 16 is EXCLUDED**

Head 16 is live (1.60) and fresh, and including it would move the floor from 0.00556 to **0.00079**.
**It is excluded anyway**, because it predicts **L14 — the layer the whole spanning-rule apparatus
exists to guard against**, and PR-CSI-016 measured that an L14 prediction can match for reasons
unrelated to the screen. **Both floors clear α by two orders of magnitude, so the floor is not the
binding constraint**; keeping every candidate's prediction out of the adversary's favoured layer is
worth more than a factor of 7 on a number that already passes.

Heads **17, 19, 23** are excluded for the S-320 reason: PR-016 already measured their button cells, so
their argmaxes are **known**, and a known success counted as a fresh draw is manufactured.

### 5. ⛔ THE ANTI-GAMING CLAUSE, written because I caught myself about to shop a threshold

The six screen margins run **5.96× down to 1.07×**, and **head 20's is effectively a coin flip**
between L11 and its runner-up. S-307 recorded that a near-tie which happens to land right is far
weaker corroboration than a decisive peak, so a sharpness gate looked obviously right. Then I computed
what each gate does to the floor:

```
no gate          6 heads   180 assignments   floor 0.0056   clears alpha
margin >= 1.25   5 heads    60               floor 0.0167   clears alpha
margin >= 1.50   4 heads    12               floor 0.0833   CANNOT CLEAR
margin >= 2.00   2 heads     2               floor 0.5000   CANNOT CLEAR
```

⚠ **Every candidate threshold changes whether the family can certify at all.** Choosing among them —
and 1.25 is *right there*, keeping five heads and a floor that still passes — would be **tuning a free
parameter by its effect on the result**. So **no sharpness gate is applied**.

📌 **And that is sound rather than merely convenient, which matters because "I declined to gate" is
exactly what someone would say who had gated and lost:** a flat screen prediction is a **near-random**
one, which is **precisely what the permutation null models**. Flat predictions therefore cost
**POWER**, not **VALIDITY** — they make a true effect harder to find and cannot manufacture a false
one. The failure mode runs one way only.

The prereg and the read both now carry: **reporting any margin-restricted subset after the read — as
the result, as a rescue of a null, or as a qualification of a positive — is FORBIDDEN.** The six
margins are frozen per head *precisely so a post-hoc subset can be recognised as one*.

### 6. VOID condition 8 — six free provenance checks

Each `HD_<h>` arm re-measures the whole-head effect **PR-CSI-013 already recorded** on the same head,
codeword and split. S-318 demonstrated that PR-016's `HD_19` reproduced PR-013's `BT_CTRL_01`
**bit-identically across two jobs and two NODES**. So the prereg makes a difference above **1e-6** a
VOID: it would mean the population, bank, exclusions or model revision has drifted, and nothing in the
family would be readable. **Six independent provenance checks at zero extra cost**, because the arms
had to be run anyway to supply the bars.

### 7. Code: widened, not duplicated — and the regression checked

`scripts/dcs_csi_pr016_argmax_test.py` hard-coded `id == "PR-CSI-016"`. It is **widened to an EXPLICIT
list** `("PR-CSI-016", "PR-CSI-018")` — explicit rather than open, because *a test reader that accepts
any prereg is not a preregistered test*, which is the property the single-id check was protecting. It
also now validates the five prereg fields it needs **before** opening the census (S-296).

⚠ **The filename is now a misnomer and is kept anyway**: `runargs/dcs_csi_pr016_read.txt` names that
path, and a frozen read must go on resolving to the file it was frozen against (R26 chain of custody).

```
permutation assignments 180 (floor 0.00556), binomial floor at K=6 1.882e-06, 62 arms, ratio 1.5
TOTAL MISMATCHES: 0
```

**The class that bit twice in three entries did not bite this time.** That is worth one line and no
more — the interesting part is what running the artefacts found instead.

### 2. 🔴 BLOCKER 1 — the reader had PR-CSI-016's ARM PREFIX hardcoded

S-321 widened the reader to `("PR-CSI-016", "PR-CSI-018")` and added a prereg-field pre-check. **It
changed the id check and nothing else.** Two lines still built cell-arm names by string:

```
scripts/dcs_csi_pr016_argmax_test.py:106   if "BC_H%s_L%02d" % (h, band[0]) not in E:
scripts/dcs_csi_pr016_argmax_test.py:117   cells = {L: E["BC_H%s_L%02d" % (h, L)] for L in band}
```

`BC_` is PR-CSI-016's prefix. **PR-CSI-018 uses `BF_`.** Running the frozen STEP 2 on a well-formed
PR-018 census:

```
REFUSING: head 6's single-cell arms are absent from the census report. (R28/S-312)
```

— on a census containing **all 54 of them**. The refusal was S-312's own guard, firing correctly on a
question the reader was asking wrongly.

**Fixed by deleting the convention, not by adding a second one:** the prereg already maps arm → cells,
so the reader now **inverts `cell_sets`** to resolve each `(head, layer)` to its arm. A family may call
its arms anything. It also refuses a prereg with two arms for one cell, and one missing a band layer.

### 3. 🔴 BLOCKER 2 — the reader applied PR-016's SUCCESS RULE to PR-018, and it prints PASS at p = 0.33

With BLOCKER 1 fixed the reader ran — and produced this:

```
case                  K  M  binomial    conditional  permutation  VERDICT
3 of 6 match          6  3  2.117e-02   0.2099       0.0167       PASS   <- weakest 0.21
all six match, K=3    3  3  1.372e-03   0.1111       0.3333       PASS   <- weakest 0.33
```

**PR-CSI-018's prereg says: `SUCCESS = the WEAKEST of the three p-values <= 0.05`.** The reader
implements **PR-CSI-016's** rule, whose prereg says the opposite in as many words — *"these do NOT gate
the preregistered PASS/FAIL … They BOUND THE WORDING"* — because at `K_unique = 0` gating on them
would have failed that family **structurally** rather than empirically.

⚠ **Both preregs are right about themselves. The reader was right about only one of them.** A criterion
that lives in prose in one document and in code written for another is **two criteria** (S-302) — and
the second case is the damning one: **three admitted heads give a permutation floor of 1/3, so a
perfect M = K = 3 would have been announced as a PASS at p = 0.333.**

**Fixed by making the gating rule the PREREG's declaration:** `PRIMARY.GATING`, with
`binomial_only` as the **default** so PR-016's published read is untouched, `weakest_of_three` declared
explicitly by PR-018, and **any other value REFUSED** rather than silently defaulted.

```
after the fix:  3 of 6 match  -> FAIL (conditional 0.2099)
                K=3, M=3      -> FAIL (permutation 0.3333)
                6 of 6, 5 of 6 -> PASS (weakest 0.0056)
```

📌 **Why PR-018 may gate on the permutation test when PR-016 could not**, recorded in the prereg rather
than left implicit: PR-016's exemption was structural — it had no informative head left. **PR-018 was
BUILT so that test is answerable**: six heads over four distinct layers, 180 assignments,
`K_unique = 2`. The structural excuse does not apply, so the test a shared band-edge bias cannot fake
is allowed to **gate**, not merely to annotate.

### 4. Verification

```
4 new tests, each asserting the PROPERTY -> ALL FOUR FAIL on the committed pre-fix reader
   (checked by `git stash` on that file alone, so the failure is behavioural and not an import error
    -- S-315 recorded me nearly accepting a crash as a vacuity check)
70 tests pass across test_csi_pr016_argmax.py and test_csi_cell_identity.py
PR-CSI-016's published argmax report re-runs with EVERY VALUE IDENTICAL; three keys are ADDED
   (GATING, gating_p_name, gating_p) and none changed. Same precedent as S-312's PR-015 re-read.
prereg re-emitted: md5 c4483891 -> 18994cf6 (the GATING declaration); it re-emits byte-identically
   and NO ARM HAS RUN, so this is a re-freeze before data, not after (VOID 10 untouched)
```

### 5. 📌 The pattern, named because it is now the second instance in two entries

S-321 widened a reader by changing the one thing that **named** the old family, and left everything
that **assumed** it. R28 found the same shape: a reader gating on a key its producer never wrote,
behind nine green tests. The generalisation:

> **Widening a single-family artefact means finding everything that ENCODES the family, not everything
> that NAMES it.** The id check is what names it; the arm prefix and the success rule are what encode
> it, and neither is grep-able from the id.

And both were invisible to reading and obvious to running — which is why the S-312 rule
(*run the frozen artefacts end to end before submitting*) is now the only reason this family is not
about to waste 2.9 GPU-hours on a read that could not execute and then could not be believed.

S-322 made gating prereg-driven with `binomial_only` as the default. R29 pointed out the consequence:

### 4. ⚠ AND MY OWN TESTS FOR §2 WERE VACUOUS ON FIRST WRITING

The three VOID-8 tests asserted `"VOID CONDITION" in out` where `out` was **captured stdout only**.
`sys.exit("message")` puts the refusal in `e.code`, **not on stdout** — so those assertions were
looking for text that is *structurally never there*. They failed loudly, which is the good case; had
I written them as `assert rc != 0` alone they would have passed while checking nothing.

**Fixed by returning both channels as one searchable blob**, and recorded because it is the third
distinct way I have written a weak test in this sprint — after the literal-matching test S-315
rewrote, and the fabricated-input helper R28 caught.

```
73 tests pass across test_csi_cell_identity.py and test_csi_pr016_argmax.py
PR-CSI-016 is UNAFFECTED: 0 PROVENANCE lines (it declares no reference block), max |dE| = 0.0
```
