## S-325 — **the attention-mass instrument is BUILT, and the criterion it will be read against is FROZEN BEFORE IT RUNS.** 🔴 **And building it found a live TEST hazard: `retrieval_strength.py` had NO way to restrict its population, so pointed at any `ts116m` bank it would have read the POOLED 116 domains — every TEST domain included.** Never realised, now impossible

### 1. Why the criterion comes first

S-316 blocked the source-side family on an unmade measurement, and S-319 corrected which *direction*
the measurement licenses. **A measurement whose interpretation is settled afterwards is how post-hoc
rationalisation gets in**, so the rule is written here, before the instrument has produced a number.

The confound, stated exactly. `demo_all` removes the demo keys (mass `m_d`); a `nondemo_matched_d*`
arm removes an equal **COUNT** of non-demo keys (mass `m_c`). What a null control means depends
entirely on which is larger:

```
m_c > m_d, control NULL   -> MORE attention removed, LESS damage. Mass cannot explain it.
                             CLEAN EVIDENCE FOR source-specificity.
m_c < m_d, control NULL   -> less attention, less damage. CONFOUNDED -- could be either.
m_c ~ m_d, control NULL   -> equal mass, less damage. CLEAN, and the ideal case.
m_c > m_d, control EQUAL  -> ambiguous, leans non-specific (saturation cannot be ruled out).
m_c < m_d, control EQUAL  -> LESS attention, SAME damage. CLEAN REFUTATION of source-specificity.
```

**FROZEN CRITERION, to be applied to the measurement before any source-side arm is designed:**

```
measure, per row, in band 6-14 at the readout position:
   m_d = demo-block mass ; m_c = the STRICT, PROTECTED nondemo_matched_d1 draw's mass
report   the median ratio rho = m_c / m_d, AND the per-row count of rows with m_d > m_c
         (C-CONT-019's own statistic was a per-row count, not a mean, and it must stay one)

rho >= 1.0 and m_d > m_c on < 50% of rows  ->  the family may run as a CONFIRMATORY source test
rho <= 1.0 and m_d > m_c on > 50% of rows  ->  the family may run ONLY as a REFUTATION test
mixed / straddling                          ->  CANNOT ANSWER: the direction is not established and
                                                no source-side family is licensed either way
```

⛔ **The direction is fixed BEFORE the arms are designed, and whichever prereg follows must state
which of the two readings it is licensed for.** A family that discovers its licensed direction after
its own read is not preregistered.

### 2. 🔴 THE HAZARD FOUND WHILE BUILDING IT

`src/boombness/retrieval_strength.py` (184 lines) had **no `--exclude-prompt-ids` argument at all**.
Its population is a bank path plus four content filters. So pointed at any `ts116m` bank it reads the
**pooled 116 domains — all 23 TEST domains included.**

Per **S-314**, TEST's one confirmatory read is **already spent** (job 869523, 2026-09-08) *and* the
split is **selection-contaminated**. Adding to that silently would be the worst available outcome.

✅ **It has never happened.** Every existing run used `boombness_prompt_bank.jsonl`, and
`grep -rl ts116m outputs/boombness/retrieval_strength/` returns **0**. **The hazard was real and
unrealised — which is exactly when it is cheap to close**, and it is the same lesson S-310 paid for:
a collision inert only because no artefact has the shape yet is a dated liability.

Closed by a refusal that fires **before anything loads**, mirroring the guard
`scripts/dcs_ts_make_exclusions.py` already carries:

```
[retr] REFUSING: 'boombness_prompt_bank_ts116m_basket_bomb.jsonl' is under the frozen ts116m domain
       split, and no --exclude-prompt-ids was given, so this run would read the POOLED population
       INCLUDING all 23 TEST domains. ... Pass the split's exclusion file, or --confirm-test-read to
       say you mean it. (S-325)
```

📌 And this is **part of the mechanism behind S-314's finding**. S-314 recorded 23 `ts116m` runs with
no exclusion list at all, and observed the contamination without explaining how it kept happening.
**An instrument with no way to express a population will be run without one.**

### 3. What the instrument now measures

```
--exclude-prompt-ids     the missing argument. Verified: 930 excluded -> exactly n=230, the frozen
                         validation population, on the basket bank.
strict_protected_mass_band   the STRICT, PROTECTED, correctly-seeded nondemo_matched_d{1,2,3} draws
strict_protected_n_keys / _infeasible / n_protected_positions
```

⚠ **The existing `ctrl_mass_band_REFERENCE_ONLY` is NOT this.** It calls
`knockout_key_set("nondemo_random", dk, seq_len, args.seed + i)` — **no `protected=`**, so it draws
from the UNPROTECTED pool, and its seed corresponds to **no arm any run would ever use**. That is the
draw C-CONT-019 refuted. It is kept, unchanged, for continuity with the 2026-08-24 artefacts, and it
is not the number the criterion is applied to.

### 4. NOT established, and NOT run

⛔ **The measurement has NOT been made.** The instrument is built and guarded; `923833` holds the GPU.
Nothing about `m_c / m_d` is known, and **S-316's block therefore still stands** — the source-side
family remains unrunnable until the criterion in §1 is applied to a real number.

**And S-319's correction to the old figure stands unaltered:** the "~5.7×, demo > ctrl in 0 of 12
rows" I quoted from the predecessor log does not reproduce from the artefact it cites (3.85× and 1 of
60 on Llama; 4.77× and 0 of 46 on Qwen3). Those are the **unprotected** draw on a **different bank**,
so they do not predict what §1 will measure either.

### 5. PR-CSI-018 state

```

all launcher guards passed on the first attempt: BASE-ARM, CODEWORD -> button, 62 arms with 60
  carrying a frozen cell list, argv lines 62. Fourth family in a row with every guard green first try.
No endpoint has been read. The frozen read (cbdf34a2) is untouched.
```

⚠ n-304 has no prior load measurement, so per S-324 **no prediction was made and none is being scored**
— whatever it records is a first data point for that node.

923833  n-304  60 min elapsed  |  0 of 62 arms  |  NO "MODEL LOAD" line
  .err   0 bytes, unmodified since 00:41 -- THE WEIGHT-LOADING BAR NEVER APPEARED AT ALL
  .out   20850 bytes, unmodified since 01:01 -- 36 minutes with no byte written
  last .out line: "[score] population filter {...}"  -- the first arm's setup, BEFORE the load
```

**Two readings four minutes apart, byte-for-byte identical.** S-039's operational rule:

> *"the weight-loading bar in `.err` after **two readings a few minutes apart** is the only reliable
> liveness test, and a node that shows **0/291 twice is bad** — cancel immediately rather than waiting
> out the walltime."*

This is worse than 0/291 twice: **the bar never appeared**, so the process had not reached the point
of reading a single shard. Cancelled.

### 2. ⚠ THE COUNTER-PRECEDENT, because a relaunch decision has gone wrong here before

**S-285 recorded a relaunch that LOST**: *"the measured number refutes S-272's relaunch decision —
STAYING ON 919296 WOULD HAVE FINISHED ~2.8 h EARLIER."* So "it is taking a long time" is **not**
sufficient grounds, and that entry exists to stop exactly this reflex.

**The discriminator is ADVANCEMENT, not elapsed time**, and that is precisely what S-039's rule
encodes:

```
n-302, S-285   COLD load, 19278.4 s (5.36 h)   -- but the shard counter was ADVANCING throughout
n-304, here    60 min, no bar, no bytes         -- nothing to advance
```

A 5.36-hour advancing load is **slow**; a 60-minute load that has not read shard 1 is **stuck**. The
two look identical on a wall clock and opposite in `.err`, which is why the rule is written about
`.err` and not about minutes.

### 3. The quarantine, which S-261 makes mandatory rather than tidy

923833 left **one** arm directory:

```
outputs/boombness/score_behavior/csi10_cell6_button_validation_BF_BASE_20260924_005635_1893033
  contents: config.json, RUNMETA.json, plots        NO DONE.json, NO results.jsonl
```

Its contents confirm the diagnosis independently — the arm printed its population filter and then
never produced a row.

⛔ **It could not simply be left there.** S-261 measured that the runner's **skip-if-complete RESUMES
into an existing arm directory**, so a relaunch under the same tag would have inherited this corpse
rather than re-running `BF_BASE` — and `--require-slurm-job` is a **READ-time** remedy for a
**WRITE-time** problem. Moved to `outputs/boombness/QUARANTINE/` with a `QUARANTINE_REASON.md`
recording the evidence, the rule applied, and where the family went. `csi10_*` under
`score_behavior/` is now **0**.

### 4. The relaunch, pinned rather than excluded

```
sh scripts/gates/dcs_csi_submit.sh slurm_scripts/dcs_csi_pr010_arms.slurm --nodelist=n-301
provenance: BLOB 3c3c3d26  PORCELAIN clean
Submitted batch job 923972   -> RUNNING on n-301
```

S-039: *"Keep a known-good list and pin to it. **Exclusion lists chase the problem; a positive pin
ends it.**"* **n-301 is this sprint's known-good node** — three completed loads (1339.1 / 1273.2 /
1265.8 s) and three completed families (PR-014, PR-015, PR-016).

**Confirmed advancing, by the same two-reading test that condemned n-304:**

```
reading 1   Loading weights:  0%|  | 0/291 [00:00<?, ?it/s]     <- the bar EXISTS, which n-304 never managed
reading 2   Loading weights:  3%|▎ | 9/291 [03:18<42:03, 8.95s/it]
```

📌 **n-304 is recorded as bad ON THIS OCCASION, not permanently.** S-039 listed n-302 and n-307 among
the indefinitely-stalling nodes, and this sprint has since seen n-302 complete a 5.36 h load and n-307
return a 47.5 s one. **A node's mount is a state, not a property**, so the known-good list is a
heuristic for choosing, never evidence about a node that was not tried.

### 5. 📌 A FALSIFIABLE PREDICTION, recorded before the load completes

S-314 concluded that **on n-301** the load is *"effectively a NODE CONSTANT (~1270–1340 s), not a
function of cache residency at all"*, from three measurements varying 5.5 % across gaps of 3 minutes
to 2.5 hours. **This load is running at ~9 s/shard over 291 shards.**

```
S-314's node-constant reading predicts    ~1270-1340 s   (21-22 min)
the observed rate projects                ~2600-3200 s   (43-53 min)
```

**These are incompatible.** If 923972's `MODEL LOAD` lands near 2600–3200 s, **S-314's "node constant"
reading is REFUTED** — n-301's load would then be a function of cache state after all, and the gap
since PR-016 finished (~2.5 h, the same order as the gaps S-314 examined) would no longer explain it.
If it lands near 1300 s despite the current rate, the early shards are simply unrepresentative and the
constant survives.

⚠ Recorded now because **it costs nothing and a prediction written afterwards is not a prediction** —
the same reason S-303 and S-313 wrote theirs, one of which was then refuted (S-304) and one confirmed
(S-314). **I have no stake in which way this one goes.**

## S-327 — ⚠ **MY S-326 PREDICTION IS REFUTED and S-314's "node constant" SURVIVES, now on four measurements.** The load landed at **1264.0 s** against my projected 2619–3201 s — **a 2.07× overestimate, because I extrapolated a 291-shard load from its first NINE shards**

### 1. The number, and the prediction it settles

S-326 recorded, before the load completed, that the two readings were incompatible:

```
S-314's node-constant reading predicted     ~1270-1340 s
my extrapolation from the first 9 shards    ~2619-3201 s   (9 s/it x 291)
```

```
[w3] MODEL LOAD #1 (1264.0 s)
Loading weights: 100%|##########| 291/291 [20:48<00:00, 4.29s/it]
```

**1264.0 s. My projection is REFUTED; S-314's reading survives.**

### 2. The rule is now on four measurements, and it has tightened

```
n-301 MODEL LOAD       S-298  1339.1 s      S-304  1273.2 s
                       S-314  1265.8 s      S-327  1264.0 s
range 75.1 s over four loads  |  spread 5.8 %  |  sd 31.1 s
THE LAST THREE LIE WITHIN 9.2 s OF EACH OTHER
```

The gaps behind these are **3 minutes, 2 hours, 2.5 hours and now ~2.9 hours** since the previous job
on that node. S-314 called it *"effectively a NODE CONSTANT … not a function of cache residency at
all"* and refused to generalise past n-301. **A fourth point at a fourth gap does not overturn that
and does tighten it** — but it is still one node, and n-302 (19278 s cold) and n-307 (47.5 s warm)
remain the evidence that the constant is a property of *this* node's mount, not of the model or the
filesystem.

### 3. 📌 WHY I WAS WRONG, and it is a methodological error rather than bad luck

**The shard rate is NOT STATIONARY within a load.** The first nine shards ran at ~9–11 s/it; the whole
291 averaged **4.29 s/it**. I extrapolated from **3 % of the work** and overestimated by **2.07×**.

⚠ **This is the same error as S-288 and S-289, one object over.** S-288 built an arm-time band on
"the three fastest arms" and had to revise it; S-289 then found S-288's own window had been dominated
by the slow block it had just discovered, and revised again — *five revisions in total*, each caused
by projecting a non-stationary series from an unrepresentative early window.

**I knew that lesson and applied it to arm times, not to shard rates.** The generalisation worth
keeping:

> **A rate measured over the opening of a monotone-looking process is an upper bound on nothing.**
> Load bars, arm series and domain sweeps in this sprint have all been non-stationary; the honest
> projection uses either the whole prior distribution for that node, or no projection at all.

📌 And the prediction was still worth writing. **It cost nothing, it was falsifiable, and being wrong
sharpened a rule that a confirmation would have left vague** — S-314's constant now has a fourth point
*and* an explicit statement of what would have broken it. S-304 made the same trade and lost the same
way; S-313 made it and won.

### 4. What this does NOT establish

* **Nothing about n-304.** S-326 recorded it as bad *on that occasion*; this entry adds no evidence
  either way, and the pin to n-301 was a choice about known-good nodes, not a claim about n-304.
* **Nothing about the science.** No endpoint has been read. 923972 is past its load with 0 of 62 arms
  landed at the time of writing; the frozen read (`cbdf34a2`) is untouched and every branch of its
  PRIMARY is open.
* **Nothing about the attention-mass measurement** (S-325), which needs the GPU this family holds.

half of that: *"a deferral never discharged is just a defect with a citation."* Both are discharged

              +0.0026 -> 0.8156 | +0.0028 -> 0.8725 | +0.0030 -> 0.9240

as a multiple of the observed effect      1.89x        AM-25 states 2.3x

number is too high, and **the table now carries mine**, because it is the one I can defend.

## S-331 — **the attention-mass instrument gets a COMMITTED launcher, and GATE 0 caught ME.** The sweep refused my own mistyped invocation with "THIS IS NOT A PASS" instead of a silent zero — the S-308/S-315 hardening firing on its author. 🔴 **Nothing was measured.**

### 1. What was done

`src/boombness/retrieval_strength.py` — the instrument S-316 blocked the whole source-side
family on, and whose criterion S-325 froze — **has been run under slurm before (job 777320, n-801)
but NO COMMITTED SLURM SCRIPT LAUNCHES IT.** The invocation lived somewhere uncommitted. That is
the same provenance gap class as S-302: a measurement that decides whether an entire family may
run must be reproducible from the repo, not reconstructed from memory at the moment the GPU frees.

`slurm_scripts/dcs_csi_retrieval_mass.slurm` is now that launcher. It is deliberately boring:

```
CW=basket|button          the codeword, mandatory -- no default, so it cannot be run "on whatever"
--exclude-prompt-ids      MANDATORY. Without it a ts116m bank is read POOLED, which includes all
                          23 TEST domains. S-325 added the flag AND a refusal guard that fires
                          before the model loads. This script never relies on the guard alone.
forward-only              output_attentions=True, use_cache=False, no generation. Reads no
                          endpoint, writes no arm, cannot touch any family's GATE 0.
S-325's criterion         reproduced verbatim in the header as a comment, so the decision rule
                          travels with the invocation instead of living only in the log.
```

### 2. The verification, and the hole I found in my own verification

Every path it names resolves (script, both banks, both exclusion lists, the model snapshot).
Then I checked that every flag it passes is actually declared by the CLI — the S-293 lesson.

**My first check had the exact defect I recorded two ticks ago.** The regex was line-anchored,
`^\s+(--[a-z0-9-]+)`, so on a line reading `--band-lo 6 --band-hi 14` it matched **only the
first flag**. It reported "13 flags, none missing" and I nearly took that as the all-clear.
`--band-hi` and `--late-hi` had never been looked at. Re-run unanchored over everything after the
invocation: **15 flags, all 15 declared.** So the conclusion survives — but it survived by luck,
not by the check.

> A verification pattern that silently skips half its inputs reports "all clear" in exactly the
> same voice as one that checked them. This is the SECOND time this sprint that a
> silently-under-matching pattern has produced a false all-clear (the first was `^\[w3\] [0-9]+/32`
> against a right-aligned counter). Both times the text looked right. **Anchoring is an assumption
> about formatting, and formatting is not a contract.**

`--partition`, `--account=gpu-research` and `--gpus=geforce_rtx_3090:1` were confirmed against
`dcs_csi_pr010_arms.slurm`, a launcher known to work, rather than against my recollection.

**The seed is the load-bearing detail.** `--seed 20260913`, read out of a landed PR-018 arm's own
`config.json` (`seed = 20260913`, `seed_source = 'args.seed'`) rather than assumed. The strict
PROTECTED control draws are `nondemo_draw_seed(seed, idx)`, so this makes the instrument measure
**the same draws the real arms make**. A different seed would have measured a different random
control set and answered a question nobody asked.

### 3. GATE 0 on PR-CSI-018 — and the gate refusing its author

I first invoked the sweep with `--tag-prefix csi10_cell6_button`. The frozen read
(`runargs/dcs_csi_pr018_read.txt`, md5 cbdf34a2) specifies `csi10_cell6_button_validation`. The
arm dirs carry the split in the tag, so the glob matched nothing and **all 62 arms reported
"-- not landed --"** while 29 of them sat on disk with `DONE.json`.

It did not print a pass. It printed:

```
GATE 0: NOTHING TO CHECK -- 0 of 62 declared arms resolved. THIS IS NOT A PASS.
  Either no arm has landed yet, or --tag-prefix/--split/--require-slurm-job name something
  that does not exist.
```

That is R27/S-308 and S-315 working **on the person who wrote them**. The failure mode those
entries were about — an arm that is present but unreadable being silently scored as absent, and
the family then certified on a shrunken denominator — is precisely what would have happened here
had the gate trusted its own zero. It cost me one re-run and zero false confidence.

Re-run as frozen:

```
GATE 0: every landed arm passes (29 of 62). Identity verified from each arm's own
        knockout_cells. No endpoint field was read.
  .. 1 arm(s) IN FLIGHT (run dir present, no DONE.json). THIS SWEEP IS PARTIAL and is
     NOT the family's GATE 0 verdict.
                                   29 passing + 1 in flight + 32 not landed = 62  ✓
```

### 4. The ETA, and why I am not quoting the range my own script produced

Median inter-arm gap over the 29 completed gaps is **171.0 s**; min 167.0; max **1442.0**.
Naively propagating the range gives "1.5 h to 12.8 h", which is worthless. The 1442 s gap is
`BF_BASE -> BF_KO` — one-time model load plus the base arm — and **does not recur**. Every
cell-arm gap sits in a 167–175 s band. So:

```
32 arms x 171 s = 5472 s = ~1.5 h remaining.   Job 923972, n-301, 1:44:52 elapsed of a 12 h
                                               walltime. Walltime is not the binding constraint.
```

S-327 is the reason this paragraph exists: I overestimated a load by 2.07x by extrapolating from
its first nine shards. The discipline that fixes it is not "distrust extrapolation" — it is
**identify the non-repeating events and exclude them before you extrapolate.**

head  pr013 arm      n_dom     E (derived)    E (prereg ref)    |diff|      bar     |E|/bar   read says
  6   BT_CTRL_06        23     -0.00509022     -0.00509022     4.16e-09   0.002100   2.4241     2.42

**The witness chain is not a stored field — it is `prereg -> named pr013_arm -> landed rows -> frozen

### 3. THE DEFECTS. Six real, one BLOCKER. All fixed.

**R30-B F1 — BLOCKER. The reader instructed the write-up to quote the forbidden number.**
`THE_CLAIM_MUST_BE_STATED_WITH` was gated on *"do two ADMITTED heads share a predicted layer"* —
PR-CSI-016's criterion — not on the prereg's declared `PRIMARY.GATING`. S-323 moved the **gate** onto
the prereg and left the **wording** one field behind. Any admission leaving the survivors' predicted
layers distinct flipped that field to *"the binomial p alone"* — inside a JSON whose own
`MUST_NOT_BE_SAID_IF_POSITIVE[0]` says quoting the binomial alone is FORBIDDEN. R30-B produced it:
a PASS gated on permutation = 0.041667 whose published instruction named a binomial **273x smaller**,
with the conditional and permutation p's never printed at all. Both now follow `GATING`.

**R30-B F4 — the reader could not substantiate its own frozen read's claim.** The GATE 0 check
iterated the census record's own keys and used `len(per_arm)` as the denominator, so a truncated
record self-reported a truncated total: **absence was a pass**, two lines below a refusal saying
absence is not a pass. `n_arms_per_split` was never read. Cutting `per_arm` to one arm while leaving
all 61 other E's intact published `VERDICT PASS, K=6, M=6`. Now refuses on any declared arm missing.

**R30-A F2 — a check that printed `OK` beside a 3860x violation.** `void_tolerance` fell back to a
`1e-6` **supplied by the reader** and was accepted at any magnitude — while ten lines away
`BAR_IS_A_RULE.z` must be declared *("the rule's only numeric parameter cannot be supplied by this
file — that would publish a default as though it were preregistered")* and range-checked. With
`void_tolerance: 1e9` the reader printed `|diff|=3.86e-03  OK`. Now: must be declared, must lie in
`(0, 1e-3]`.

**R30-A F1 — VOID 8 skipped silently, and the artefact could not tell.** A missing or null reference
hit a bare `continue`: no count, no print, no record, and **the report carried no provenance key at
all**, so "checked and free" was indistinguishable from "never checked" — which *was the substance of
R29's finding*. Closing the drift case while leaving the absence case silent reinstated it one branch
over. Now every skipped head is named on stdout and a `VOID_8_PROVENANCE` block records each check,
its diff, and the tolerance actually used.

**R30-A F5 — a check that was literally `X or True`.** The base arm's identity verdict read
`ok_id, why = (got in (None, "ALL", []) or True), "not intervened"` — unconditionally `True`, with

the report wrote `"recorded": null`, actively concealing a flag rather than merely missing it. VOID
condition 4 was in exactly the state R29 found VOID 8 in: prose consumed by no reader. Now a real test.

**R30-D CONCERN 1 — CONFIRMED, and it bit at the worst possible moment.** GATE 0's terminal verdict
was indistinguishable from its partial one: `61 of 62` with one crashed arm exited **0**, the same
code as a complete pass. R30-D's fixture — `DONE.json` deleted, `results.jsonl` truncated to 117 of
230 rows — printed `.. IN FLIGHT` and `every landed arm passes (31 of 62)`, exit 0. Worse, the file's
own comment promised *"the arm-count guard is what catches a family that never completed"* and **no
such guard existed anywhere in it**. The R29 VOID-8 shape again: a comment asserting a protection
nothing performs. Now `landed != len(arms)` exits 3 — `1 = failure`, `3 = ran but NOT the verdict`,
`0 = all arms passed`.

### 4. 🔴 TWO OF MY OWN FIXES OVER-REACHED, AND THE EXISTING SUITE CAUGHT BOTH

**(a) I silently overrode a preregistered verdict.** R30-B's F2 is that at `K_unique = 0` the
conditional is the placeholder `1.0` — not a p-value — and `max()` promotes that placeholder to the
gate, publishing a perfect 4-of-4 as a FAIL carrying the IF_NULL prohibitions: verbatim the S-317
death this family was built to escape. I fixed it with a general guard: *if the gating statistic's
own floor cannot clear alpha, the read was unwinnable, so CANNOT ANSWER.*

It converted `K=3, M=3` — permutation floor 1/3 — from FAIL to CANNOT ANSWER. **An existing test
failed.** And the test was right: the prereg says in terms *"FAILURE = the weakest p > 0.05 **with
K >= 3**"*. K=3 qualifies. I had decided, after the fact, that a preregistered FAILURE was really a
non-answer because its floor was unflattering — **the exact post-hoc move this sprint exists to
forbid**, dressed as a bug fix.

> A guard that converts an adverse preregistered verdict into "no verdict" is not a fix. It is the
> thing preregistration is for, running backwards. That the reasoning was sound in the K<3 case is
> what made it dangerous in the K>=3 case: **a correct principle applied one step past its licence.**

Corrected: the floor now changes the verdict **only at K < 3**, where the prereg licenses no FAILURE
at all. At K >= 3 the prereg's FAILURE stands — with the structural fact attached to `why`, so an
unwinnable FAIL can never be cited as evidence against the screen.

**(b) I made a legitimate prereg shape illegal.** I turned a *partial* reference declaration into a
refusal, reasoning by analogy with S-308's "if a prereg declares bars PER HEAD, every head must be in
it". The analogy is false, and the VOID-8 tests caught it. A bar is something every head must have; a
**prior measurement** is something a head either has or does not — PR-CSI-016's heads 17 and 23 had
never had a button arm, *which is the entire reason S-311's bar-as-a-RULE exists*. Corrected to
disclosure rather than refusal.

**Both over-reaches shared one shape: I generalised a rule from the case that motivated it to a case
that merely resembled it.** Neither was caught by reading the diff; both were caught by tests written
for a different purpose months of entries ago.

### 7. The design map, computed before the read so it cannot be argued about after it

`scripts/dcs_csi_pr018_design_map.py` (new; nothing existing computes an argmax-agreement statistic
— `dcs_csi_head_power.py` gives the same "nothing was reusable" reason for its own existence).

```
outcome patterns that CERTIFY : 5 of 64      minimum M among them : 5
ALL of them require BOTH unique-layer heads (11 and 29) to match : TRUE
```

The conditional p runs over the two unique-layer heads **alone**, so it can take only three values —
`0.012346`, `0.209877`, `1.0`. Therefore **`M=5` certifies if heads 11 and 29 are among the matches
and FAILS at p = 0.21 if either is not**, and `M=4` fails whatever happens (permutation 0.0778).

Admission moves this, because the prereg defines uniqueness *among the admitted*:

```
admitted        K_uniq  n_perm   cond floor   perm floor   perfect-result verdict
all six              2     180     0.012346     0.005556    CERTIFIES  (weakest 0.012346)
drop a TIE head      3      60     0.001372     0.016667    CERTIFIES  (weakest 0.016667)
drop h11 or h29      1      30     0.111111     0.033333    CANNOT CERTIFY, however perfect
K = 3 admitted       -       -            -            -    0 of 20 subsets can certify
```

And the admission slack, from the bars re-derived in section 2:

```
head 27  ratio 1.5426  slack over the preregistered 1.5 = +2.8%   <-- the one at risk
head 24  ratio 1.8365  +22.4%
head  6  ratio 2.4241  +61.6%        head 29  ratio 2.4937  +66.2%
head 20  ratio 2.8537  +90.2%        head 11  ratio 2.8551  +90.3%
```

**The design is robust exactly where it must be.** The head most likely to fail admission (27, at
2.8% slack) predicts L10 — a tie — so losing it *raises* K_unique to 3 and the family survives. The
two heads whose loss would kill it (11 and 29) have the largest slack of all six. That is a property
of the frozen design, recorded now, with no number from this family in hand. ⚠ These are PR-013's
bars; PR-018 recomputes admission from its **own** HD_<h> arms, so they are an EXPECTATION and not
the verdict.

## S-333 — **R30-A's four remaining findings are CLOSED, so nothing from R30 is left open before the read.** 🔴 The worst of them: **a stray `per_head` key could DELETE A WHOLE HEAD from a published depth map, moving the headline from "6 of 8 cells CLEAR" to "3 of 4", exit 0, with no line of stdout mentioning it**

### 1. Why these and why now

S-332 fixed everything in R30 that fires on the PR-CSI-018 read as written and left R30-A's F3, F4,
F6 and F7 open, recording that all four are **latent on the current prereg**. The family is ~50
minutes from its read and the queue is otherwise idle, so the cheapest moment to close a latent
defect is now — before the config that makes it latent is the only thing standing between the read
and a silent wrong answer.

> "Latent" is a property of today's config, not of the code. The four fixes below cost one tick;
> discovering any of them *from a published depth map* would cost the family.

### 2. F3 — **arms were deleted from the census on the strength of a name nothing checked**

`_BAR_SOURCE_ARMS` unions the granularity set with **every arm any `per_head` entry names**, and
`_judged` then drops all of them. `_bar_from_rule`'s in-family and full-band guards only ever run for
heads that reach `_bar_for` — heads that *still have judged cells* — so a `per_head` key for a head
with no single-cell arms was never validated at all.

R30-A demonstrated both magnitudes. One stray entry `per_head["99"] = {"bar_source_arm":
"BF_H11_L07"}` cut `n_cells_judged` from 8 to 7. **Four stray entries naming head 6's four cells
deleted head 6 entirely** — gone from the depth map, from the per-head bars, from every clearing
count, the per-head summary collapsing to the single-bar form, the headline moving from *"6 of 8
cells CLEAR THE PREREGISTERED BAR"* to *"3 of 4"* — exit 0, and **not one line of stdout mentioning
the exclusion**. The only trace was a JSON key a reader of the log never sees.

The file's own comment already names this shape — *"the named arm has already been removed from the
census … An arm can vanish from a published depth map with no check having looked at it"* — and had
closed only the both-criteria sub-case. The geometry guard is now **hoisted to run for every named
source before any exclusion**: the key must be a head of this family, and the arm must be that head's
full band.

### 3. F4 — the exclusion set existed only in the JSON

`bar_source_arms_EXCLUDED_FROM_THE_DEPTH_MAP` was written to the report and **printed nowhere**.
These families are read from the log. A depth map and a clearing count appeared with no indication
that arms had been removed to produce them. Now printed next to the GATE 0 banner, with the judged
count beside it.

### 4. F6 — `or` is not a search

`_detect_block = (PER_HEAD or DETECTABILITY_PREREGISTERED or {})`. The moment a prereg carried a
per-head block the **legacy block became unreachable for every field**. That is exactly the S-308
defect the single resolver was written to end — *"a null in a published artefact"* — transposed off
the bars and onto the coherent-outcome text: a prereg that **does** record
`COHERENT_OUTCOME_IF_NOTHING_CLEARS` in the legacy block published `null`, and had nothing cleared
the bar, stdout would have printed *"⚠ THE PREREG RECORDS NO COHERENT-OUTCOME TEXT … do not read this
null as a preregistered null"* against a prereg that records precisely that text. Now both blocks are
searched in precedence order: the per-head block still wins every field it defines, but a field it
does **not** define is no longer invisible.

### 5. F7 — closed as a consequence, and a self-inflicted repeat of it

F7 was that the VOID-8 provenance loop ran *before* the geometry guard, so a prereg-authoring error
("this source arm is one cell") was reported as a data-drift VOID ("the population, bank, exclusions
or model revision has DRIFTED"). Both refuse; the operator is sent to the wrong line. Hoisting F3's
guard puts the geometry check ahead of the provenance loop, so the diagnosis is now the specific one.

🔴 **And hoisting it immediately reproduced F7 one level up.** My new loop fired ahead of two
*narrower* prereg-authoring checks that had lived downstream, so *"you gave this head two criteria"*
came back as *"this arm is not a full band"*. Two existing tests failed on the message, not the
behaviour. Precedence is now centralised in the one loop — most specific diagnosis first — rather
than left to whichever check happens to run earliest.

> That is three times in two entries that moving a check **earlier** has been correct for safety and
> wrong for diagnosis. The guard and the *explanation* are separate things, and hoisting only the
> guard degrades the explanation every time.

### 6. Verification

```
105 tests pass (was 102). Five new, each verified to FAIL on the pre-fix code by `git stash`
  on the single source file and PASS after:
    a STRAY per_head entry cannot silently delete arms from the census      (F3)
    the EXCLUDED arms are named on stdout, not only in the JSON             (F4)
    the detectability resolver searches BOTH blocks, not just the first     (F6)
    + S-332's two gate-0 exit-code tests
346 guard tests and 9 deliverable guards pass at commit.
```

⚠ **One of the new tests was vacuous on its first run and I nearly kept it.** PR-015 spells the field
`COHERENT_OUTCOME_IF_NOTHING_CLEARS`; I popped only `COHERENT_OUTCOME_IF_NOTHING_CLEARS_IT`, so the
per-head block still held it and the resolver found it there **correctly, on precedence**. The test
failed with *and* without the fix — which is the honest signature of a bad test, and the only reason
I caught it is that I run the stash check in both directions rather than just confirming a pass.
A test that fails both ways proves exactly as little as one that passes both ways.

## S-334 — **the last open R30 finding is closed: two generations of one arm are now a GATE 0 FAILURE, not a benign "IN FLIGHT".** And the frozen read was put through an **argv gate before the read** rather than discovered to be wrong during it

### 1. R30-D CONCERN 2 — the relaunch shape the frozen read warns about, folded into a friendly message

The sweep's in-flight branch printed `.. IN FLIGHT -- 2 run dir(s), no DONE.json yet (neither passed
nor failed)` and continued, exit 0. **Two directories for one arm can never be legitimate.**

The reason it matters here specifically: `_cands` is built from the **name glob alone** —
`--require-slurm-job` filters inside `strict_run_dir`, *not* at this point — so two candidates means
two **generations** of the same arm sitting exactly where the reader looks. That is the S-103/S-104
relaunch shape the frozen read names in terms, and S-261's rule exists because the runner's
skip-if-complete **RESUMES** into an existing arm dir rather than re-running it. R30-D put the real
n-304 dir back beside a DONE-stripped live one and got the benign message and exit 0. The `>1` case
was escalated only when at least one candidate carried a `DONE.json` — i.e. only in the half where
`strict_run_dir` would have caught it anyway.

Now a FAILURE, naming both dirs and citing S-261. **This is the last open finding from R30.**

```
R30-A  F1 F2 F5 fixed S-332 | F3 F4 F6 F7 fixed S-333
R30-B  F1 F3 F4 fixed S-332 | F2 addressed as the FLOOR report, verdict unchanged (S-332 §4a)
R30-C  clean; its one CONCERN REVERSED by my own re-derivation (S-332 §2)
R30-D  CONCERN 1 fixed S-332 | CONCERN 2 fixed HERE | CONCERN 3 recorded, NOT fixed

### 2. The frozen read, put through an argv gate BEFORE it is executed

## S-337 — 🔴 **S-325's FROZEN CRITERION IS APPLIED AND IT RESOLVES: the source-side family is licensed as a REFUTATION TEST ONLY, on both codewords independently.** ⚠ **And it REVERSES the direction AM-40 recorded** — the protected control removes **LESS** band mass than the demonstrations (ρ ≈ 0.60–0.63), not the ~3.85× MORE that row quotes

### 1. The measurement

Jobs `924485` (basket) and `924486` (button), both COMPLETED `0:0` in 20:58 on n-301, provenance
`BLOB d0e4444c PORCELAIN clean`. 230 rows each — the exclusion list dropped 930 of 21 342, leaving
exactly the validation population the CSI arms use. **Zero infeasible strict draws; zero rows where
the d1 key count differs from the demo count** (56 vs 56 on the hand-checked row) — the count-match
that the whole comparison presupposes is verified, not assumed.

### 2. The criterion, quoted and applied — NOT paraphrased

```
m_d = demo-block mass ; m_c = the STRICT, PROTECTED nondemo_matched_d1 draw's mass
report the median ratio rho = m_c/m_d AND the per-row count of rows with m_d > m_c
  rho >= 1.0 and m_d > m_c on < 50%  ->  CONFIRMATORY source test
  rho <= 1.0 and m_d > m_c on > 50%  ->  REFUTATION test ONLY
  mixed / straddling                  ->  CANNOT ANSWER, nothing licensed
```

```
codeword   rho = median(m_c/m_d)    rows with m_d > m_c     branch A   branch B
basket           0.627889            219 of 230  (95.2%)      False      TRUE
button           0.595093            223 of 230  (97.0%)      False      TRUE

>>> FROZEN VERDICT, BOTH CODEWORDS INDEPENDENTLY:  REFUTATION TEST ONLY
```

Not straddling: both halves of branch B hold on both codewords, and branch A fails on both.

**Re-derived by me twice, by two methods.** Median by `statistics.median` and again by sorting the
230 ratios and taking the midpoint — identical to six decimals. Counts reconcile exactly
(219 + 11 = 230, 223 + 7 = 230). One row hand-checked end to end.

⚠ The criterion names **`d1` specifically**, so d1 is what it is applied to. d2 and d3 are reported
as robustness and **are not the quantity**: `d2` ρ = 0.843/0.809, `d3` ρ = 0.704/0.677, all four
below 1.0 with m_d > m_c on 80.4–98.3% of rows. Same direction, no branch change.

⚠ **Codewords are NOT pooled** (§3.3). Two independent measurements that agree; not an n of 460.

📌 **Supplementary, at the sprint's own statistical unit.** The criterion is frozen as a per-row
statistic (C-CONT-019's was a per-row count and §1 of S-325 says it must stay one), so per-row is
how it was applied. At the DOMAIN unit the answer is unanimous anyway: **23 of 23 domains have
ρ < 1 on both codewords**, domain-median-of-medians 0.656 (basket) and 0.583 (button).

### 3. 🔴 THE CORRECTION: AM-40's direction is REVERSED by the protection

AM-40 records *"demo **0.0630** vs ctrl **0.2421** = **3.85×**"* — the control removing nearly four
times MORE band mass than the demonstrations. That number comes from the field the producer itself
names **`ctrl_mass_band_REFERENCE_ONLY`**, and this run reproduces its family exactly:

```
ctrl_mass_band_REFERENCE_ONLY  median ratio vs m_d = 3.7426 (basket) / 3.6767 (button)
STRICT, PROTECTED d1 draw      median ratio vs m_d = 0.6279 (basket) / 0.5951 (button)
                                                      ^^^ a factor of ~6, and the OPPOSITE SIDE OF 1
```

**The unprotected pool draws from the query/generation span**, which carries most of the attention
at the readout position. Excluding it — which is what `query_span_positions` protection does, and
what every real arm does — does not shrink the control's mass a little. **It moves it from four
times the demo block to three fifths of it.** AM-40's *conclusion* (the source question is open, the
count-matched control is not mass-matched) survives intact; **its number pointed the wrong way**, and
a source-side family designed against 3.85× would have been designed against the wrong confound.

> A field named `_REFERENCE_ONLY` by its own author was doing load-bearing work in a claim-table
> row. The name was the warning and it was not heeded — including by me, in S-319, when I
> re-derived that very number and reported only that the predecessor's *magnitude* did not
> reproduce. **I checked the arithmetic of the wrong quantity.**

### 4. What is now LICENSED, and what is still not

From S-325's own table, with `m_c < m_d` established:

```
m_c < m_d, control NULL   ->  less attention removed, less damage.  CONFOUNDED -- says nothing.
m_c < m_d, control EQUAL  ->  LESS attention removed, SAME damage.  CLEAN REFUTATION of
                              source-specificity.
```

So: **a source-side family may be preregistered, and its prereg MUST state that it is licensed for
the REFUTATION reading only.** If the count-matched control comes out EQUAL to `demo_all`, that is a
clean refutation of source-specificity. If it comes out NULL, that outcome is **confounded and must
be reported as CANNOT ANSWER, not as support** — the null is exactly what less-mass-less-damage
predicts anyway.

⛔ **S-316's block is now PARTIALLY lifted — in one direction only.** It is not lifted for a
confirmatory source claim, and no such family may be designed.

```

## S-338 — **PR-CSI-019 is DESIGNED (not frozen): the source-side REFUTATION family S-337 licensed.** 📌 **Two reuse findings decide its shape — NO existing arm is admissible, and NO new measurement code is needed.** And a feasibility check says the design can actually answer

### 1. Reuse, checked before anything was designed

**(a) 29 `nondemo_matched` arm dirs already exist. NONE is admissible.** Every one differs from the
CSI population on at least one coordinate that changes what is being measured:

```
dcsbeh_* / dcss904_*   query_kinds=BEHAVIORAL (not semantic_one_word), scope=query_prefill_only,
                       380 rows, NO exclusion file -> pooled population
ts116m_sowk_*          query_kinds=semantic_one_word OK, but scope=query_last_k_rows,
                       670 rows, exclusion from runargs/dcs_succ, seed 20260909
THE CSI ARM            scope=target_surface_row_only, 230 rows,
                       exclude_button_bomb_sow_validation.txt, seed 20260913
```

The knockout **scope** is the decisive mismatch: `query_prefill_only` and `query_last_k_rows` edit
different positions than `target_surface_row_only`, so those arms answer a different question. A
new family is required.

**(b) 🔴 But NO NEW MEASUREMENT CODE IS NEEDED — the runner already supports the arm.** The CSI
intervention is specified as a string whose FIRST FIELD names the key set:

```
BF_KO   intervene = 'demo_all:attn_knockout:6-14:1.0'   scope = target_surface_row_only
```

and `score_behavior.py:1286` declares
`KNOCKOUT_ARMS = ("demo_all", "nondemo_random", "allpast") + NONDEMO_DRAW_ARMS`, where
`NONDEMO_DRAW_ARMS` is exactly `nondemo_matched_d{1,2,3}` and `nondemo_capped_d{1,2,3}`. Line 1830
passes `protected=protected`, so the draw is the **STRICT, PROTECTED** one — the draw S-325 built the
criterion around and S-337 measured. So the whole family is
`intervene = 'nondemo_matched_d1:attn_knockout:6-14:1.0'` and two siblings: **a prereg, a tag
registration and a frozen read, and not one line of new measurement code.**

### 2. THE DESIGN — PR-CSI-019, licensed for the REFUTATION reading ONLY

```
population   BUTTON validation, 230 rows, 23 DOMAINS (the unit), n_examples 4, cell C,
             readout semantic_one_word, exclude_button_bomb_sow_validation.txt, seed 20260913
arms (5)     SR_BASE   no intervention
             SR_KO     demo_all:attn_knockout:6-14:1.0
             SR_D1/2/3 nondemo_matched_d{1,2,3}:attn_knockout:6-14:1.0
             all at scope target_surface_row_only
endpoint     y_install, concept-free
per domain   d_X(dom) = y_X(dom) - y_BASE(dom)          <- what the census already computes as E
statistic    r = mean_dom(d_C) / mean_dom(d_KO), where d_C is the MEAN OF THE THREE DRAWS per
             domain; ci95 by bootstrap over DOMAINS, paired. Each draw ALSO reported separately.
```

**THE THREE PREREGISTERED BRANCHES, and only one of them is a claim:**

```
ci95(r) lower bound >= 0.75  ->  REFUTATION of source-specificity. The count-matched control does
                                 essentially the damage the demonstrations do.
ci95(r) upper bound <= 0.25  ->  CANNOT ANSWER. The control does far less damage -- which is
                                 EXACTLY what S-337 measured less removed mass predicts
                                 (rho = 0.595 on button). ⛔ THIS IS NOT SUPPORT FOR
                                 SOURCE-SPECIFICITY and must never be reported as any.
otherwise                    ->  CANNOT ANSWER.
```

⛔ **The asymmetry is the point and it is inherited, not chosen.** S-325's criterion, frozen before
the instrument ran, licenses the refutation reading ONLY; S-337 applied it and got
`REFUTATION TEST ONLY` on both codewords. A family that could "confirm" the demonstrations are the
source is **not available** and none is being designed. The 0.25 branch exists solely so that the
confounded outcome has a preregistered home and cannot be quietly written up as a positive.

⚠ **Why 0.75.** The control removes ρ ≈ 0.595 of the demo block's band mass (S-337, button). A
control delivering ≥ 75% of the damage from ~60% of the mass is doing *more* damage per unit of
removed attention than the demonstrations, which is hard to reconcile with the demonstrations being
a privileged source. **This is a stated rationale, not a model**: no linearity of damage in mass is
asserted anywhere, and the threshold is frozen before the data precisely so it cannot be tuned to
whatever r turns out to be.

**VOID CONDITION (the S-323/VOID-8 pattern).** `SR_KO` is the SAME intervention, population, scope
and seed as PR-CSI-018's `BF_KO`. It must reproduce `E = -0.28990714` within `1e-6`, or the
population/bank/revision has drifted and nothing in the family is readable. S-318 and S-335 both
demonstrated bit-identical reproduction across jobs and nodes, so this is a real check, not a hope.

### 3. Feasibility — asked BEFORE freezing, because a family that cannot answer must not be frozen

From PR-CSI-018's own landed arms (already read and published), bootstrapping over the 23 domains:

```
per-domain d_KO   mean -0.289907   SD 0.120497   SE 0.025125
                  ^^^ reproduces the census's E[BF_KO] = -0.28990714 by a path that reads RAW ROWS

true r     ci95 lo    ci95 hi    width     branch reached
  0.00     -0.1584    -0.0010    0.157     CONFOUNDED branch fires  (hi <= 0.25)
  0.50      0.4197     0.5697    0.150     CANNOT ANSWER
  0.75      0.7226     0.9174    0.195     CANNOT ANSWER (borderline, as a threshold should be)
  1.00      0.8728     1.0463    0.173     REFUTATION fires (lo >= 0.75)
```

**Both branches are reachable.** The KO effect is large (−0.29) and precisely estimated (SE 0.025,
8.7% relative), so a ratio is well determined at n = 23.

⚠ **The simulation's assumption, stated because it is the weak point:** the control's per-domain
delta was generated as `r · d_KO + noise` at half the KO per-domain SD, i.e. **correlated with
d_KO across domains**. That pairing is realistic — the same domains are hard or easy under both
arms — and it narrows the CI. If the control's effect were independent of the KO's, the interval
would be wider and the thresholds harder to reach. **This is a feasibility argument, not a power
guarantee, and the real MDE must be computed from the family's own arms at read time.**

## S-339 — 🔴 **REVIEW R31 KILLS PR-CSI-019 BEFORE IT REACHED A GPU. The comparison it proposed HAS ALREADY BEEN RUN — on TRAIN, with byte-identical `--intervene` strings — and it returns r ≈ 0.00 on 8 of 8 conditions.** The family is WITHDRAWN. 🔴 **Plus a real bug in MY OWN instrument (double-strided control seed) and two arithmetic/logic errors in MY OWN rationale**

### 1. The finding that decides it, RE-DERIVED BY ME

R31-C observed that S-338 §1(a) asked *"is any existing `nondemo_matched` arm admissible as the CSI
measurement?"*, answered **no** correctly, **and stopped there** — never asking the other question:
*what do those arms say about the PRIOR?* PART I §3.2 makes TRAIN exactly the split for that.

The `ts116m_sowk_*` families carry **byte-identical intervene strings** to the ones PR-CSI-019
proposed — `demo_all:attn_knockout:6-14:1.0` and `nondemo_matched_d{1,2,3}:attn_knockout:6-14:1.0`
— on the same banks and band, differing only in scope (`query_last_k_rows`), split (TRAIN, 67
domains) and seed. **I re-derived the whole table myself** with `w4.by_domain`, at the domain unit:

```

button   K09      67    -0.2860     0.0035    -0.0015    -0.0002    -0.0021
button   K10      67    -0.6428     0.0099     0.0037     0.0037    -0.0089

basket   K09      67    -0.3453     0.0092     0.0043     0.0024    -0.0153

basket   K11      67    -0.4585     0.0116     0.0062     0.0016    -0.0140

                                            min |d_KO|:              0.2643   (a factor of 21)
```

**It reproduces R31-C's table to the digit.** And the scope objection does not rescue it: TRAIN
button K08's `d_KO = -0.2643` is **0.912 of** PR-CSI-018's `target_surface_row_only`
`E[BF_KO] = -0.28990714`, so the two scopes deliver essentially the same demo-knockout, and there
is no reason to expect the control to behave differently under the CSI scope.

**PR-CSI-019's only claim-bearing branch was `ci95(r) lower >= 0.75`.** Against 24 draws clustered
at r ≈ 0, that branch has a prior indistinguishable from zero. The family would have bought
**~34 GPU-minutes of preregistered silence.** ⛔ **WITHDRAWN.**

> S-338's §1(a) reuse check was *correct and insufficient in the same breath*. "No existing arm is
> admissible as my measurement" and "no existing arm bears on my prior" are different questions, and
> I answered the first while writing an entry that read as though I had answered both. **The
> admissibility of old data and its evidential value are independent, and I conflated them.**

### 2. 🔴 A REAL BUG IN MY OWN INSTRUMENT — the control seed was strided TWICE (fixed, `c14a46eb`)

R31-B found it; I confirmed it from both call sites before accepting it. `retrieval_strength.py:164`
passed `nondemo_draw_seed(args.seed, _idx)` as `control_seed`, and `knockout_key_set` strides it
again (`score_behavior.py:1518`). Computed, not argued:

```
draw   a real arm draws with   the instrument used
 d1         28180690               36100467   <- which is a real arm's D2 seed
 d2         36100467               51940021   <- no arm uses this
 d3         44020244               67779575   <- no arm uses this
```

So the instrument sampled draws at strides **2, 4, 6** while arms use **1, 2, 3**: one of the three
was a genuine arm draw **wearing the wrong label**, and two belong to no arm at all.

⚠ **What this does and does not touch.** The draws are exchangeable, so S-337's ρ remains a valid
estimate of the **distribution's** removed mass, and the `REFUTATION TEST ONLY` verdict is not

result as `control_seed`) verified to FAIL on the pre-fix file, plus a test asserting the mis-seeded
d1 coincides with the arm's d2 — so the guard is protecting something real. **Both codewords are
re-running now as `924666` / `924667` to replace the numbers with the arms' actual draws.**

### 3. 🔴 TWO ERRORS IN MY OWN 0.75 RATIONALE, both verified by me

**(a) The rationale's premise is refuted by this sprint's own artefacts.** I wrote that ≥75% of the
damage from ~60% of the mass is "more damage per unit of removed attention", while claiming no
linearity was asserted. R31-C is right that the disclaimer cannot be true of that argument: it needs
**removed band mass to be a sufficient statistic for damage**. It is not, and the counter-example is
in the file S-337 read:

demo_mass_band (L6-14)  0.04523        demo_mass_late (L20-31)  0.08146   ->  late/band = 1.80x
```

The late band carries **1.8x the demo mass** and its control is **the ACCEPTED INERT one** (S-316
§3). Mass is not function — **S-337 §5 says exactly that, and S-338 then built a threshold on a

**(b) The rationale quotes the wrong ρ.** The frozen criterion names `d1` (ρ = 0.5951). My primary
statistic averaged d1/d2/d3, whose ρ are 0.5951 / 0.8094 / 0.6774 — **mean 0.6939**. So the sentence
should have read "75% of the damage from 69% of the mass", a ratio of 1.08, not 1.26. **The
rationale nearly evaporates on its own arithmetic, and the tested quantity was not the licensed one.**

### 4. R31-B's two BLOCKERs, which would have bitten even had the design been worth running

**F4 — the argv generator has no per-arm `intervene` axis, and the obvious workaround runs the

⚠ **Taken together F4 and F5 are worse than either alone: the family's only positive branch is

## S-340 — **R31-A completes REVIEW R31 and independently confirms the withdrawal.** 🔴 **My S-338 feasibility simulation assumed a cross-arm correlation of 0.83 — HIGHER THAN ANY OF THE 60 REAL ARMS ON THIS POPULATION.** "Both branches are reachable" was false: the only claim-bearing branch had an honest MDE of r ≈ 1.07

### 1. What R31-A confirms as SOUND, which matters for whatever replaces PR-CSI-019

Two design choices survive the review and should carry forward:

```
RATIO OF MEANS       the denominator never approaches zero. 200 000 domain-bootstrap resamples of
                     mean_dom(d_KO): ci95 [-0.342, -0.246]; closest approach to zero -0.2075
                     (71.6% of the point estimate); ZERO resamples with |mean| < 0.10; ZERO sign
                     flips. No Fieller pathology. Delta-method and percentile CIs agree to ~3 dp.
MEAN OF RATIOS       would be 100-6000x noisier with unbounded tails -- at true r = 0.50 its SD is
                     420.78 against ratio-of-means' 0.0675. Not hypothetical: in the real
                     ts116m_sowk_basket K10/K11 arms one domain's d_KO is +0.0003 and the
                     per-domain ratio there reaches 5.93.
```

R31-A also independently reproduced `mean_dom(d_KO) = -0.2899071449850837` — **matching the published
`E[BF_KO] = -0.28990714` to ten digits** by the same loader path the census uses. That is now the
third independent reproduction of that number (S-335, S-338 §3, here).

### 2. 🔴 THE BLOCKER, AND IT IS A CORRECTION TO A SENTENCE I PUBLISHED

S-338 §3 generated the control arm as `d_C = r·d_KO + N(0, 0.5·SD_KO)` and I flagged, in that
entry, that this "correlates d_C with d_KO across domains … and narrows the CI". **I named the
direction and published the conclusion anyway.** R31-A quantified it; I then verified the
quantification myself against PR-CSI-018's own 60 non-base arms:

```
cross-arm corr(d_arm, d_KO) across the 23 domains, 60 real arms:
    min -0.347    q1 0.063    MEDIAN 0.169    q3 0.301    max 0.800
    arms reaching 0.83:  0 of 60

what my generator implied:   corr = 0.832 at true r = 0.75
                             corr = 0.894 at true r = 1.00
```

**My simulation assumed a correlation higher than the maximum ever observed on this population.**
Removing it widens the CI roughly threefold and moves the 80%-power MDE:

```
                          S-338's assumption   corr = 0.17 (measured)   independent
CI width at r = 1.00            0.166                 0.454                0.494
80%-power MDE (REFUTATION)      r ~ 0.87              r ~ 1.05             r ~ 1.07
P(REFUTATION | true r = 1.00)   1.000                 0.678                0.578
```

So a control doing **exactly** the demonstrations' damage — S-325's own textbook
`control EQUAL -> CLEAN REFUTATION` case — would have fired the branch only **58-68%** of the time.

> ⚠ **S-338's "Both branches are reachable" was FALSE, and it was false in the half that mattered.**
> The CONFOUNDED branch is robustly reachable (P = 0.998 at r = 0) precisely *because at r = 0 the
> generator's correlation is zero anyway* — that branch never depended on the assumption. The
> REFUTATION branch depended on it entirely. I checked reachability with a generator whose defect
> was invisible in exactly the branch I used to argue the design was viable.
>
> **Stating an assumption is not bounding it.** S-338 named the correlation caveat in its own text
> and still drew the conclusion the caveat forbids. A flagged assumption that is never given a
> number is a disclaimer, not a control — and this one was not merely optimistic, it was outside
> the observed range.

### 3. 🔴 The second BLOCKER: averaging three draws tested a quantity the criterion never licensed

S-337 recorded in terms: *"The criterion names `d1` specifically, so d1 is what it is applied to.
d2 and d3 are reported as robustness and are not the quantity."* S-338's primary was
`mean(d1,d2,d3)`. R31-A shows the three draws are a **systematic arm-level effect, not row noise** —
`nondemo_draw_seed(control_seed, idx)` is one integer for the whole arm, and on the real ts116m
quartets the paired per-domain difference between draws is significantly non-zero in **8 of 8** cases
for d1−d2 and 8 of 8 for d1−d3.

**And for d2 the 0.75 rationale REVERSES.** Their mass ratios are ρ = 0.595 / 0.809 / 0.677. "75% of
the damage from 80.9% of the mass" is *less* damage per unit mass — which does not refute
source-specificity at all. A REFUTATION fired at r ≈ 0.78 on the mean-of-three could have had one
of its three components pointing the opposite way from the rationale justifying the threshold.
(S-339 §3(b) already recorded that the mean ρ is 0.6939, not the 0.595 I quoted; this is the same
error seen from the licence side rather than the arithmetic side.)

### 4. Two smaller ones, both mine

**My §1(a) contradicted my own §2.** I wrote *"29 `nondemo_matched` arm dirs already exist. NONE is
admissible"* — true of the **control** arms — while §2's VOID condition required `SR_KO` to be the
same intervention, population, scope and seed as PR-018's `BF_KO`. **Two of the five arms were exact
re-runs of arms that already exist and ARE admissible.** Defensible as a drift check (S-318/S-335
precedent); the framing was simply wrong. One good consequence: because `SR_KO` was pinned to
reproduce `BF_KO` to 1e-6, the denominator was a fixed 23-number vector, so R31-A's simulations are
exact for the family rather than approximate.

**Percentile-bootstrap coverage is off on the side that mattered.** One-sided P(lower bound > true r)
is **0.033–0.040** against a nominal 0.025 at n = 23 — inflated on the **lower** bound, which is the
exact side the only claim branch (`lo >= 0.75`) reads. Free fix for any successor: BCa or a
studentised bootstrap, or state the level as approximate.

### 5. NOT established

```
NOTHING WAS MEASURED THIS TICK. PR-CSI-019 was already WITHDRAWN in S-339; R31-A does not reopen
  it and nothing here revives it. These findings are recorded because they are CORRECTIONS to
  published sentences of mine and because they constrain whatever replaces the family.
S-339's withdrawal rested on the TRAIN prior (r ~ 0 on 8 of 8 conditions), which I re-derived

THE MASS RE-RUN 924666/924667 IS STILL RUNNING. AM-43's seed-provenance correction is NOT YET

NO REPLACEMENT FAMILY IS DESIGNED OR FROZEN. What carries forward is only: ratio-of-means over a

## S-341 — **the criterion application gets a COMMITTED script, and the artefact now RECORDS the draw seed that produced it.** 📌 S-339's bug was invisible in the artefact; that is the part worth fixing, not just the bug

### 1. Two provenance gaps of the same class, closed

**(a) S-337 applied the frozen criterion from a scratch file.** That criterion decides whether an
entire family may be preregistered — S-316 blocked one on it and S-337's verdict licensed a reading
— and a decision of that weight was reproducible only from a temporary path. Same class as S-302
(a witness taken inside a job) and S-331 (an instrument with no committed launcher).

`scripts/dcs_csi_apply_mass_criterion.py` is now that script. It quotes S-325 verbatim rather than
paraphrasing, applies the branches to **`d1` only** — the draw the criterion names — and prints d2/d3
under a heading that says they are **not the quantity**. It refuses outright if any row is infeasible
or if the d1 key count differs from the demo count, because a ratio of masses between sets of
different size is not what S-325 froze.

**Validated against the OLD artefacts, where the answer is already published:** it reproduces S-337
exactly — ρ = 0.595093, 223 of 230 rows (97.0%), `REFUTATION test ONLY`, d2 0.809371, d3 0.677382,
domain-median 0.582595, and the `ctrl_mass_band_REFERENCE_ONLY` contrast at 3.6767.

**(b) 🔴 The S-339 bug was INVISIBLE IN THE ARTEFACT.** The masses it produced looked entirely
reasonable; the only way to find the double stride was to read two call sites and notice the stride
was applied twice. Nothing in `retrieval.jsonl` said which seed produced its numbers. So
`retrieval_strength.py` now records `strict_protected_draw_seed` per row, and the criterion script
checks it against `nondemo_draw_seed(run_seed, idx)` and marks a mismatch.

> **This is R29/VOID-8 in a new place: a property nothing witnesses is a property nobody can check.**
> R29 found a VOID condition that existed only as prose; S-339 found a seed convention that existed
> only in code. Both were correct-looking from outside and both were wrong. The fix in each case was
> not to be more careful — it was to make the artefact carry the fact.

The index is parsed from the arm NAME, not from enumeration order: a seed keyed by position would be
right only while the dict happened to be sorted, which is the kind of incidental correctness S-339
was made of. Verified standalone: d1/d2/d3 → 28180690 / 36100467 / 44020244, matching the arms.

### 2. NOT established

```

## S-342 — 📌 **EXPLORATORY: the damage-vs-removed-mass curve is ALREADY MEASURABLE from arms on disk, and it kills the premise of my withdrawn threshold in a sharper way than R31 did.** Across scales damage is near-proportional to mass (log-log slope **0.96**) — but at FIXED scale, two heads with non-overlapping CIs invert it: **HD_20 removes 2.82× the mass of HD_11 and does 0.444× the damage**

### 1. Applying S-339's lesson prospectively, for once

R31-C proposed a new head-subset dose ladder to **measure** the curvature my withdrawn 0.75
threshold merely assumed. S-339's lesson — *ask what existing data says about the question before
designing anything to answer it* — says to check first. It is checkable, with no GPU at all:

```
PR-CSI-018 landed, on BUTTON validation:
   BF_KO         all demo keys, 32 heads, band 6-14   -> the FULL dose
   HD_<h> x 6    all 9 band layers of ONE head        -> a MID dose
   BF_H<h>_L<l>  x 54, ONE (layer, head) cell         -> a SMALL dose
and the published retrieval artefact records demo band mass per (layer, head), so the REMOVED MASS
of every one of those arms is computable offline.
```

### 2. What the existing arms say

```
total demo band mass, 32 heads x 9 band layers = 13.02604   (what BF_KO removes)

arm        mass share          |E|   |E| / mass share
HD_11           1.77%     0.016310         0.9213
HD_29           1.72%     0.009291         0.5392
HD_6            2.93%     0.005090         0.1736
HD_27           2.40%     0.002666         0.1109
HD_24           2.69%     0.002854         0.1061
HD_20           5.00%     0.007248         0.1450
BF_KO         100.00%     0.289907         0.2899

log-log fit |E| = k * (mass share)^p over the 7 resolvable arms:  p = 0.9626,  R^2 = 0.7345
```

**Across two orders of magnitude, damage is close to proportional to removed mass** (p ≈ 0.96).
A mass-proportional null would predict r = 0.595 for a control removing ρ = 0.595 of the mass; this
fit predicts 0.607. So at the aggregate level, my withdrawn threshold's premise was **not absurd** —
which is a more useful thing to know than "it was wrong".

### 3. 🔴 But at FIXED scale the premise fails outright, and the counterexample is clean

`|E| / mass share` ranges **0.1061 to 0.9213 across the six heads — a factor of 8.7** — at mass
shares that all sit between 1.7% and 5.0%. The sharpest pair:

```
HD_11   removes 1.77% of the demo band mass   |E| = 0.016310   ci95 [-0.022308, -0.011096]
HD_20   removes 5.00%                          |E| = 0.007248   ci95 [-0.009809, -0.004899]
                                               CIs DO NOT OVERLAP

HD_20 removes 2.82x MORE mass and does 0.444x the damage.
```

**Removed band mass is not a sufficient statistic for damage.** S-337 §5 asserted "mass is not
function" as a caution; this measures it, with non-overlapping intervals, on this sprint's own arms.
R31-C reached the same conclusion from the L20–31 band (1.80× the mass, inert); this is the
within-band, same-population version, and it is sharper because both arms are live and the
inversion is between them.

⚠ **What this implies for the count-matched control, and it is not comfort.** The control removes
~60% of the demo band mass **from entirely different positions** — the prompt prefix, since the
query span is protected. If position matters this much *among heads at fixed mass*, then the
control's damage is not predictable from its mass **at all**, in either direction. That is
consistent with TRAIN's r ≈ 0 (S-339) and it means the aggregate proportionality in §2 gives no
licence to predict a single control draw's effect. **The two findings do not conflict; they apply
at different scales, and my threshold used the aggregate one to license a claim about a single draw.**

### 4. NOT established — and this section is longer than the finding

```
⛔ EXPLORATORY. NOT PREREGISTERED. This is a premise check on a WITHDRAWN design, not a result,
   and it may not be cited as one.

## S-344 — 📌 **EXPLORATORY, and the most interesting thing on disk: THE WHOLE IS FIVE TIMES THE SUM OF ITS PARTS.** Twenty-one single-head knockouts on button validation sum to **20.1%** of what knocking out all heads does; the largest single head is **12.3%**; PR-CSI-018's six live heads are **6.7%**. ✅ And `BT_KO` reproduces `BF_KO` **BIT-IDENTICALLY** across two families

### 1. The question S-342 forced

S-342 measured that PR-CSI-018's six live heads carry 16.5% of the demo band mass and deliver 6.7%
of `BF_KO`'s damage, and asked where the other ~93% is. PR-CSI-013 ran whole-head arms on **21 of
the 32 button heads**, so a large part of the answer is already on disk.

### 2. The head budget, on button validation, 23 domains

```
head  19   -0.035568     head  25   -0.001830     head  26   +0.001493
head  11   -0.016310     head   0   +0.000078     head  27   +0.002666
head  20   -0.007248     head  15   +0.000424     head  31   +0.002747
head   6   -0.005090     head  21   +0.000566     head   1   +0.002875
head  16   -0.004787     head   5   +0.000879     head  28   +0.002894
head   2   -0.003522     head   7   +0.001295     head  29   +0.009291
head  10   -0.003168
head   3   -0.003117
head  24   -0.002854
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
SUM of all 21 single-head effects   -0.058286   =  20.1% of the full knockout
SUM of the 10 DAMAGING ones only    -0.083494   =  28.8%
LARGEST single head (19)            -0.035568   =  12.3%
PR-CSI-018's six live heads         -0.019545   =   6.7%
FULL KNOCKOUT (all demo keys)       -0.289907   = 100%
```

**No head carries the mechanism.** The largest is an eighth of it. Twenty-one of them together are a
fifth. Even counting only the ten that damage at all — discarding the eleven whose sign is positive
— the total is under 30%.

### 3. What that shape means, stated carefully

`|whole| >> |sum of parts|` is **super-additivity of the joint knockout**, and the standard reading
is **redundancy**: removing any one head barely hurts because the others still carry the signal;
removing all of them destroys it. That is the signature of a **distributed** mechanism, not a
localised one.

📌 **And it reframes PR-CSI-018 rather than threatening it.** S-335's result is that the basket-TRAIN
screen predicts, per head, **WHICH DEPTH** that head's contribution peaks at — 5 of 6, p = 0.012346,
across four layers. This entry says **no head is individually necessary**. Both can be true at once,
and together they are more interesting than either: **the depth structure is real, transferable and
predictable, while the head-level mechanism is redundant.** The screen locates *where in depth* a
head does its work; it does not identify a head that the model cannot do without.

### 4. ✅ A fifth independent reproduction, and the strongest form yet

```
PR-CSI-013  BT_KO  E = -0.2899071450   job 919531   (family: 21-head census)
PR-CSI-018  BF_KO  E = -0.2899071450   job 923972   (family: 6-head cell census)
|difference| = 0.000e+00   -- BIT-IDENTICAL, two jobs, two families, two weeks apart
```

S-318 demonstrated this on one arm across two nodes; S-335 on six heads at ~1e-9; this is exact
equality on the full knockout between two families that share nothing but the population.

### 5. NOT established

```
⛔ EXPLORATORY. NOT PREREGISTERED. A budget assembled from published arms, not a designed test.
⛔ ELEVEN OF THE 32 HEADS HAVE NO ARM in this family: 4, 8, 9, 12, 13, 14, 17, 18, 22, 23, 30.
   TWO of them (17 and 23) DO have button whole-head arms in PR-CSI-016, not folded in here.
   So "21 heads sum to 20.1%" is a statement about the 21, and the missing 11 could in principle
   carry the remainder -- though they would have to average ~4x the measured heads to do it.
⛔ SUMMING SINGLE-HEAD EFFECTS PRESUPPOSES A DECOMPOSITION THE DATA ITSELF QUESTIONS. The 20.1%
   figure is exactly the evidence that effects do NOT add; quoting it as "the heads explain 20%"
   would use an additive frame the number refutes.
⛔ ELEVEN OF THE 21 HEADS HAVE POSITIVE E, i.e. knockout RAISES installation. Most are small and
   consistent with zero; this entry does NOT claim any of them is a real opposing effect, and the
   "sum of damaging ones" line is offered as a bound, not as a subset result (no post-hoc
   sign-selected subset may be reported as a finding).
⛔ "REDUNDANCY" IS THE STANDARD READING OF THIS SHAPE, NOT A MEASUREMENT. Super-additivity is also
   consistent with a threshold/saturation response in which partial removal is simply insufficient.
   DISTINGUISHING THOSE REQUIRES A DOSE LADDER, which is exactly the gap S-342 identified between
   5% and 100% mass share -- and it is NOT run.
⛔ Nothing here licenses any source-side claim. S-316/S-325 stand; PR-CSI-019 stays WITHDRAWN.
NOTHING WAS MEASURED ON A GPU THIS TICK. The queue is EMPTY.

"The whole is five times the sum of its parts" rested on an INCOMPLETE AND BIASED head budget** — and PR-CSI-012 already contains a real joint-knockout ladder, never read as one, which says effects are **roughly ADDITIVE and CONCENTRATED**: eight screen-selected heads deliver **86.4%** of the full knockout, the bottom eight **5.5%**

### 1. The ladder that was already on disk

Checking the plumbing for a proposed dose-ladder family turned up something better: **PR-CSI-012 ran
ten MULTI-HEAD joint knockouts** on basket validation — `HD_TOPK` and `HD_BOTK` (8 heads each) and
eight `LOO_<h>` arms (top-8 minus one) — plus 32 single-head arms and `HD_KO`. That is a joint dose
ladder, and this sprint has never read it as one.

```
BASKET validation, 23 domains, HD_KO (all 32 heads) E = -0.226961

arm          heads            E    % of KO
HD_TOPK          8    -0.195984      86.4%     <- top 8 by the basket TRAIN screen
LOO_* mean       7    -0.170323      75.0%     <- top-8 minus one, mean of 8 arms
HD_BOTK          8    -0.012567       5.5%     <- bottom 8 by the same screen
SINGLE_* mean    1    -0.005211       2.3%     <- mean over all 32 single-head arms
HD_KO           32    -0.226961     100.0%

SUM of all 32 single-head effects  -0.166745  =  73.5% of KO
```

✅ **The selection is HELD OUT, so the concentration result is not circular.** `HD_TOPK`/`HD_BOTK`
were chosen from `w1_screen_train_basket_916132.json` — the basket **TRAIN** screen, 67 domains —
and measured on **validation**. The two sets are disjoint. **The screen picks the right eight heads:
86.4% versus 5.5%, a factor of 15.7.**

### 2. 🔴 And it REFUTES the reading I published in S-344

S-344 reported that 21 single-head knockouts on button sum to 20.1% of the full knockout, called
that "the whole is five times the sum of its parts", and read it as **super-additivity → redundancy
→ a distributed mechanism**. Measured directly here, super-additivity is **mild**:

```
HD_TOPK   sum of the 8 individual effects  -0.154386  = 68.0% of KO
          JOINT knockout of those heads    -0.195984  = 86.4% of KO
          super-additivity factor                        1.27x

HD_BOTK   sum of the 8 individual effects  -0.014523  =  6.4% of KO
          JOINT knockout of those heads    -0.012567  =  5.5% of KO
          super-additivity factor                        0.87x   <- SUB-additive
```

**1.27x, not 5x — and the bottom-8 are sub-additive.** On basket, where **all 32 heads have arms**,
the single-head effects sum to **73.5%** of the joint knockout. That is roughly additive, with mild
super-additivity concentrated in the heads that matter.

🔴 **Why S-344 got it wrong, and it is not a subtle reason.** Its budget covered **21 of 32** button
heads. The eleven with no arm are `4, 8, 9, 12, 13, 14, 17, 18, 22, 23, 30` — and **three of them

known to be large on the other codeword, and then I read the shortfall as a property of the
mechanism rather than of the sample.

> S-344 listed "eleven of 32 heads have no arm" in its own NOT-established block and still built the
> headline on the total. **Naming a gap in the caveats does not stop the headline from depending on
> it** — the same failure as S-338, where I flagged the correlation assumption and published the
> conclusion it forbids. Twice now, in four entries, a caveat I wrote myself was the thing that
> killed the claim it was attached to.

⛔ **WITHDRAWN from S-344:** "the whole is five times the sum of its parts", "no head carries the
mechanism" as a general statement, and the redundancy/distributed reading. **What SURVIVES from

### 1. What I should have done first, and did not

Before computing anything from PR-CSI-012's arms I should have read what the claim table already
says **about those same arms**. Doing it now:

```
D33   ALREADY PUBLISHES  E(HD_TOPK) = -0.195984 ci95 [-0.243068, -0.153491], E(HD_KO) = -0.226961

AM-30 HD_ALL32_07 = [1,2,4,7,8,14,18,22] shares EXACTLY ONE head with HD_TOPK and reaches 77.8%

**Re-derived by me, not taken from the row:** `HD_ALL32_07` E = **-0.152458 = 77.8% of `HD_TOPK`,

### 2. 🔴 The withdrawals

**(a) "Eight screen-selected heads deliver 86.4% of the full knockout" — WITHDRAWN as framed.**
It is AM-27's forbidden reading of `F = 0.8635` in different words. The number is real and
published (D33); the *interpretation* — that the eight implement 86.4% of the mechanism — is the one
AM-27 rules out, because both terms are net of backup-head compensation.

**(b) "The screen picks the RIGHT eight heads: 86.4% vs 5.5%, a factor of 15.7" — WITHDRAWN.**
`HD_BOTK` is the screen's **bottom** eight, i.e. the worst available 8-set, not a neutral
comparison. Against a set sharing **one** head with the candidate, the margin is 86.4% vs **67.2%**.
An essentially disjoint 8-set does most of the work. The honest statement is D32/D33's — the 8-set
is **sufficient and ranks 1 of 21** — with AM-30's bound attached, not a 15.7x contrast.

**(c) "Roughly ADDITIVE — 73.5% of the joint effect is recovered by summing singles" — WITHDRAWN,
and it VIOLATED AM-33's explicit prohibition.** AM-33 froze *"no singleton may be summed against
E(HD_KO)"*. S-345 summed thirty-two of them against exactly that. And the conclusion is
independently contradicted: AM-30 measured the dose-response in candidate-head count as weak and
**non-monotone**, which argues against additivity — while AM-33 measured that **4 of HD_TOPK's 8
heads carry no individually detectable load and 2 have marginals of the wrong sign.**

**What SURVIVES from S-345:** its withdrawal of S-344 (correct, and it stands — the button budget
was incomplete and biased), the head-by-head tables themselves, and "predictable from TRAIN", which
is D32/D33's published result and was never mine to claim.

### 3. 🔴 THE PROCESS FAILURE, which is the real content of this entry

```
S-338  flagged the correlation assumption in its own text, then published the conclusion it forbids
S-344  listed "11 of 32 heads unmeasured" in its own NOT-established block, then built the
       headline on the total
S-345  computed from PR-012's arms without reading the four claim-table rows about those arms,
       and violated one of them
```

Three entries, one mechanism. **I have been treating the raw arms as the source of truth and the
claim table as an output.** It is both — and where a family has already been read, the table is the
*prior* constraint on any new reading of it. Recomputing `E(HD_TOPK)` from `results.jsonl` felt like
independent verification; it was independent of the only thing that would have caught me.

> **A number re-derived from raw data is not thereby a claim that is safe to make.** The
> verification the standing rule demands — *never take a subagent's number on trust, re-derive it
> yourself* — protects against wrong ARITHMETIC. It does nothing against a wrong READING, and all
> three of these were readings. S-329 said this once already, from the other direction, and I did
> not carry it across.

**The fix, stated as a rule I will follow:** before any exploratory analysis of an already-read
family, grep the claim table for that family's arms and read every row that names them — FIRST,
before computing. If a row forbids a reading, that prohibition binds the new entry too. This costs
one grep and would have prevented all three.

head  6 -> L11 (5.96x)    head 13 -> L10 (1.08x)
head 24 -> L10 (4.70x)    head 28 -> L9  (1.40x)

multiset {L9, L10, L10, L11} -> THREE distinct layers -> 12 distinct assignments
permutation floor = 1/12 = 0.083333 > alpha = 0.05
                          -> NO OUTCOME CERTIFIES, not even a perfect 4 of 4.
```

Heads 13 and 24 collide on L10 and that alone kills it. **This is PR-CSI-019's failure mode exactly
— a family structurally unable to produce a claim — caught by the feasibility check R31-A taught me
to run, before a prereg existed rather than after.**

⛔ And it is not rescuable by dropping a head: K=3 with distinct layers gives 6 assignments, floor
0.167 — worse. Nor by reverting the gating to `binomial_only`: PR-CSI-018 moved to
`weakest_of_three` because S-317/S-319 established the permutation p as the load-bearing guard
against a shared-band-bias null, and **choosing the statistic that lets a family pass is the
selection this sprint exists to forbid.**

### 3. ✅ But the block is NOT structural — S-319's move, repeated

Over all 32 basket heads, applying the S-311 bar rule to PR-CSI-012's published single-head arms
(|E| >= 1.5·bar AND ci95 excluding 0), and excluding the four already cell-censused (2, 17, 19, 23 —
counting a known outcome as a fresh draw is the selection PR-CSI-018 excluded heads 17/19/23 for):

```

  6   -0.008475  0.003402   2.49      L11     5.96x

distinct assignments 10080   permutation floor 0.000099
binomial floor 2.323e-08   conditional floor 1.524e-04 (K_unique = 4)
WEAKEST FLOOR = 0.000152   -- 81x below PR-CSI-018's 0.012346
