### 4. Two composition facts that must be preregistered, not discovered later

**(a) Three of the eight had their predictions tested on BUTTON by PR-CSI-018 — and all three
MATCHED.** Heads 6 (L11), 11 (L8) and 27 (L10). The screen is the same frozen basket-TRAIN artefact
in both families, so testing them on basket validation is a **replication on a different
population**, not an independent draw. It is legitimate — the prior is "the screen is right", which
is the hypothesis — but it is a prior and it goes in the prereg by name.

**The family certifies WITHOUT them.** The five never-tested heads (4, 10, 13, 18, 21) predict
{L6, L10, L11, L12, L14} — all distinct, 120 assignments, permutation floor **0.008333**, weakest
floor 0.008333. So a preregistered PRIMARY on all eight and a preregistered SECONDARY on the five
fresh ones are BOTH able to certify, and the result would not rest on the replication heads.

**(b) Head 18 predicts L14 — the band-edge rival.** PR-CSI-018 excluded head 16 for exactly this.
That exclusion was right *there*, where a small set could be indistinguishable from top-of-band
bias; here the predictions span six distinct layers, so the spanning rule and the permutation p
both bite. ⛔ Excluding head 18 **after** seeing the composition would be post-hoc selection, so the
prereg must either include it or state a rule that excluded it before the composition was known.

```
  same limitation: it says NOTHING about heads that are null on basket. The firewall is that
  liveness is a WHOLE-HEAD property and the test is about WHICH CELL within a head -- admission is

  not bias which cell is the argmax. That firewall must be written into the prereg, not assumed.
THE |E|/bar FIGURES ARE EXPECTATIONS, NOT THE VERDICT. They come from PR-CSI-012's arms; the
  family would recompute admission from its OWN HD_<h> arms by the S-311 rule, as PR-CSI-018 did

THE FLOORS ARE FLOORS, NOT POWER. They say what a PERFECT result would yield. The MDE at the

  is that a feasibility claim computed at a convenient correlation is worthless.
R32 IS DUE BEFORE ANY OF THIS REACHES A GPU. Three reviews have now stopped a family there.
```

## S-348 — **the basket family's POWER, by EXACT ENUMERATION rather than a generator.** Type I at the null is **0.0004**, power at PR-CSI-018's observed match rate is **0.856**, and — unlike PR-CSI-018 — **losing its thinnest heads makes it STRONGER, not fatal**

### 1. Why this one can be computed honestly, and PR-CSI-019's could not

S-347 reported floors and said in its own NOT-established block that floors are not power. S-340 is
why that distinction is load-bearing: PR-CSI-019's feasibility was computed with a generator whose
assumed cross-arm correlation (0.83) **exceeded every one of 60 measured arms**, and the honest
number was three times worse.

**That failure cannot recur here, because this statistic is COMBINATORIAL.** The outcome is *which
heads match* — 2^8 = 256 patterns — so `P(certify)` is an exact sum over enumerated patterns. There
is no effect size, no variance, no correlation to assume and no generator to get wrong.

⚠ **One assumption remains and it is named:** heads are taken to match INDEPENDENTLY with
probability q. If matches are positively correlated across heads — plausible, since a screen that
is right about depth may be right in a correlated way — the spread is wider and these numbers are
**optimistic**. That is a real limitation and it is not disguised by the exactness of the enumeration.

### 2. The power curve

```
PRIMARY K=8  heads 4,6,10,11,13,18,21,27   6 distinct layers, 10080 assignments
   q        P(certify)   reading
   0.1111     0.0004     THE NULL -- type I is 0.0004 against alpha 0.05
   0.3300     0.0481
   0.5000     0.2305
   0.6700     0.5532
   0.8300     0.8563     PR-CSI-018's OBSERVED rate (5 of 6)
   1.0000     1.0000     D37's observed rate (4 of 4, descriptive)

SECONDARY K=5 (never-tested heads only)     5 distinct layers, 120 assignments
   0.1111     0.0007      0.8300     0.7973      1.0000     1.0000
```

**Type I is 0.0004 — the test does not come close to exhausting alpha.** That is the price of
gating on the WEAKEST of three, and it is a price worth naming: the family is conservative by
construction, so a null result from it is weak evidence against the screen, not strong.

⚠ **It is powered for a STRONG screen only.** At q = 0.33 — a screen three times better than chance
— power is **0.048**, i.e. nothing. This family can confirm a screen that works; it cannot
distinguish a mediocre screen from a useless one.

### 3. Exactly which outcomes certify, recorded BEFORE the read

```
matches m   subsets   certify   fraction
    5         56        28        0.50
    6         28        22        0.79
    7          8         8        1.00
    8          1         1        1.00
                                     (m <= 4 : NONE certify)
```

**The six-match patterns that FAIL all miss TWO of the four unique-layer heads** — 10 (L12),
11 (L8), 18 (L14), 21 (L6). So the structural rule, stated now:

> **At m = 6, the family certifies iff at most ONE of the four unique-layer heads is missed.**

That is the direct analogue of PR-CSI-018's "both unique heads must match" (S-332), and recording
it before the read is what stops a 6-of-8 result being argued about afterwards.

### 4. ✅ Admission robustness — and it runs the OPPOSITE way to PR-CSI-018

S-347 flagged heads 27 (|E|/bar 1.80) and 13 (1.84) as the thin ones, likeliest to fail admission.

```
admitted                 K  K_uniq  n_assign   P(certify | q = 0.83)
all                      8      4      10080          0.8563
minus 27                 7      5       2520          0.9578   <-- HIGHER
minus 13                 7      5       2520          0.9578   <-- HIGHER
minus 27 and 13          6      4        360          0.8522
minus 27, 13 and 18      5      3         60          0.7973
```

**Losing a thin head makes the family STRONGER**, because 13 and 27 are the two heads that collide
on L10 — dropping either breaks the tie and raises K_unique from 4 to 5. Power never falls below
0.797 in any scenario tested. PR-CSI-018 had the opposite exposure: losing either of its two
unique-layer heads was fatal (S-332). **This design's fragile heads are its redundant ones.**

### 5. NOT established

```
NOTHING IS DESIGNED, FROZEN OR LAUNCHED. No prereg file, no tag, no arm exists. S-167c binds.
THE INDEPENDENCE ASSUMPTION IS THE WEAK POINT and is not removable by enumeration. Correlated
  matches would widen the true spread; every number in 2 is optimistic under positive correlation.
q = 0.83 IS ESTIMATED FROM SIX HEADS (PR-CSI-018's 5 of 6). A rate estimated from n = 6 has a very
  wide interval, and the power curve is reported ACROSS q precisely so the answer does not rest on
  one estimate of it.
THE ADMISSION RATIOS ARE EXPECTATIONS from PR-CSI-012's arms, not this family's. The real family
  recomputes admission from its OWN HD_<h> arms; heads may be admitted or dropped differently.
TYPE I IS NOT A MEASUREMENT OF VALIDITY. 0.0004 is the rate under the stated independence model,
  not a guarantee; the reader's own refusals and GATE 0 are what protect the read.
NO CLAIM ABOUT THE SCREEN IS MADE OR STRENGTHENED HERE. This entry is arithmetic on a proposed
  decision rule and touches no data beyond the frozen predictions and PR-CSI-012's published arms.
R32 IS DUE BEFORE ANY GPU, and R31-C listed THIRTEEN degrees of freedom that a prereg must close.
```

### 6. State

```
queue EMPTY. The basket family now has floors (S-347) AND power (here), both computed before a
  prereg exists -- the order S-340 and R31-A said it should have been in all along.
NEXT  write the design against R31-C's thirteen-item list, then R32, then freeze, then launch.
```

### 1. Found by trying to build the thing, not by reading the code

S-347/S-348 established that a basket counterpart to PR-CSI-018 is viable and powered. Building its
prereg means giving each head a frozen prior measurement for VOID condition 8. PR-CSI-018's come
from PR-CSI-013 (button whole-head arms); a basket family's must come from **PR-CSI-012**.

They exist, and I verified every one of them:


All eight derivable, all eight with a ci95 excluding 0, and head 11 cross-checked against **my own

### 2. 🔴 But the census could not have read them

```python
_ref = (_hd or {}).get("pr013_whole_head_REFERENCE")     # scripts/dcs_csi_head_census.py
```

**The key name encodes the family.** A basket family declaring `pr012_whole_head_REFERENCE` would
have been **skipped** — loudly since S-341, which is the only reason this was survivable at all —
and the only way to be checked would have been to **misname PR-012's numbers as PR-013's**, putting
a false provenance claim inside the artefact that exists to establish provenance.

> **This is S-322 exactly, in a new place.** That entry's lesson was *"widening a single-family
> artefact means finding everything that ENCODES the family, not everything that NAMES it"* — the
> hardcoded `BC_H%s_L%02d` arm prefix. Here the family is encoded in a JSON key rather than a format
> string, and I found it only because I went to build the next family rather than to read the code.
> **The two previous times this pattern appeared (S-321/S-322, and here) it was invisible until
> something new had to use the path.**

### 3. The fix

`whole_head_REFERENCE` is now the family-neutral key. The PR-013 spelling is still honoured, because
a widening that breaks the artefacts it was widened from is not a widening — PR-CSI-018's published
prereg carries the old name and must keep working. **Declaring BOTH is a REFUSAL**: a head has one
provenance reference, and silent precedence between two spellings carrying two numbers is S-312's
both-criteria defect in a new costume.

```

   VOID 8 is reachable under the FAMILY-NEUTRAL key        FAILS without the fix
   declaring BOTH reference keys REFUSES                    FAILS without the fix
   the LEGACY pr013 key still works                         passes either way, BY DESIGN --
        it pins backward compatibility, which existed before and must survive
```

## S-351 — 🔴 **the INTERVENTION argmax marginal is NOT uniform, and PR-CSI-020 predicts the two modal layers for three of its eight heads.** A random screen predicting this multiset would match at **0.1625, not 1/9 = 0.1111** — so **the binomial p is ANTI-CONSERVATIVE here**, and the weakest-of-three gating is what saves it

### 1. The exposure, asked before the read rather than after

PR-CSI-020's permutation null is *"the prediction multiset is randomly assigned to heads"* — the
right null for *does the screen put the right layer on the right HEAD*. It says nothing about the
**marginal**. If some band layers are far likelier to be the intervention argmax for reasons
unrelated to the screen, a screen predicting those layers collects matches for free.

D37 computed this for the **SCREEN's** marginal (L14 is the screen argmax for only 6 of 32 heads,
modal L11 at 8/32) and used it to refute a band-edge rival. **The marginal of the INTERVENTION
argmax — the thing heads are actually scored on — has never been computed.** Every cell census this
sprint has published, 10 heads across both codewords:

```
L6   1  10.0%  #          L11  1  10.0%  #
L7   1  10.0%  #          L12  0   0.0%
L8   1  10.0%  #          L13  0   0.0%
L9   0   0.0%             L14  3  30.0%  ###
L10  3  30.0%  ###
                  6 of 9 band layers ever observed as an argmax; modal L10 at 30%
```

**L10 and L14 together take 60% of ten heads.** Uniform would be 11.1% each.

### 2. What that does to PR-CSI-020's multiset

```
head  4 -> L11   10.0%      head 13 -> L10   30.0%   <-- modal
head  6 -> L11   10.0%      head 18 -> L14   30.0%   <-- modal
head 10 -> L12    0.0%      head 21 -> L6    10.0%
head 11 -> L8    10.0%      head 27 -> L10   30.0%   <-- modal

mean match probability for a RANDOM screen predicting THESE layers: 0.1625
the binomial null assumes:                                          0.1111
                                                            -> 46% higher
```

**Three of the eight predictions land on the two modal layers.** So `P(Binom(K, 1/9) >= M)`
understates the null match rate for this particular multiset, and the binomial p is
**anti-conservative** here.

### 3. ✅ Why the family is nevertheless sound — and it is not luck

```
THE PERMUTATION p IS IMMUNE. It CONDITIONS on the multiset and asks only whether the right layer
  went to the right HEAD. A marginal that favours L10 and L14 helps every assignment equally, so
  it cancels. Same for the CONDITIONAL p, which runs over unique-layer heads.
THE GATING IS weakest_of_three, AND THE BINOMIAL IS ALWAYS THE SMALLEST. Its floor is 2.323e-08
  against the permutation's 9.921e-05 and the conditional's 1.524e-04. max() never selects it --
  verified on four synthetic reads in S-350, where the gate was `conditional` or `permutation`
  every time and never `binomial`.
```

**This is precisely why S-317/S-319 moved the gating off the binomial.** That change was made
because a shared band-edge bias could fake the binomial on PR-CSI-016's two-head set; the same
mechanism at a different scale is measured here, and the same guard handles it.

### 4. What this changes

The prereg's `MUST_NOT_BE_SAID_IF_POSITIVE` already forbids *"the binomial p alone"* on
methodological grounds. **It now has a MEASURED reason**: for this multiset the binomial's own null
is wrong by 46%, so quoting it would not merely be incomplete, it would be quantitatively
misleading. That prohibition is strengthened, never weakened, and no decision rule moves.

⚠ **The prereg is FROZEN at md5 `9fce4bda` and I have NOT amended it in this entry.** R32-A and
R32-B are reviewing that exact file right now; changing it under them would make their findings
reference a document that no longer exists. The amendment — recording this marginal and the
strengthened prohibition — will be folded into ONE re-freeze together with whatever R32 returns,
before any arm runs. **Nothing has been measured, so a pre-launch strengthening is not post-hoc;
PR-CSI-018's prereg was re-frozen twice on the same basis (c4483891 → 18994cf6 → 6790df3a).**

### 5. NOT established

```
⛔ EXPLORATORY, n = 10 HEADS. The marginal rests on ten censused heads across two codewords and
   three families. It is not a distribution, it is a tally, and L12 showing 0% does NOT mean L12
   cannot be an argmax -- head 10 is predicted there and may well land there.
⛔ IT DOES NOT MEAN THE SCREEN IS PICKING EASY LAYERS. The screen is frozen on TRAIN and its
   predictions were fixed before any of these censuses existed. That three of eight land on modal
   layers may be because the screen is RIGHT about where effects live -- which is the hypothesis --
   and this entry cannot distinguish those.
⛔ THE 0.1625 FIGURE IS NOT A CORRECTED NULL and must not be substituted into anything. It is a
   diagnostic showing the binomial's assumed 1/9 is not the empirical rate for this multiset.
   Constructing a "corrected binomial" after seeing the marginal would be exactly the post-hoc
   statistic-selection this sprint forbids.
⛔ NOTHING HERE LICENSES A CLAIM ABOUT D39. PR-CSI-018's read was gated on `conditional` at
   0.012346, not the binomial, so its verdict is untouched by this.
PR-CSI-020 IS NOT LAUNCHED. No tag, no frozen read, no arm. R32 has NOT reported.
NOTHING WAS MEASURED ON A GPU. The queue is EMPTY.
```

```
NEXT         collect R32 -> ONE re-freeze folding in its findings and 4 -> freeze the READ ->
             register the tag -> submit.
```

## S-352 — 🔴 **REVIEW R32: DO NOT LAUNCH. Four BLOCKERs, all confirmed by my own re-derivation.** The worst: **the freeze script and the reader compute DIFFERENT permutation statistics**, so the frozen prereg's power, type I and structural rule describe a test the reader does not implement — and **S-350's "two independent implementations agree" was wrong**

### 1. 🔴 BLOCKER — two statistics under one name (R32-A)

```
READER   scripts/dcs_csi_pr016_argmax_test.py:226-230
         obs = [r["argmax_layer"] for r in admitted]        <- the OBSERVED argmaxes
         p = |{q in perms(preds) : #(obs[i]==q[i]) >= M}| / |perms|

FREEZE   scripts/gates/dcs_csi_pr020_freeze.py  perm_p
         truth = the PREDICTION vector                       <- the predictions themselves
         p = |{a : #(a[i]==truth[i]) >= M}| / |distinct|
```

Re-derived by me on R32-A's own case — m = 6, heads 4 and 6 missing:

```
reader perm_p, over every landing of the two misses : 0.00009921 .. 0.00059524
freeze perm_p at M=6                                : 0.00267857      <- 4.5x to 27x larger
they agree EXACTLY at M = K                         : 0.0000992063 both
denominators are IDENTICAL (10080 each) -- the divergence is the COMPARISON TARGET, not the space
```

**The reader's is the correct one.** A permutation test must condition on the observed outcome; the
freeze version asks a different question and is systematically anti-conservative for the design
(it *over*-states p, so it *under*-states power and *under*-states what certifies).

**The consequence is not cosmetic.** The frozen prereg records
`STRUCTURAL_RULE_RECORDED_BEFORE_THE_READ: "m <= 4 never certifies"`. Under the reader:

```
matched = the four unique-layer heads {10, 11, 18, 21}, the other four land on L9
M=4  M_unique=4   binomial 0.00736988 | conditional 0.00015242 | permutation 0.00059524
weakest 0.00736988 <= 0.05, matched layers span 4   ->  READER VERDICT: PASS
```

**A 4-of-8 outcome would be published PASS by the reader while the frozen prereg says that outcome
cannot certify.** That is exactly the property S-348 claimed to buy — *"recording it before the read
is what stops a 6-of-8 result being argued about afterwards"* — and it is not there.

### 2. 🔴 What this says about S-350, in my own words

S-350 claimed: *"Two independent implementations of the same decision rule agree on all four."*
**That was wrong.** They are not the same rule. They agree exactly at M = K, which is case 1, and
in the other three cases they agreed on the **verdict** while differing on the **statistic** — S-350
even printed the reader's `permutation 0.000298` for a case my enumeration scored at 0.002679 and I
did not notice, because I was checking verdicts.

> **Agreement on verdicts is not agreement on statistics.** I built a cross-check that could only
> detect a disagreement large enough to flip a branch, then reported it as confirmation of the rule.
> This is the S-338/S-344 shape a third time: the check I ran was weaker than the claim I made from it.

## S-353 — 🔴 **R32-A's proposed replacement rule is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT — and the reason matters more than the rule: under the READER's statistic NO rule in (M, M_unique) alone can be exact.** S-348's "structural rule recorded before the read" is not merely wrong, it is **unavailable**

### 1. R32-A's arithmetic is right

```
P(Binom(4,1/9) >= 2) = 0.06355738   >  alpha  -> forces M_unique >= 3
P(Binom(4,1/9) >= 3) = 0.00502972   <= alpha
P(Binom(8,1/9) >= 2) = 0.22051131   >  alpha  -> forces M >= 3
P(Binom(8,1/9) >= 3) = 0.04999816   <= alpha  <- the knife edge: clears alpha by 1.8e-6
unique-layer heads {10, 11, 18, 21}, K_unique = 4
```

### 2. 🔴 But the rule it proposes is not the rule

Sampling every match pattern against 25 random landings of its misses — 6400 (pattern, landing)
combinations, 3021 distinct observation signatures:

```
CERTIFIES but the rule says no :  0   -> the rule is NECESSARY
rule says yes but does NOT cert : 34  -> the rule is NOT SUFFICIENT
                                         e.g. M=3, M_unique=3, weakest = 0.091071
```

**"M >= 3 AND M_unique >= 3" is a necessary condition, not a characterisation.** R32-A offered it as
*"the rule that is actually exact under the reader"*; it is not, and I would have frozen it into the
prereg had I taken the report on trust.

### 3. 📌 THE REASON, which is the real content of this entry

Under the reader's statistic the permutation p is computed against the **observed argmax vector**,
so it depends on **where the misses land** — not only on how many there are. Two outcomes with
identical `M` and identical `M_unique` can have different permutation p's, and therefore different
verdicts. The `M=3, M_unique=3` example above certifies for some landings and not others.

> **So no rule expressed in (M, M_unique) alone can be exact — not R32-A's, not any.** Under the
> *freeze* script's statistic such a rule existed, because there p depended only on M. **S-348's
> "structural rule recorded before the read" was not an insight about the design; it was an artefact
> of computing the wrong statistic.** Fixing the statistic does not repair that table, it *removes
> the kind of table it was*.

That is a strictly worse position for the sprint's own discipline: S-348 claimed the table was what
"stops a 6-of-8 result being argued about afterwards", and the honest replacement cannot offer the
same guarantee in the same form.

### 4. What the re-freeze must say instead

```
NECESSARY CONDITIONS, exact and frozen:   M >= 3 AND M_unique >= 3
                                          (verified: 0 certifications violate them)
SUFFICIENCY:                              additionally depends on the observed argmax vector
                                          through the permutation p; it CANNOT be reduced to a
                                          count, and the prereg must say so rather than imply a
                                          completeness it does not have
POWER:                                    by Monte Carlo under a NAMED model (each head matches
                                          with probability q, else lands uniformly on one of the
                                          other 8 layers), with N and seed FROZEN
```

⚠ **The power table is NOT re-derived yet.** The computation is expensive in the honest form — the
permutation tail must be evaluated per distinct observation signature (3021 of them appeared in a
6400-sample sweep, each costing a 10080-permutation pass), and two attempts timed out at 560 s.
S-348's numbers remain **WITHDRAWN**, not replaced.

### 5. NOT established

```
⛔ PR-CSI-020 STILL MUST NOT LAUNCH. Nothing from S-352's four BLOCKERs is fixed. The prereg at
   md5 9fce4bda remains defective and no re-freeze has been attempted.
⛔ THE POWER AND TYPE I ARE UNKNOWN under the correct statistic. S-348's 0.8563 / 0.0004 are
   withdrawn; R32-A's Monte Carlo figures (0.8631 / 0.00400) are ITS numbers, not mine, and the
   standing rule forbids taking them on trust -- I have not reproduced them.
⛔ THE NECESSARY CONDITION IS VERIFIED ON A SAMPLE, not proved. 6400 combinations with 25 landings
   per pattern is not exhaustive over landings (8^m per pattern). It is strong evidence of
   necessity and a DEMONSTRATION of non-sufficiency -- the 34 counterexamples are exhibited, and
   one counterexample is enough to refute sufficiency, which is the load-bearing direction.
⛔ D39 REMAINS UNAFFECTED (S-352 verified this: PR-018's permutation p is identical under both
   statistics and it gated on the conditional).
NOTHING WAS MEASURED ON A GPU. The queue is EMPTY.
```

```
NEXT         the re-freeze, with: the permutation definition written verbatim from the reader;
```

## S-354 — **the power under the CORRECT statistic, computed by me.** R32-A's figures reproduce to Monte-Carlo error. 🔴 **S-348's type I was wrong by 11x (0.0004 → 0.0041) and its low-q power by 2x** — but the headline power at the plausible rate is essentially unchanged

### 1. The computation, and why it is now cheap

S-352 withdrew S-348's power because it used the freeze script's statistic. R32-A supplied its own
figures; the standing rule forbids taking them on trust, so this reproduces them independently.

The honest computation had timed out twice at 560 s. Two facts make it cheap:

```
(1) positions sharing an observed layer are INTERCHANGEABLE, so the match-count distribution
    depends only on the SIGNATURE (a_6..a_14) -- how many positions carry each layer, not which;
(2) for one signature the whole distribution is a single vectorised comparison of the
    10080 x 8 permutation matrix against one row.
```

So the permutation tail caches on the signature and the Monte Carlo becomes dictionary lookups.
**11 995 distinct signatures** appeared across the six runs — which is exactly why the uncached
version could not finish.

### 2. The numbers

```
Monte Carlo N = 200 000, seed 20260924; a miss lands UNIFORMLY on one of the other 8 layers

q            MINE      R32-A      S-348 (WITHDRAWN, wrong statistic)
1/9       0.00410    0.00400     0.00037      <- type I: S-348 wrong by 11x
0.33      0.10151    0.1012      0.0481       <- low-q power: S-348 wrong by 2.1x
0.50      0.30545    0.3076      0.2305
0.67      0.59687    0.5976      0.5532
0.83      0.86237    0.8631      0.8563       <- PR-018's observed 5-of-6 rate
1.00      1.00000    --          1.0000
```

**Mine and R32-A's agree to within Monte-Carlo error at N = 200 000 (~0.002).** Independent
implementations, independent seeds, same answer — which is what S-350 claimed and did not have.

### 3. 🔴 What this corrects, and what it does not

```
TYPE I  0.0004 -> 0.0041.   Wrong by an order of magnitude. STILL far below alpha = 0.05, so
        S-348's qualitative reading holds -- the test is conservative and a NULL from it is weak
        evidence against the screen -- but the figure it quoted was not the test's.
LOW-q   at q = 0.33, power 0.048 -> 0.102.  S-348 warned "POWERED FOR A STRONG SCREEN ONLY: at
        q = 0.33 power is ~0.05". The true figure is twice that. The warning is still right in
        direction (0.10 is not usable power) but it OVERSTATED the limitation.
HEADLINE at q = 0.83, 0.8563 -> 0.86237. Essentially unchanged. The design's power at the only
        rate this sprint has ever observed is what S-348 said it was.
```

📌 **The errors ran in both directions.** The wrong statistic made the test look *more* conservative
than it is (type I) and *less* capable than it is (low-q power). That is worth stating because a
single-direction bias would have been easier to spot: I had no reason from the numbers alone to
suspect them.

### 4. NOT established

```
⛔ PR-CSI-020 STILL MUST NOT LAUNCH. This closes ONE of the four BLOCKERs' consequences -- the
   power block can now be written -- but fixes NONE of them. The prereg at md5 9fce4bda is
   unchanged and still defective: the census refuses it, the launcher has no tag for it, its
   permutation definition is still the wrong one, and VOID 5 is still enforced by nothing.
⛔ THIS IS POWER UNDER A NAMED MODEL, not a guarantee. The model is: each head matches with
   probability q INDEPENDENTLY, and a miss lands UNIFORMLY on one of the other eight layers.
   Both halves are assumptions. S-351 measured that the empirical argmax marginal is NOT uniform
   (L10 and L14 take 60% of ten heads), so the uniform-miss half is known to be wrong in detail;
   R32-A computed the type I under the empirical marginal at 0.00306, BELOW the uniform figure,
   so the direction is conservative -- but I have NOT reproduced that number and do not assert it.
⛔ THE q VALUES ARE NOT PREDICTIONS. 0.83 is PR-CSI-018's observed 5-of-6 on a DIFFERENT codeword;
   it is a reference point, not an expectation for basket.
⛔ S-353's finding stands: NO rule in (M, M_unique) alone characterises certification, so the
   prereg cannot carry the kind of outcome table S-348 wrote. Necessary conditions only.
NOTHING WAS MEASURED ON A GPU. The queue is EMPTY.
```

### 5. State


## S-356 — **the freeze SELF-TEST exists and runs at freeze time, and the READ is frozen.** 📌 The self-test is generic, calibrates clean on every prereg that has already been read, and **REFUSES a reconstruction of the first PR-CSI-020 freeze**

### 1. A prereg is a contract with its readers. Nothing was checking it was satisfiable

`scripts/gates/dcs_csi_prereg_selftest.py` AST-parses each reader for every `pr["KEY"]` **hard**
subscript — `.get()` is an author declaring a field optional and this file does not second-guess it
— and reports which of those keys a prereg lacks.

**Calibration, which is the part that makes it trustworthy:**

```
PR-CSI-016   1 absent: head_sets            <- read successfully
PR-CSI-018   1 absent: head_sets            <- read successfully
PR-CSI-020   1 absent: head_sets            <- same profile as the two that worked
PR-CSI-014   2 absent: head_sets, heads     <- single-head cell census
PR-CSI-015   2 absent: head_sets, PRIMARY   <- descriptive, no primary. Correct.
```

`head_sets` is the expected cell-family branch exemption. **PR-CSI-020 now has exactly the profile
of the two families that read successfully.**

**And the decisive test — the reconstructed first freeze**, with the two keys removed:

```
   CENSUS_DELIVERABLE            scripts/dcs_csi_head_census.py:882   <-- --require
   DOSE_IDENTITY_IS_BLIND_HERE   scripts/dcs_csi_head_census.py:885   <-- --require
REFUSING: 2 REQUIRED key(s) absent
   exit 1 on the defective prereg,  exit 0 on the current one
```

**It runs INSIDE the freeze script now**, not as a thing someone remembers. Re-emitting with it
wired in produces a byte-identical artefact — md5 still `d68eae71`.

⚠ **What it cannot do, stated in the file itself:** a static scan cannot tell which subscripts sit
behind a branch a family never takes, so absences are *reported* and must be judged; `--require`
promotes a named key to a hard failure. **It is a tripwire, not a proof.**

### 2. The READ is frozen

`runargs/dcs_csi_pr020_read.txt`, md5 `9fdbecea`. Validated by the S-334 argv gate: three commands,
**every flag declared by its script's own argparse, every input path resolving**. The single flagged
path is STEP 2's `--census` naming STEP 1's output, the documented false positive.

the helper's preconditions, the launcher's argument resolution, the landing zone. A family that

```
K_unique=3 : P(Binom(3,1/9) >= 2) = 0.03429355  <= alpha  -> forces M_unique >= 3   NO
```

## S-365 — the claim-table audit finds ONE live defect, and the withdrawn number turns out to be the smaller half of the problem (2026-09-24)

### 1. Why this tick was read-only

`925438` is on a GPU. S-362's VOID 11 disclosure says I do not edit `scripts/` or `src/` while a
family is in flight, so this tick did the one high-value thing that needs neither: audit the claim
table for numbers THIS SPRINT WITHDREW but never went back and corrected. The claim table is the
paper's backbone; a withdrawn number sitting in it is a defect whether or not anyone is reading.

### 2. What the audit checked, and what it found

Three withdrawn/suspect figures were grepped and each occurrence read in full.

```
"5 of 64"   1 occurrence, line 924, AM-42          -> LIVE DEFECT. Corrected below.
"23 of 23"  3 occurrences: line 27 (D12, unrelated), 935 (AM-43 original, A25),
                           947 (AM-43 corrected, A26)  -> LEGITIMATE. A26 explicitly
                           supersedes A25; that is append-only practice working as designed.
"20.1%"     1 occurrence, line 879, AM-36          -> NOT A DEFECT. See below.
```

**AM-36 needed no correction, and finding that out mattered more than it sounds.** AM-36 already
carries, verbatim, the caveat S-345 had to invent to withdraw S-344 — *"⚠ THIS IS A 21-OF-32
SUBSET, NOT A COMPLETE DECOMPOSITION ... the full 32-head sum is unknown and could be larger"* —
**and** the prohibition S-346 caught me violating: *"No singleton may be summed against `E(BT_KO)`
to attribute a share."* AM-36 predates S-344. So S-344 did not merely state a wrong number: it
**rediscovered a claim the table already held and stated it WORSE**, stripping a caveat that was
already written down. S-346 diagnosed the cause as not reading the claim table first. This is that
diagnosis confirmed against the artefact, and it is the more expensive failure of the two — a
sprint that re-derives what it already knows will eventually re-derive it badly.

### 3. AM-42 re-derived: the count is wrong, and the QUESTION was ill-posed

S-352 withdrew S-332's *"only 5 of 64 outcome patterns could certify, and every one requires BOTH
unique-layer heads"* because it was computed under the freeze script's permutation statistic rather
than the reader's, and left it PENDING RE-DERIVATION. Nobody re-derived it. AM-42 has been asserting
it since. Closed now, by exact enumeration — K=6, so all 2⁶ patterns and all 8^m miss-landings fit,
with no Monte Carlo:

```
patterns where SOME landing certifies : 15 of 64
patterns where EVERY landing certifies:  7 of 64
S-332's withdrawn figure               :  5 of 64   <- neither
```

**The count being wrong is the smaller finding. "N of 64 outcome PATTERNS certify" is not a
well-posed question under the reader's statistic.** In **8 of 64** cases the same match pattern
certifies under some landings of its misses and not others, because the reader's permutation p is
scored against the OBSERVED ARGMAX VECTOR — it depends on *where* the misses went, not only on how
many hit. A map indexed by pattern alone cannot have a single right answer. S-332 asked a question
whose form already assumed the freeze script's statistic, which is why fixing the statistic does
not produce a corrected number so much as dissolve the original one.

**The structural half survives, and is now a proof rather than an enumeration.** Every certifying
outcome requires BOTH unique-layer heads (11 and 29): if either is unmatched then `M_unique ≤ 1`,
so `p_cond = 1 − (8/9)² = 17/81 = 0.209877 > alpha` and the conditional alone kills it, whatever
the other four heads do. That holds by arithmetic, not by search.

### 4. What this does to D39 — nothing, except strengthen it

D39's PASS and every number in it stand; S-352 already scoped the withdrawal to the accompanying
pre-read map, and this tick confirms that scope was right. The enumerator, written from the
reader's source and not from D39, independently reproduces D39's PASS on the real outcome.

**New result:** PR-CSI-018's observed pattern (M=5, matched {6,11,24,27,29}, head 20 the only miss)
certifies under **all 8** landings that miss could have taken. The PASS did not depend on head 20
happening to land on L14 — so no post-hoc argument about where the miss went is available to
either side.

### 5. Re-derived, not trusted

Per the standing rule, the load-bearing figures were checked by hand, independently of the script:

```
M=6  binomial (1/9)^6 = 1.88e-6 | conditional (1/9)^2 = 0.012346
     permutation 1/180 = 0.005556 over 6!/(2!2!) = 180 distinct assignments
     weakest = 0.012346 <= 0.05  -> certifies                                    CONFIRMED
M=3 matched {6,11,29}  binomial 0.021167, conditional 0.012346 -- BOTH clear alpha,
     so the verdict rests entirely on the permutation and is landing-dependent    CONFIRMED
```

A defect in my own enumerator was found and fixed mid-tick: it skipped the spanning check at M=0.
It changed no count (at M=0 the binomial is 1.0 and refuses anyway), but it was a branch of the
reader I had not actually reproduced, and "it happens not to matter" is not the same as "it is
right". Fixed, re-run, counts identical.

### 6. What was NOT established

```
- NOT established: any design map for PR-CSI-020. These numbers are specific to PR-CSI-018's
  multiset [L11,L8,L11,L10,L10,L6]. PR-CSI-020 has 82 arms and a larger head set, and its map
  has NOT been computed. It MUST NOT be assumed to resemble this one.
- NOT established: that no OTHER claim-table row carries a withdrawn number. Three figures were

- NOT re-derived: whether S-332's "5" is reproducible under the freeze statistic. I did not
```

## S-366 — the PR-CSI-020 design map, FROZEN BEFORE THE READ. Two structural hazards found: the family CANNOT certify at K ≤ 3 whatever the data, and the binomial at M=3 clears alpha by 1.8 PARTS IN A MILLION (2026-09-24)

### 1. Why now, and why this is the expiring branch

`925438` is still on a GPU (39 of 82 when this was written), so under VOID 11 nothing in `scripts/`
or `src/` may be touched. But a *pre-read* design map is the one piece of work that becomes
worthless the moment the read happens — its whole value is that it was written down first. S-365
recorded that this map did not exist and must not be assumed to resemble PR-CSI-018's. It exists now.

Computed from `scripts/dcs_csi_pr016_argmax_test.py:307-331` — the reader's PASS branch, which needs
`gate <= alpha` **and** `spanning_ok` — **not** from the freeze script. That exact confusion is what
S-352 had to withdraw and what S-365 had to correct in AM-42. The enumerator is
`pr020_design_map.py`, md5 `ad0fafa0`, in the session scratchpad (it may not enter `scripts/` while
the family is in flight).

### 2. The prereg's own frozen floors, re-derived rather than trusted

```
binomial     prereg 2.323057312542e-08   mine 2.323057312542e-08   MATCH   (1/9)^8
conditional  prereg 1.524157902759e-04   mine 1.524157902759e-04   MATCH   (1/9)^4
permutation  prereg 9.920634920635e-05   mine 9.920634920635e-05   MATCH   1/10080
distinct assignments at K=8: 10080 = 8!/(2!2!)              unique-layer heads: [10, 11, 18, 21]
```

Predictions: `4→L11, 6→L11, 10→L12, 11→L8, 13→L10, 18→L14, 21→L6, 27→L10`. Two shared pairs
(4&6 on L11, 13&27 on L10), four singletons.

The memo this calculation rests on — that the match distribution depends on the observed vector only
through its per-layer counts, because positions demanding the same value are exchangeable — was
**checked, not assumed**: 12 random observed vectors against re-shuffles of themselves, 0 of 12
histograms differed.

### 3. HAZARD 1 — at K ≤ 3 the family cannot certify, and at K = 3,4,5 it can publish an uninformative FAIL

```
 K  #sets  best floor   worst floor   admitted sets that CAN certify
 1      8  1.00000000   1.00000000     0 of 8
 2     28  0.50000000   1.00000000     0 of 28
 3     56  0.16666667   0.33333333     0 of 56     <- NONE
 4     70  0.04166667   1.00000000    41 of 70     <- 29 cannot
 5     56  0.00833333   0.11111111    52 of 56     <- 4 cannot
 6     28  0.00138889   0.01234568    28 of 28
 7      8  0.00039683   0.00137174     8 of 8
 8      1  0.00015242   0.00015242     1 of 1
```

**No admitted set of size ≤ 3 can certify at any data.** The reader's S-332 guard converts `K < 3`
into CANNOT ANSWER — but the prereg defines FAILURE at `K >= 3`, so an admitted set of **exactly 3**,
or one of the **29 of 70** unwinnable 4-sets, or **4 of 56** unwinnable 5-sets, would publish
**FAIL** — with the reader's ⛔ STRUCTURALLY UNWINNABLE annotation attached, but FAIL nonetheless.
That is the S-317 shape this family was built to escape, surviving in a narrow band the S-332 fix
does not cover. It is not a reader bug — the reader is obeying the prereg — but **the prereg's
`FAILURE` threshold and the design's floor do not meet at the same K**, and that is knowable now.

⚠ The probability of landing there is NOT estimable in advance: admission is the power gate's
decision on data that does not exist yet. What is established is the structure, not its likelihood.

### 4. HAZARD 2 — the M=3 binomial clears alpha by 1.8 parts in a million

```
binomial  M=3, K=8  =  717419/14348907  =  0.04999816362319444
alpha - p                                =  0.00000183637680556
```

Exact as a rational, not a float artefact: `1 - (8^8 + 8*8^7 + 28*8^6)/9^8`. **The design's weakest
admissible outcome sits 1.8e-06 below alpha.** Nothing is wrong — 0.049998 ≤ 0.05 and the prereg is
frozen — but any of the following would flip M=3 from certifying to blocking: a band of 10 layers
instead of 9, K=9 instead of 8, or alpha stated as 0.0499. This is recorded so that if the read
lands on M=3 nobody discovers the margin afterwards and nobody is tempted to renegotiate the band.

### 5. The map at K=8

```
ALWAYS certifies (every landing of its misses) :  59 of 256
SOMETIMES (the landing decides)               :  21 of 256
NEVER                                         : 176 of 256
  -- all 176 die to the binomial/conditional/spanning ALONE; the landing is irrelevant to them.
```

**21 of 256 patterns do not determine their own verdict** — the same set of matching heads certifies
under some landings of the misses and not others, because `p_perm` is scored against the observed
argmax vector. This is S-365's lesson applied prospectively rather than discovered afterwards: the
question "how many PATTERNS certify" has no single answer, and the map is reported as a
three-way classification instead of a count.

### 6. The necessary conditions, as arithmetic rather than search

Both gating statistics that do **not** depend on where misses land:

```
binomial  M=0 1.000000  M=1 0.610256  M=2 0.220511  BLOCK    M>=3 0.049998  ok
cond     Mu=0 1.000000 Mu=1 0.375705 Mu=2 0.063557  BLOCK   Mu>=3 0.005030  ok
```

**Every certifying outcome at K=8 requires M ≥ 3 of 8 AND M_unique ≥ 3 of the four unique-layer
heads [10, 11, 18, 21].** Hand-verified independently of the enumerator:
`P(Binom(4,1/9) >= 2) = 1 - (8/9)^4 - 4(1/9)(8/9)^3 = 0.063557 > alpha`, so two unique heads are not
enough whatever the other six do. The screen must get **three of {10, 11, 18, 21}** right or the
conditional alone ends it.

### 7. What was NOT established

```
- NOT established: any probability. This map says what CAN happen, never what is LIKELY to.
  The power table (S-354) is a separate object and is not combined with this one.
- NOT established: the map for K != 8. Section 3 gives the FLOOR for every admitted set, which
  settles "can it certify at all"; the full ALWAYS/SOMETIMES/NEVER classification was computed
  at K=8 only.
- NOT established: that the family will reach K=8. Admission is the power gate's call on data
  that does not exist yet.
- NOT a defect in the reader. Section 3's hazard is the PREREG's FAILURE threshold sitting below
  the design's floor. The reader obeys the prereg and annotates the outcome correctly.
- NOT fixable this tick: VOID 11. Nothing in scripts/ or src/ was touched, and nothing should be
  -- the prereg is FROZEN and a frozen prereg is not amended because its map is unflattering.
```

S-366 §6 presented `M >= 3 AND M_unique >= 3 of {10,11,18,21}` as "the necessary conditions, as
arithmetic rather than search". Both numbers that force them — `P(Binom(8,1/9)>=2) = 0.22051131`

This is the S-333-era lesson recurring: *a verification pattern that silently misses its target
reports "nothing found" in exactly the same voice as "nothing wrong"*. The line-anchored flag regex
did it, and in this same tick a third instance appeared — see section 5. The defence that worked
here was refusing to accept a negative result without first confirming the field's absence
independently (`grep -ril attn` on one arm dir, which found it immediately).

## S-369 — 🔴 **R34 FOUND TWO BLOCKERS IN THE READ PATH, BOTH CONFIRMED BY MY OWN READING OF THE SOURCE.** GATE 0 does not enforce the S-334 duplicate rule the frozen read promises BY NAME, and the primary reader publishes the gating p-value on the one branch whose stated contract is "M and p are NOT computed". ### 1. How this review was run

Four subagents (R34-A GATE 0, R34-B census/VOID 8, R34-C primary reader, R34-D prereg↔reader
contract), each barred from opening any `rows.jsonl`, effect, bar or argmax of the live family —
the read must stay blind. **Every load-bearing claim below was re-derived by me from the source
before being accepted**, per the standing rule. R34-B has not yet reported.

⚠ **Timing is the whole point of this entry.** Both blockers are in code that runs AFTER the GPU.
They are recorded now, with their patches written out, while `925438` is still producing arms and
**no number from this family has been seen by anyone**. A reader patched after the data is in hand
is indefensible; a reader patched to a specification frozen before the data exists is what review
is for. Neither fix touches the statistic, the gating rule, or any threshold.

### 2. 🔴 BLOCKER 1 — GATE 0 passes an arm with TWO run dirs, and exits 0

`scripts/gates/dcs_csi_pr012_gate0_sweep.py`. `_cands` is built from the NAME GLOB at `:191-192`.
The duplicate check `if len(_cands) > 1` sits at `:227`, nested inside `if not _done:` (`:213`),
which is itself inside `except` (`:196`). **On the success path — `strict_run_dir` RETURNS — control
goes straight to `landed += 1` at `:244` and `_cands` is never looked at again.**

`strict_run_dir` refuses only when the number of dirs that are complete AND survive its filters is
not exactly 1. So a second generation rejected for ANY reason — no DONE.json, wrong row count, bad
`DONE.status`, or a `slurm_job_id` outside `--require-slurm-job` — leaves exactly one survivor and
is silently dropped. **`--require-slurm-job` actively HIDES the duplicate it is supposed to coexist
with.**

This contradicts the frozen read in terms, `runargs/dcs_csi_pr020_read.txt:192-194`:

> *"If a relaunch happens, the earlier generation's arm dirs must be QUARANTINED rather than
> filtered at read time (S-261), and GATE 0 will FAIL on two run dirs for one arm (S-334)."*

It will not. And this is the R30-D/S-334 defect **one branch over** — the same fix, applied to the
failure path only, left the success path untouched. That is the recurring shape of this sprint:
*proving something in one regime and freezing it everywhere.*

⚠ **Reachability is not hypothetical.** The partition is `killable` with a 12 h wall, and
`scripts/dcs_csi_arm_runner.py:87-92` re-runs any arm that is not already exactly-one-complete —
a re-run writes a NEW timestamped dir. A preemption mid-arm produces this state directly.

```
PATCH, SPECIFIED BEFORE ANY NUMBER EXISTS:
  hoist the duplicate check out of the `except`. Immediately after `_cands` is built at :192,
  and BEFORE the `try`, fail whenever len(_cands) > 1 -- regardless of DONE.json and regardless
  of what strict_run_dir returns. The existing in-except branch then becomes unreachable for
  len>1 and its message is kept for the no-DONE case.
```

### 3. 🔴 BLOCKER 2 — on a TIE, the reader publishes the gating p-value

`scripts/dcs_csi_pr016_argmax_test.py`. `_gate_name` / `_gate_p` are computed at `:231-236`,
BEFORE the tie branch nulls the endpoint at `:278` (`M, p, span, spanning_ok = None, None, None,

`p_conditional` and `p_permutation` at `:355` ARE correctly gated on `M is None`. `gating_p` is not.

undetermined, not a miss"*, **the JSON publishes the single most quotable number in the file — the p
the claim must be stated with — computed under a tie-as-miss scoring rule the prereg never froze.**
`ROBUSTNESS.M_unique` leaks on the same path and is a scoring count, not an observation.

```
PATCH, SPECIFIED BEFORE ANY NUMBER EXISTS:
  null `gating_p`, `gating_p_name` and `ROBUSTNESS.M_unique` when `M is None`, exactly as
  `p_conditional` and `p_permutation` already are. Three keys, no statistic touched.
```

## S-370 — R34-B closes the review: no blocker in the census, but **VOID CONDITION 8 pins only the MEAN**, and the frozen read draws a stronger conclusion from it than the code supports. Two reviewers independently found the preregistered bootstrap is enforced nowhere, and the TEST-leak refusal is vacuous on this prereg (2026-09-24)

### 1. 📌 The finding that matters — VOID 8 closes one channel of three

`scripts/dcs_csi_head_census.py:765`. The entire comparison is:

```python
_d = abs(E[_src] - float(_ref["E"]))
```

`E[_src]` is a **mean**. Admission turns on three quantities derived from that same arm —
`E`, `bar(h) = 1.96·SD(per-domain delta)/√23`, and the bootstrap `ci95`. **VOID 8 constrains only
the first.** Verified by grep: the only fields any script reads out of `whole_head_REFERENCE` are
`E` and `void_tolerance`. **Every one of the eight reference blocks already carries a frozen
`ci95` that no reader ever opens**, and `pr016` never touches `whole_head_REFERENCE` at all. Two
per-domain delta vectors with the same mean and different spread are indistinguishable to VOID 8.

**The frozen read overstates what this buys.** `runargs/dcs_csi_pr020_read.txt:162-163`:

> *"⚠ Given VOID 8 pins each HD_<h> to PR-012's value within 1e-6, admission is expected to be
> effectively DETERMINISTIC."*

VOID 8 pins `E`. It does not pin `bar(h)` and does not pin `ci95`, and admission is a conjunction
over all three. The sensitivity, computed from the prereg's own `ADMISSION.EXPECTED` figures
against `ratio = 1.5`:

```
head 13  |E|/bar 1.84  ->  bar may grow +22.7% with E UNMOVED before admission fails
head 27  |E|/bar 1.80  ->  bar may grow +20.0%
head  4  1.92 -> +28.0%   head 11  1.92 -> +28.0%   head 21  2.07 -> +38.0%
head 10  2.13 -> +42.0%   head 18  2.33 -> +55.3%   head  6  2.49 -> +66.0%
```

### 2. ⚠ But the direction of the exposure is the OPPOSITE of the harm VOID 8 was written against

The census's own comment says VOID 8 exists because *"a drifted HD_<h> silently moves that head's
BAR … the head is quietly DROPPED by ADMISSION … shrinking K and the permutation space."* For
**these two specific heads that is backwards**, and the prereg already records why, under
`ADMISSION.✅ LOSING_A_THIN_HEAD_MAKES_THIS_FAMILY_STRONGER`:

> *"heads 13 and 27 are the two that COLLIDE on L10. Dropping either breaks the tie and raises
> K_unique from 4 to 5, raising P(certify | q=0.83) from 0.8624 to ~0.9612."*

The two thinnest heads are exactly the two whose loss *raises* certification power. So the unpinned
SD channel, on the heads where it is widest, does not shrink the permutation space — it enlarges the
unique-layer set. **This does not make the gap acceptable**: a head dropped for a spurious reason
while its `E` is pinned to 1e-6 is a provenance failure whatever it does to power. But it is not the
compounding harm, and saying so required reading the prereg rather than accepting the framing.

**And the operational protection is already frozen.** The same read-file paragraph continues:
*"A head that fails it when PR-CSI-012 says it should not is ITSELF A FINDING and must be reported
as one, not quietly dropped."* The read file's INFERENCE is overstated; its INSTRUCTION covers the
case. Nothing needs amending — VOID 12 would permit it and I am again declining.

### 3. Confirmed by two independent reviewers — the preregistered bootstrap is enforced NOWHERE

R34-B (finding 4) and R34-C (note 8) found this separately. Verified by grep across `scripts/` and
`src/`: **`ESTIMATOR_AND_RESAMPLER` is WRITTEN by `dcs_csi_pr020_freeze.py:484` and READ by nothing.**
No script compares `--B / --seed / --ci` against the prereg's frozen `{B: 10000, seed: 20260922,
ci: 0.95}`. `ci` is load-bearing: it feeds `ci95_excludes_0`, hence ADMISSION, hence K.

The read file at `:84-86` presents this as a tightening — *"FROZEN HERE rather than left to the CLI
defaults it used to be"* — but the census's argparse defaults are ALREADY `10000 / 20260922 / 0.95`,
so writing them on the command line changes nothing that runs. **The freeze is real only in the
prereg, and no code reads it there.** R29/R32-B's "prose that reads as automatic" shape, on a
load-bearing field, found only because two reviewers were pointed at the same file from different
angles. ⚠ The near-miss is one keystroke: the sibling reader `dcs_csi_head_analyze.py:138` defaults
to seed `20260921`.

### 4. A check whose PASS is consistent with reading nothing

`dcs_csi_head_census.py:267-270` refuses when a TEST domain appears, reading
`pr["population"].get("test_domain_ids")`. **This prereg's `population` holds
`validation_domains`, `validation_expect_n`, `test_domains`, `test_note` — and no
`test_domain_ids`** (verified). So `test_dom` is empty, `leaked` is always `[]`, and the refusal
cannot fire. That is the file's own R20-6 rule — *"any check whose PASS is consistent with reading
NOTHING is not a check"* — violated at a site the file never revisited. The message also cites
"VOID 5", which in this prereg is the screen artefact's md5, so an operator hitting it is sent to
the wrong condition.

⛔ **TEST is not endangered by this.** The split guard (`pr["split"] != a.split` → exit) forces
`validation`, and the read passes `--split validation`. The check is vacuous, not the protection.

```
THE BAR IS THE S-311 RULE EXACTLY. statistics.stdev IS ddof=1 -- four bars reproduced against a
```

## S-371 — both S-369 patches BUILT AND VERIFIED END TO END on isolated copies, while the family is still in flight. The tie leak is reproduced on the REAL reader and closed; GATE 0 now fails the duplicate it used to pass. The repo is still untouched (2026-09-24)

### 1. What this tick did and why it is not a VOID 11 violation

`925438` is still running (74 of 82), so `scripts/` and `src/` remain frozen. The patches specified
in S-369 were therefore built and tested **entirely outside the repo**: a mirror tree at
`scratchpad/mirror/` holding a COPY of `scripts/`, with its own empty
`outputs/boombness/score_behavior/`. Every reader derives `REPO` from `os.path.abspath(__file__)`,
so the mirror's sweep resolves `SCORE_DIR` to the mirror's own fixture directory. **The live
family's output tree was never written to, and never globbed by the tests.**
`git status --porcelain scripts/ src/` is EMPTY.

The patcher is `scratchpad/apply_s369_patches.py`. It is anchor-matched and **refuses unless each
anchor matches EXACTLY once**, so if either file has moved under it the patch will not apply
silently — it will stop and say the file changed. It is idempotent (re-running prints ALREADY
APPLIED). Neither patch touches the statistic, the gating rule, or any threshold.

### 4. 📌 The pre-read map called it — and this is the AM-42 exercise done right

S-366 froze the K=8 design map BEFORE any arm was read: **59 of 256 patterns ALWAYS certify, 21
SOMETIMES, 176 NEVER.** The observed pattern `{4,6,11,13,18,21}` is in the **ALWAYS** class —
re-derived after the read, it certifies under **all 64** landings of its two misses, and the
observed landing (10→L7, 27→L9) is one of them. **The verdict never depended on where the misses
fell**, so no post-hoc argument about head 10 or 27 is available to either side.

The frozen necessary conditions are both met: **M ≥ 3** (M=6) and **M_unique ≥ 3 of {10,11,18,21}**
(M_unique=3). ⚠ **M_unique is EXACTLY at its minimum.** Had head 11, 18 or 21 missed instead of
10, M_unique would be 2, the conditional would be `0.063557 > alpha`, and **no outcome could have
certified whatever the other four heads did**. The margin is one head.

Contrast AM-42, which S-352 had to withdraw and S-365 had to correct because it was computed under
the freeze script's statistic rather than the reader's. This time the map was computed from the
reader, frozen before the read, and compared afterwards.

## S-374 — 📌 **THE "MORE HEADS" DIRECTION IS CLOSED ON BOTH CODEWORDS, and the arithmetic says so exactly.** Every basket head that clears the preregistered admission gate has already been cell-mapped; on button, PR-CSI-020's heads are mapped, below the gate, DEAD, or never measured. The next family must be a different KIND of experiment (2026-09-24)

### 1. Why this was the tick

The queue is empty and idle GPU is the binding cost, so the tick is to choose the next family.
Per S-367's rule I read the record first, and the record already settles one candidate: the
**arbitrary-cell control family** that would lift *"cell (L,h) is the writer"* was analysed in S-279
and found **unpreregisterable** — head identity comes from a TRAIN selection (`HD_TOPK`), so judging
a candidate cell against arbitrary cells on train reuses that selection, and restricting controls to
one head's own nine cells hits the 1/9 = 0.111 floor that cannot certify at α = 0.05. *"Held out on
one coordinate and contaminated on the other is not held out."* **I am not re-litigating that
without new information.** So the live question was the obvious extension: more heads.

### 2. ⛔ BUTTON is closed for PR-CSI-020's head set

PR-CSI-018's own frozen `CANDIDATE_PROVENANCE` records the gate and the exclusions. Cross-referenced
against PR-020's eight heads, using **PR-CSI-013's published button whole-head arms** (already read,
so no contamination):

```
head  6, 11, 27   ALREADY CELL-MAPPED ON BUTTON by PR-CSI-018. Re-running counts a known
                  outcome as a fresh draw -- selection on data already read (S-320).
head 10           MEASURED, ci95 excludes 0, but |E|/bar = 1.45 -- BELOW the 1.5 gate
                  (PR-018 recorded this exclusion by name).
head 21           E = +0.00056624, ci95 [-0.00131620, +0.00255249] -- CROSSES ZERO.
                  NOT LIVE on button. Fails the ci95 leg of admission outright.
head  4, 13, 18   NO BUTTON WHOLE-HEAD MEASUREMENT EXISTS. PR-013 measured 21 heads and
                  none of these three is among them.
```

Head 18 additionally predicts **L14**, the band-edge layer PR-CSI-018 deliberately excluded as
*"the adversary's layer"*. So the best conceivable button extension is heads **4 and 13** — and each
would first need its own button `HD_` arm run, with admission unknown until it lands.

**That ceiling is K = 2. My own pre-read floor table (S-366) says 0 of 28 admitted sets at K = 2 can
certify at ANY data** (floor 0.5), and 0 of 56 at K = 3. A button extension could not produce a
verdict whatever the model did.

### 3. ⛔ BASKET is closed too — and this one is exact, not estimated

Of 32 heads, **19 have a ci95 excluding 0** on basket validation. Twelve of those are already
cell-mapped: head 2 (PR-CSI-014), heads 17/19/23 (PR-CSI-015), and PR-020's eight. That leaves
**seven fresh candidates: 3, 7, 14, 15, 20, 24, 31.**

I first estimated their `|E|/bar` from the published ci95 half-width, then **calibrated the proxy
against the eight heads where both the true S-311 bar and the ci95 are known** (bar/hw ∈ [1.0102,
1.0297], mean 1.0213 — the proxy understates the bar by ~2%). Because the answer now steers the
sprint, I then computed the bars **exactly** from PR-012's raw arms with the S-311 formula, against
a control:

```

   head 13   mine 0.00450819   census 0.004508   |diff| 1.93e-07
   head 27   mine 0.00228707   census 0.002287   |diff| 6.65e-08
   (the census rounds to 6 dp, so these agree exactly)

EXACT |E|/bar, the seven FRESH basket heads, n = 23 domains:
   head  3   E=-0.00873165  bar=0.00623705   1.400   BELOW 1.5
   head 20   E=-0.00414804  bar=0.00312729   1.326   BELOW 1.5
   head 24   E=-0.00275031  bar=0.00220626   1.247   BELOW 1.5
   head  7   E=+0.00373227  bar=0.00314403   1.187   BELOW 1.5
   head 14   E=+0.00407016  bar=0.00361040   1.127   BELOW 1.5
   head 31   E=+0.00493364  bar=0.00435936   1.132   BELOW 1.5
   head 15   E=-0.00134051  bar=0.00136492   0.982   BELOW 1.5
```

### 4. ⛔ The near-misses are a trap, and naming it is the point

Head 3 sits at **1.400** and button's head 10 at **1.45**, against a gate of **1.5**. Lowering the
ratio — or "just including head 3, it is basically there" — would admit heads chosen **after** their
distance from the gate was known. That is the post-hoc selection this sprint exists to forbid, and
it would be worse here than usual: `ratio` is frozen in every prereg this family line has used
(`ADMISSION.ratio = 1.5`), so changing it retroactively reinterprets **PR-CSI-016, 018 and 020** as
well. **The gate stays. The heads below it stay out.**

### 5. 📌 What this means for the sprint

```

CLOSED   more heads on BUTTON  -- mapped / below gate / dead / unmeasured, ceiling K=2
```

**The binding constraint has changed.** For twenty ticks idle GPU was the cost; it is now the

## S-375 — the R34 code debt is cleared, with tests that fail without each fix. 🔴 **And one of my four "fixes" was WRONG and had to be REVERTED: pinning the reference `ci95` at `void_tolerance` REFUSED ALL EIGHT HEADS of the PUBLISHED PR-CSI-020 read.** A determinism tolerance applied to a bootstrap quantity (2026-09-24)

### 1. Why this tick

The queue is empty and S-374 established there is no admissible cell-census question left on
either codeword, so GPU idleness is no longer the binding cost. The four R34 concerns that S-369
and S-370 recorded and deferred need no GPU, and VOID 11 has lifted. They are cleared here.

### 2. 🔴 THE ONE THAT WAS WRONG, and how it was caught

R34-B's finding was real: **VOID CONDITION 8 pinned the MEAN and nothing else**, while ADMISSION is
a conjunction over `E`, `bar(h)` and `ci95`. Every reference block already carried a frozen `ci95`
that no reader opened. So I wrote the obvious fix — compare the reference `ci95` endpoints at the
same `void_tolerance` — and then ran it against the **already-published, already-PASSED** PR-CSI-020
read before committing:

```
head   |E diff|      |ci95 worst-endpoint diff|    tol 1e-6     verdict under my "fix"
 4     0.00e+00      5.151e-05                                  *** WOULD REFUSE ***
 6     0.00e+00      9.251e-05                                  *** WOULD REFUSE ***
10     0.00e+00      5.339e-05                                  *** WOULD REFUSE ***
11     0.00e+00      2.056e-05                                  *** WOULD REFUSE ***
13     0.00e+00      1.603e-04                                  *** WOULD REFUSE ***
18     0.00e+00      1.474e-04                                  *** WOULD REFUSE ***
21     0.00e+00      1.997e-05                                  *** WOULD REFUSE ***
27     0.00e+00      2.032e-05                                  *** WOULD REFUSE ***
                                                   8 of 8 REFUSED
```

**The mean reproduces BIT-IDENTICALLY — `|diff| = 0.00e+00` on all eight — because `E` is
DETERMINISTIC given the arms. The `ci95` differs by 2.06e-05 to 1.60e-04 because it is a BOOTSTRAP
quantity and the two families resampled with different seeds.** `void_tolerance` is 1e-6,
calibrated by S-318 on bit-identical reproduction of a deterministic value. **Applying a determinism
tolerance to a resampled statistic is a category error**, and shipping it would have made every
published family in this sprint unreadable — in the name of tightening a check.

REVERTED. The `ci95` diff is now RECORDED in the provenance record (`ci95_abs_diff`,
`ci95_checked`) because the disclosure is useful, and **it gates nothing**. A test locks the
decision in so it cannot be re-added by someone reading R34-B and not this entry.

⚠ **The real SD channel is still open, and the correct close is NOT this.** It is to freeze a
DETERMINISTIC reference — the per-domain SD, or the bar itself, both computed by formula rather than
by resampling. **No prereg declares one today**, so S-167c forbids enforcing it now. That is future
prereg work, not a patch, and it is recorded as such rather than half-done.

### 3. The three that were right

```
(b) THE PREREGISTERED RESAMPLER IS NOW ENFORCED.  Found INDEPENDENTLY by R34-B and R34-C.
    ESTIMATOR_AND_RESAMPLER was WRITTEN by the freeze script and READ BY NOTHING. The frozen read
    presents B/seed/ci as "preregistered instead of inherited", but the census's argparse defaults
    already equalled them, so the CLI changed nothing that runs and the freeze was real only in the
    prereg. `ci` feeds ci95_excludes_0, hence ADMISSION, hence K. The near-miss is one keystroke:
    the sibling reader dcs_csi_head_analyze.py defaults to seed 20260921.
    Gated on the field's PRESENCE, so a prereg without it reads exactly as before.

(d) THE ONE UNGUARDED ALIAS IN THE READ PATH IS GUARDED.  R34-D. pr016 subscripted `per_head[h]`
    bare while the identical guard sat four lines below (`if h not in bars`). A head named in
    `heads` but absent from `per_head` was a KeyError in STEP 2 -- AFTER the GPU -- instead of a
    named refusal. R33 used exactly this mutation, and the prereg self-test STILL cannot see it,
    because `per_head` is a LOCAL ALIAS and the static scan only follows `pr[...]` chains.

(c) THE VACUOUS TEST-LEAK CHECK IS DISCLOSED.  R34-B. It reads
    population["test_domain_ids"], which NO prereg this sprint has frozen declares, so `leaked`
    could never be non-empty -- the file's own R20-6 rule violated at a site it never revisited.
    NOT promoted to a refusal: that would make every published family unreadable. The NON-CHECK
    is printed instead, and the message's wrong "VOID 5" citation (the SCREEN md5) is corrected.
    ⛔ TEST was never at risk from this: the split guard is what keeps the read off TEST.
```

And `pytest tests/` has **8 failures the hook cannot see** (2026-09-24)

### 1. What I found, and why I was looking

S-375's commit hook reported **346 passed** — the same number I have quoted after every commit
this session. But I had just added a 7-test file, so the total should have moved. It did not. The

**Throughout this session I reported "346 guard tests pass" at each commit in a way that implied the

CSI tests did pass — I ran them explicitly at the ticks where I changed reader code — but the number
I kept quoting was not evidence of that, and pairing it with a CSI change was misleading in exactly
the way this sprint keeps finding elsewhere: **a check reported in the voice of a check that covers
the thing at hand.**

### 3. The 8 full-suite failures are PRE-EXISTING, verified rather than assumed

None of the failing files references `dcs_csi_head_census.py` or `dcs_csi_pr016_argmax_test.py`

The hook's own header already records this failure mode, from a previous session:

> passed."*

The response then was to sort the list, not to widen it. So the project has known since August that
its commit gate covers a curated subset, and the subset has not grown as the CSI line added five
test files and ~119 tests. **The sprint's most-changed code is its least-gated.**

## S-377 — the CSI readers are under the commit gate at last, installer and hook together. 📌 **And the agreement was only ever enforced in ONE direction — the one that did NOT bite.** The August failure, a guard living in the deployed hook and not the installer, had no test (2026-09-24)

### 1. What S-376 left, and what it turned out to hide

S-376 found the commit gate had never contained a single CSI test and deliberately did not rush the
fix, because the installer and the deployed hook have silently diverged before. Doing it properly
first meant checking the current state:

```
scripts/install_commit_guard.sh   17 files
.git/hooks/pre-commit             17 files      AGREE: True
```

They agree today — the August divergence was repaired. But `tests/test_commit_guard.py` guards that
agreement in **one direction only**:

```
test_the_DEPLOYED_hook_carries_every_file_the_installer_lists   installer ⊆ hook   TESTED
                        (the reverse)                            hook ⊆ installer   NOT TESTED
```

📌 **The untested direction is the one that actually happened.** The installer's own note records
it: three guards were added to the DEPLOYED hook directly by another session while the installer
carried only eight, so *"re-running it would have silently dropped them and restored the state in
which that session's deliverables were unguarded at commit time."* The note then states the rule —
*"the installer is the source of truth and must therefore carry every guard the hook runs"* — **and
nothing enforced it.** A hook-only guard is invisible twice: it does not survive a re-install, and
its loss is silent, because pytest still exits 0 on the files that remain.

## S-378 — RUNG 2 design pass, part 1: 📌 **the sprint ALREADY has a published probe result, and AM-34's "nothing has ever reached RUNG 2" survives — on four grounds, the sharpest being that the probe's layer grid and the causal band are FULLY DISJOINT.** Design only; nothing frozen (2026-09-24)

### 1. The question this tick had to settle first

S-374 left RUNG 2 as the only unexhausted direction. Before designing one I applied S-367's rule and
looked for what already exists — and found that the sprint has **both** probe machinery and a
**published probe result**:

```
src/boombness/probes.py        963 lines. A trained linear probe with FOUR train/test regimes,
                               including d3_hard_negative (train on the easy diagonal, test on the
                               OFF-DIAGONAL cells) and d4_heldout_ds (train with cell C REMOVED,
                               then score C). It documents the "stupid-probe problem" in terms.
src/boombness/dominance.py     per-CELL contributions Y[l,h,dst,src,:] = A[l,h,dst,src] *
                               (W_O[l,h] @ v[l,h,src]) -- head output at (layer, head, source).
D2 / D3 (claim table)          the QPROBE: a query-side state PREDICTS INSTALLATION.
                               TRAIN LOO rho = 0.5935, VALIDATION transfer +0.645 button /
                               +0.653 basket, perm p = 0.004975.
```

AM-34 states flatly: **"NOTHING IN THIS SPRINT HAS EVER REACHED RUNG 2, 3 OR 4."** D2 is a decoding
result with a held-out transfer and a permutation p. **If AM-34 is wrong, the ladder tag on every
claim in the paper is wrong.** So this had to be checked, not assumed.

### 2. ✅ AM-34 SURVIVES. Four independent grounds, one of them exact

```
(1) LAYERS ARE FULLY DISJOINT -- the decisive one, and it is arithmetic, not judgement:
      QPROBE layer grid   [16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 28, 30, 31]
      CSI causal band     [6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14]
      INTERSECTION        EMPTY
    The probe has never been evaluated at a single layer this sprint's causal claims are about.

(2) POSITION. QPROBE reads a QUERY-SIDE state (winner rel-6). The intervention is
    `demo_all:attn_knockout:6-14:1.0` with scope `target_surface_row_only` -- the DEMONSTRATION
    block and the target surface row. Different positions in the prompt.

(3) TARGET. QPROBE decodes the INSTALLATION OUTCOME (continuous, Spearman rho). RUNG 2 asks
    whether the CONCEPT is readable at the site claimed to carry it. Decoding the outcome from
    an upstream state is a different claim from decoding the concept at the causal site.

(4) GRANULARITY. QPROBE reads a (position, LAYER) residual state with NO head resolution. Every
    causal claim from D34 onward is at (layer, HEAD) CELL granularity -- 8 heads in PR-CSI-020.
```

📌 **So D2 is decodability of an OUTCOME, at a query-side position, in layers the causal band never
touches, without head resolution.** It is a real result and it is not rung 2 for this sprint's
claims. **This is worth writing down precisely because "we have a probe, therefore decodability" is
exactly the inflation AM-34 exists to prevent**, and the next reader of the claim table will see D2's
ρ and AM-34's "nothing has reached rung 2" on the same page.

### 3. What a real RUNG 2 family would have to be

```
DECODE      the CONCEPT (bomb-ness), not y_install
FROM        the cell contribution Y[L, h, dst, src] that dominance.py already computes
AT          (L, h) in the band L6..L14 -- the cells PR-CSI-020's screen names
OVER        the demonstration-block source positions the knockout actually removes
WITH        probes.py's d3_hard_negative and d4_heldout_ds regimes, because a probe that
            separates `bomb` from `carrot` hits ~100% at layer 0 off lexical identity and that
            number says only that the tokenizer works -- probes.py documents this as the
            "stupid-probe problem" and the sprint must not rediscover it
```

⚠ **And it would NOT strengthen D40.** The ladder's own claim is that the rungs are SEPARABLE:
*"Information may be readable at a site without being used there"*, and *"passing 1-3 does not imply
passing 4."* A rung-2 result is a **different** claim standing beside the necessity results, never a
stronger version of them. Any write-up that lets decodability reinforce a necessity headline has
made R19's error — form matched, operation not.

### 4. ⛔ The two-coordinate bind RECURS, and it constrains the design

S-279 blocked the arbitrary-cell rank test because *"held out on one coordinate and contaminated on
the other is not held out."* The same bind applies here, and it must be faced before anything is
frozen:

```
the LAYER predictions come from the basket TRAIN screen   -> validation is held out for LAYER
the HEAD SET was chosen by basket liveness measured on PR-CSI-012 VALIDATION
                                                          -> train is held out for HEAD IDENTITY
=> NEITHER split is clean on BOTH coordinates, exactly as in S-279.
```

📌 **But there is a way through that PR-CSI-020 already demonstrated**, and it is why this direction
is not simply blocked like the arbitrary-cell test: the comparison can be made **WITHIN a head,
across its nine band layers** — the same shape as PR-020's argmax test, with the same 1/9 floor.
Every cell in that comparison is measured on one split with one head set, so the head-identity
selection is **constant across the comparison and cannot create the contrast**. What it buys is
narrower than a cross-cell claim, and that narrowness is the price of admissibility.

### 5. What was NOT established, and what is NOT frozen

```
- NOTHING IS FROZEN. No prereg, no read, no tag prefix. S-167c forbids a prereg naming something
  that does not exist, and the instrument in section 3 does not exist yet: dominance.py computes
  the cell contribution along a CHOSEN DIRECTION u, not the full vector a trained probe needs.
  Whether to project onto a concept direction (cheap, no training, no generalisation test) or to
  capture vectors and train (expensive, and re-opens the stupid-probe problem) is UNDECIDED.
- NOT established: that the concept IS decodable at those cells. Nothing was measured this tick.
  This entry surveys and rules out; it reports no new number about the model.
- NOT established: that a rung-2 result is reachable at all on an admissible axis. Section 4
  names a candidate shape; it has not been powered, and the 1/9 floor that shaped PR-CSI-014's
  design applies here too.
- NOT retracted: D2 and D3 stand exactly as written. This entry does not touch their numbers or
  their status -- it settles only that they are not rung 2 FOR THIS SPRINT'S CAUSAL CLAIMS.
- NOT checked: whether probes.py still runs. It reads a cache (`cache/final_occurrence_reps.pt`)
  whose existence I did not verify, and it is per-LAYER, so it would need cell-resolved input
  either way.
```
